title: Numbers 3:37 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠עַמֻּדֵ֧י הֶ⁠חָצֵ֛ר סָבִ֖יב

"and the pillars of the courtyard all around"

The implication is that these pillars formed a fence that marked off the boundary of the courtyard around the sacred tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the posts that mark off the courtyard]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:37 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אַדְנֵי⁠הֶ֑ם וִ⁠יתֵדֹתָ֖⁠ם וּ⁠מֵֽיתְרֵי⁠הֶֽם

"and their bases and their pegs and their ropes"

Here, bases, pegs, and ropes refer to the items used to secure the pillars and curtains of the courtyard fence into place. The pillars were placed on the bases, ropes were fastened to them, and the other ends of the ropes were fastened down with the pegs, which were driven into the ground. Alternate translation: [and their metal foundations and their spikes and their cords]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 3:38 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּ֡ן קֵ֣דְמָ⁠ה לִ⁠פְנֵי֩ אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֨ד ׀ מִזְרָ֜חָ⁠ה

"to the face of the Dwelling to the east, to the face of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise"

These two phrases to the face of the Dwelling to the east and to the face of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [to the face of the tent of meeting to the east]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 3:38 (#2)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּ֡ן & לִ⁠פְנֵי֩ אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֨ד

Here, to the face of represents being in front of the Dwelling and the tent of meeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before the Dwelling … before the tent of meeting]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 3:38 (#3)
content:

"All the counted ones of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted"

It might seem that the expression All the counted ones of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

פְּקוּדֵ֨י

"the counted ones"

"upon the mouth of Yahweh"

title: Numbers 3:39 (#4)
content:
שְׁנַ֥יִם וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָֽלֶף

"were} 22,000"

If your language has a different way of expressing the number 22,000, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [were twenty-two thousand]

title: Numbers 3:40 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠שָׂ֕א אֵ֖ת מִסְפַּ֥ר שְׁמֹתָֽ⁠ם

"And lift up the number of their names"

This sentence could refer to: (1) calculating the total number of names. Alternate translation: [And calculate the number of their names]; or (2) writing down a list of names. Alternate translation: [And list their names]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 3:40 (#2)
content:
שְׁמֹתָֽ⁠ם

"of their names"

The pronoun their refers to the firstborn males of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the names of those counted]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 3:41 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠לָקַחְתָּ֨ אֶת־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֥ם לִ⁠י֙ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת

"And you shall take the Levites for me—I {am} Yahweh—instead of"

Yahweh interrupts the sentence with the statement I am Yahweh in order to remind Moses of who he is. If it would be more natural in your language, you could change the order of these clauses. Alternate translation: [Remember that I am Yahweh. You shall take the Levites for me instead of]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 3:41 (#2)
content:
בֶּהֱמַ֣ת הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם & בְּ⁠בֶהֱמַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

"the animal of the Levites & among the animal of the sons of Israel"

In this verse, the word animal is singular in form, but it refers to all livestock as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “animal.” Alternate translation: [the animals of the Levites … among the animals of the sons of Israel]

See: Collective Nouns

title: Numbers 3:42 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יִּפְקֹ֣ד מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑⁠וֹ אֶֽת־כָּל־בְּכֹ֖ר בִּ⁠בְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

"And Moses counted, just as Yahweh had commanded him, all the firstborn among the sons of Israel"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about Yahweh commanding Moses before the information about Moses counting the people. Alternate translation: [And just as Yahweh had commanded him, Moses counted all the firstborn among the sons of Israel]

See: Information Structure

וַ⁠יִּפְקֹ֣ד מֹשֶׁ֔ה

"And Moses counted"

content:
בְּ⁠מִסְפַּ֥ר שֵׁמ֛וֹת

"by the number of the names"

content:
שְׁנַ֤יִם וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה וְ⁠שִׁבְעִ֖ים וּ⁠מָאתָֽיִם

"was} 22,273"

If your language has a different way of expressing the number 22,273, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [was twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three men]

title: Numbers 3:45 (#1)
content:
בֶּהֱמַ֥ת הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֖ם תַּ֣חַת בְּהֶמְתָּ֑⁠ם

"the animal of the Levites instead of their animal"

See how you translated animal in 3:41.

title: Numbers 3:45 (#2)
content:
בְּהֶמְתָּ֑⁠ם

"their animal"

The implication is that this refers to firstborn male animals, as stated in 3:41. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [their firstborn male animal]

title: Numbers 3:46 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אֵת֙ פְּדוּיֵ֣י

"And the ransoms of"

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And you shall take the ransoms of]

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 3:46 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אֵת֙ פְּדוּיֵ֣י הַ⁠שְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שִּׁבְעִ֖ים וְ⁠הַ⁠מָּאתָ֑יִם

"And the ransoms of the 273"

Here, ransoms refers to money that must be paid for the additional 273 firstborn mentioned in this verse. Since there were not enough Levites to be in place of these 273 firstborn, God required money in their place. See the discussion of this in the Introduction for this chapter. Alternate translation: [And the payment for the 273]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:46 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠אֵת֙ פְּדוּיֵ֣י הַ⁠שְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שִּׁבְעִ֖ים וְ⁠הַ⁠מָּאתָ֑יִם

"And the ransoms of the 273"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of ransoms, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And you shall ransom the 273]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 3:46 (#4)
content:
הַ⁠שְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שִּׁבְעִ֖ים וְ⁠הַ⁠מָּאתָ֑יִם

"the 273"

If your language has a different way of expressing the number 273, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [the two hundred seventy-three]

See: Numbers

title: Numbers 3:46 (#5)
content:
הַ⁠שְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שִּׁבְעִ֖ים וְ⁠הַ⁠מָּאתָ֑יִם הָ⁠עֹֽדְפִים֙ עַל־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם מִ⁠בְּכ֖וֹר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

"the 273, the ones being in excess over the Levites from the firstborn of the sons of Israel"

The implication is that these were 273 firstborn Israelite males who did not have a corresponding Levite male to take their place. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the 273 firstborn males who did not have a Levite in their place]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:46 (#6)
content:
הָ⁠עֹֽדְפִים֙ עַל־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם מִ⁠בְּכ֖וֹר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

"the ones being in excess over the Levites from the firstborn of the sons of Israel"

This clause gives further information about the 273. It is not making a distinction between the 273 and the ones being in excess. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make the relationship between these phrases clearer. Alternate translation: [that is, the ones being in excess over the Levites from the firstborn of the sons of Israel]

See: Distinguishing Versus Informing or Reminding

title: Numbers 3:47 (#1)
content:
חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת שְׁקָלִ֖ים & בְּ⁠שֶׁ֤קֶל & הַ⁠שָּֽׁקֶל

"five shekels & by the shekel & is} the shekel"

In ancient times, a shekel was a measure of weight for silver that equaled about 11 grams. You could try to express this in terms of modern money values, but if you did, that could cause your Bible translation to become outdated and inaccurate, since those values can change over time. Instead, you might say something general like “pieces of silver,” or use the biblical term in the text and explain the value in a note.

See: Biblical Money

title: Numbers 3:47 (#2)
content:
חֲמֵ֧שֶׁת חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת

"five, five"

Yahweh repeats the same word five in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [precisely five]

See: Reduplication

title: Numbers 3:47 (#3)
content:
לַ⁠גֻּלְגֹּ֑לֶת

"for the skull"

Yahweh is using skull to represent a whole person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for each person]

See: Synecdoche

title: Numbers 3:47 (#4)
content:
הַ⁠קֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙

"of the holy place"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a shekel that was used in the holy place. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that is used in the holy place]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 3:47 (#5)
content:
עֶשְׂרִ֥ים גֵּרָ֖ה

"20 gerahs"

A gerah was a unit of weight equal to about 0.6 grams. Twenty gerahs equaled one shekel, or about 11 grams. In your translation, you could use the ancient measurement and spell the word “gerah” the way it sounds in your language. You could also use modern measurements, or you could use the ancient measurement and put a modern measurement in parentheses in the text or in a footnote.

See: Biblical Weight

title: Numbers 3:48 (#1)
content:
הַ⁠כֶּ֔סֶף

"the silver"

The implication is that this is the silver that Moses would collect as ransom money for the 273 firstborn males. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the silver that you collected in shekels]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:48 (#2)
content:
פְּדוּיֵ֕י הָ⁠עֹדְפִ֖ים

"the ransoms of the ones being in excess"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of ransoms, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to ransom the ones being in excess]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 3:48 (#3)
content:
הָ⁠עֹדְפִ֖ים בָּ⁠הֶֽם

"the ones being in excess among them"

The implication is that these were the 273 firstborn Israelite males for whom there were no corresponding Levites to take their place. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the firstborn Israelite males who did not have a Levite in their place]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:49 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יִּקַּ֣ח מֹשֶׁ֔ה

"And Moses took"

The words translated as And indicate that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, Moses took]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 3:49 (#2)
content:
אֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף הַ⁠פִּדְי֑וֹם

"the silver of the ransom"

The implication is that this was the ransom money that Moses collected in shekels to pay for the firstborn Israelite males. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the silver of the ransom that he collected in shekels]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:49 (#3)
content:
אֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף הַ⁠פִּדְי֑וֹם

"the silver of the ransom"

The author is using the possessive form to describe the silver that was paid as a ransom. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the silver for the ransom]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 3:49 (#4)
content:
אֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף הַ⁠פִּדְי֑וֹם

"the silver of the ransom"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of ransom, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the silver, by which they were ransomed,]

title: Numbers 3:49 (#5)
content:
הָ⁠עֹ֣דְפִ֔ים עַ֖ל

"the ones being in excess over"

title: Numbers 3:49 (#6)
content:
פְּדוּיֵ֥י הַ⁠לְוִיִּֽם

"the ransoms of the Levites"

Here, ransoms of the Levites represents “the ones ransomed by the Levites.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the ones ransomed by the Levites]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 3:49 (#7)
content:
פְּדוּיֵ֥י הַ⁠לְוִיִּֽם

"the ransoms of the Levites"

The author is using this possessive form to mean the ransoming that was accomplished when the Levites were given to God. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the ransoms accomplished when the Levites were given to God]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 3:50 (#1)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠כָּ֑סֶף

"the silver"

The implication is that this was the silver that Moses collected in shekels from the firstborn Israelites. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the silver that he collected in shekels]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 3:50 (#2)
content:
חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְ⁠שִׁשִּׁ֜ים וּ⁠שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת וָ⁠אֶ֖לֶף

"1,365"

If your language has a different way of expressing the number 1,365, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [one thousand three hundred and sixty-five]

content:
בְּ⁠שֶׁ֥קֶל הַ⁠קֹּֽדֶשׁ

"by the shekel of the holy place"

content:
אֶת־כֶּ֧סֶף הַ⁠פְּדֻיִ֛ם

"the silver of the ransoms"

title: Numbers 3:51 (#2)
content:
עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה

"upon the mouth of Yahweh, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses"

It might seem that the expression upon the mouth of Yahweh, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. See how you translated the similar clauses in 3:16. Alternate translation: [exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 3:51 (#3)
content:
עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה

"upon the mouth of Yahweh"

The author is using upon the mouth of Yahweh as a common expression of his culture to mean “as Yahweh had said.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 3:16. Alternate translation: [as Yahweh had said]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers - Chapter 4 Introduction
content:
Numbers 4 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter describes the assignments Yahweh gave to each of the families who descended from Levi with regard to taking care of and transporting the sacred tent.

  1. Yahweh assigns the Kohathites to carry the most holy things (1–20)
  2. Yahweh assigns the Gershonites to carry the tabernacle’s curtains and coverings (21–28)
  3. Yahweh assigns the Merarites to carry the tabernacle’s frames, posts, and bases (29–33)
  4. Moses, Aaron, and Israel’s leaders count the Levites eligible for service (34–49)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

“Keeping,” “service,” and “burden”

As in the previous chapter, the word “keeping” refers to keeping watch or guarding. No one else was supposed to approach the sacred items, so the Levites were required to guard these items, especially when they were transporting them. The word “service” refers to physical labor, particularly taking down and setting up the sacred tent and the items that were in it. The Levites were also responsible for these tasks. Finally, the word “burden” refers to the specific task of carrying the pieces of the sacred tent and the items in it when the Israelites moved from one campsite to another. See how you translated “keeping” and “service” in chapter 3.

“Clan” and “house of their fathers”

As in chapter 3, the phrase “house of the father” and the word “clan” refer to divisions of an Israelite tribe. The “house of the father” was the larger division, and each “house of the father” contained several “clans.” For example, one “house of the father” within the tribe of Levi was named after Levi’s son, Gershon. Within the “house of the father” of the Gershonites were two clans named after Gershon’s sons (Levi’s grandsons): Libni and Shimei. Translate “house of the father” and “clan” as you did in chapter 3.

“Skin of a porpoise”

This phrase refers to leather made from the skin of a specific animal. Scholars debate exactly what animal the word refers to. Some argue that it is a land animal like a goat. Others argue that it is a sea animal like a dolphin or porpoise. The ULT identifies the animal as a porpoise, and the UST models how to refer to leather without identifying the animal. Consider how the word is translated in any translations your readers might know. If you do identify a specific animal, you could include a footnote indicating that this identification is uncertain.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

“Sons of”

Throughout this chapter, the phrase “sons of” refers to the men who were part of the tribal group named after the word “of.” So, the phrase “the sons of Merari” refers to the men who were part of the Merari tribal group. Consider how you translated this phrase in chapter 3.

The “army”

In this chapter, serving at the sacred tent is sometimes described as if it were being part of an army and fighting. The rest of the Israelite men had to serve in the army when necessary, but the Levites were exempt from serving in the army. Instead, they served at the tent of meeting. Because of this, their duties as Levites can be described as if they were service in the army. The ULT preserves the army metaphor, and the UST models how to express the idea without this metaphor.

“A son of 30 years and upward and up to a son of 50 years”

The phrase “a son of … years” is an idiom that refers to the age of a man. The longer phrase here refers to a man who is at least 30 years old and at most 50 years old. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly.

Repetition in 4:34–48

In 4:34–48, the author records the number of men who were 30–50 years old in each of the three ancestral families of the Levites. The same phrases and structures are often repeated for each of the ancestral families. Once you translate the first section, in most cases you should use the same forms and phrases with the other two sections. The notes on these verses will indicate when a phrase or whole verse is identical to a previous phrase or whole verse.

title: Numbers 4:1 (#1)
content:
לֵ⁠אמֹֽר

"saying"

Here and throughout the chapter, the word saying introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated saying in 1:1.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 4:2 (#1)
content:
נָשֹׂ֗א אֶת־רֹאשׁ֙ בְּנֵ֣י

"Lift up the head of the sons of"

See how you translated the nearly identical idiom in 1:2.

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:2 (#2)
content:
נָשֹׂ֗א

"Lift up"

The word Lift up is singular here because God is speaking to Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 4:2 (#3)
content:
בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֔ת מִ⁠תּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י לֵוִ֑י

"the sons of Kohath from the midst of the sons of Levi"

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase sons of refers to male descendants. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [male descendants of Kohath from the midst of the male descendants of Levi]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 4:2 (#4)
content:
מִ⁠תּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י לֵוִ֑י

"from the midst of the sons of Levi"

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Kohath’s descendants were physically located from the midst of the other Levites. He means that they should be counted from among all the Levites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly.

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 4:2 (#5)
content:
לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖⁠ם לְ⁠בֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָֽ⁠ם

"according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers"

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase house of their fathers refers to largest divisions within a single tribe. The word clans refers to the largest divisions of each house of their fathers. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers made up of those clans]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:2 (#6)
content:
לְ⁠בֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָֽ⁠ם

"according to the house of their fathers"

See how you translated this phrase in 1:2.

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 4:3 (#1)
content:
מִ⁠בֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה וְ⁠עַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה

"from a son of 30 years and upward and up to a son of 50 years"

Here and throughout this chapter, this phrase identifies men who are at least 30 years old and no older than 50 years old. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [men who are 30–50 years old]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:3 (#2)
content:
בָּא֙ לַ⁠צָּבָ֔א

"one who comes to the army"

The expression who comes to is a common expression of his culture to mean “who is able to be part of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [one who is able to be part of the army]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:3 (#3)
content:
לַ⁠צָּבָ֔א

"to the army"

Here, Moses is speaking of the group who works in the tent of meeting as if it were an army. See the chapter introduction for more information. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the group of workers]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 4:4 (#1)
content:
זֹ֛את עֲבֹדַ֥ת בְּנֵי־קְהָ֖ת

"This {is} the service of the sons of Kohath"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This is how the sons of Kohath serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:4 (#2)
content:
קֹ֖דֶשׁ הַ⁠קֳּדָשִֽׁים

"the holy of the holies"

The expression the holy of the holies is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language.

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 4:4 (#3)
content:
קֹ֖דֶשׁ הַ⁠קֳּדָשִֽׁים

"the holy of the holies"

Here, the holy of the holies represents the most holy things or objects. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the things that are most holy]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:5 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בָ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּ⁠בָנָי⁠ו֙

"And Aaron shall come and his sons"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put Aaron and his sons together at the beginning of the clause, rather than having Aaron first and his sons later. Alternate translation: [And Aaron and his sons shall come]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 4:5 (#2)
content:
הַֽ⁠מַּחֲנֶ֔ה

"the camp"

Here, camp represents the people living in the camp. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people in the camp]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:5 (#3)
content:
אֵ֖ת פָּרֹ֣כֶת הַ⁠מָּסָ֑ךְ

"the veil of the curtain"

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that the veil of the curtain refers to the special curtain that separated the Most Holy Place from the rest of the sacred tent. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the veil of the curtain in front of the Holy of Holies]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:5 (#4)
content:
אֵ֖ת פָּרֹ֣כֶת הַ⁠מָּסָ֑ךְ

"the veil of the curtain"

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a veil that is characterized by being a curtain. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the curtain that is a veil]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:6 (#1)
content:
עָלָ֗י⁠ו

"on it"

The pronoun it refers to the Box of the Testimony. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [on the box and the curtain covering it]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 4:6 (#2)
content:
ע֣וֹר תַּ֔חַשׁ

"skin of a porpoise"

This phrase refers to high-quality leather made from the skin of an animal. The animal may be a porpoise, a type of sea creature with leathery skin. See the chapter introduction for more information. If your readers would not be familiar with this type of sea animal, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [durable animal skin]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:6 (#3)
content:
בֶֽגֶד־כְּלִ֛יל תְּכֵ֖לֶת

"a cloth of completely blue"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a cloth that is characterized by being completely blue. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an entirely blue cloth]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:6 (#4)
content:
מִ⁠לְ⁠מָ֑עְלָ⁠ה

"from above"

The implication is that the blue cloth should be placed over all the other coverings that were put on the Box of the Testimony. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on top of all these things]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:6 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠שָׂמ֖וּ בַּדָּֽי⁠ו

"and they shall set its poles"

The implication is that these poles were inserted into rings on the sides of the ark and used to carry it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the box in order to carry it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:7 (#1)
content:
שֻׁלְחַ֣ן הַ⁠פָּנִ֗ים

"the table of the faces"

The phrase the table of the faces is a common expression of this culture that means “the table that is in Yahweh’s presence.” This table was placed before Yahweh in the tent of meeting, and the Levites were to place special bread on it for Yahweh, as described in Exodus 25:30. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the table in Yahweh’s presence]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:7 (#2)
content:
בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵלֶת֒

"a cloth of blue"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a cloth of blue that is characterized by blue. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a cloth that is blue]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:7 (#3)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠קְּעָרֹ֤ת וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠כַּפֹּת֙ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠מְּנַקִּיֹּ֔ת וְ⁠אֵ֖ת קְשׂ֣וֹת הַ⁠נָּ֑סֶךְ

"the dishes and the palm-sized bowls and the bowls and the pitchers of the drink offering"

The dishes, palm-sized bowls, bowls, and pitchers are different kinds of vessels used in the tabernacle service. If your readers would not be familiar with what these vessels are, you could use the names of similar containers that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [the plates and the large spoons and the containers and the jars of the drink offering]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:7 (#4)
content:
קְשׂ֣וֹת הַ⁠נָּ֑סֶךְ

"the pitchers of the drink offering"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe pitchers that are used for the drink offering. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the pitchers used with drink offerings]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:7 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠לֶ֥חֶם הַ⁠תָּמִ֖יד

"and the bread of continuity"

The phrase bread of continuity refers to the bread that was regularly offered to God. If your readers would not be familiar with what this bread is, you could use a term that shows it was bread that was always present on the table as an offering to God. Alternate translation: [and the bread of continuity offered to me]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:7 (#6)
content:
וְ⁠לֶ֥חֶם הַ⁠תָּמִ֖יד

"and the bread of continuity"

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the bread that was characterized by being offered regularly (in continuity). If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the bread that is offered continually]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:7 (#7)
content:
וְ⁠לֶ֥חֶם הַ⁠תָּמִ֖יד

"and the bread of continuity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of continuity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the continual bread]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:7 (#8)
content:
עָלָ֥י⁠ו יִהְיֶֽה

"shall be on it"

By shall be on it, Yahweh means that the bread was to remain on the table when the priests covered it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [shall stay on it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:8 (#1)
content:
בֶּ֚גֶד תּוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י

"a cloth of worm of scarlet"

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a cloth that was dyed by a worm of scarlet. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a cloth dyed by worm of scarlet]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:8 (#2)
content:
תּוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י

"worm of scarlet"

The expression worm of scarlet is a common expression of this culture that means “red” or “crimson.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [scarlet]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:8 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠מִכְסֵ֖ה ע֣וֹר תָּ֑חַשׁ

"with a covering of skin of a porpoise"

See how you translated the same phrase in 4:6.

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:8 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠שָׂמ֖וּ אֶת־בַּדָּֽי⁠ו

"and they shall set its poles"

The implication is that the poles were placed through the rings attached to the sides of the table so people could use them to carry it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the table in order to carry it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:9 (#1)
content:
בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֗לֶת

"a cloth of blue"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:7.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:9 (#2)
content:
אֶת־מְנֹרַ֤ת הַ⁠מָּאוֹר֙

"the lampstand of the light"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the lampstand that produces light. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the lampstand that produces light]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:9 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠אֶת־נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֶת־מַלְקָחֶ֖י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֶת־מַחְתֹּתֶ֑י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֵת֙ כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י שַׁמְנָ֔⁠הּ

"and its lamps and its tongs and its trays and all the vessels of its oil"

The tongs and trays are tools used to handle hot lamp wicks. The lamps burned olive oil, and the vessels contained that oil. If your readers would not be familiar with these items, you could use the names of similar tools that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [and its oil lamps and its wick tools and its wick plates and all the containers of its oil]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:9 (#4)
content:
כְּלֵ֣י שַׁמְנָ֔⁠הּ

"the vessels of its oil"

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the vessels that contained its oil. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vessels that contained its oil]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:10 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נָתְנ֖וּ עַל־הַ⁠מּֽוֹט

"and they shall put {them} on the carrying pole"

The implication is that the poles were used for carrying the items. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall attach them to a long piece of wood in order to carry them]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:11 (#1)
content:
מִזְבַּ֣ח הַ⁠זָּהָ֗ב

"the altar of gold"

The term altar of gold assumes that readers will know this was the altar used for burning incense. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the incense altar of gold]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:11 (#2)
content:
מִזְבַּ֣ח הַ⁠זָּהָ֗ב

"the altar of gold"

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the altar that is characterized by being overlaid with gold. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the altar overlaid with gold]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:11 (#3)
content:
בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֔לֶת

"a cloth of blue"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:7.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:11 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠שָׂמ֖וּ אֶת־בַּדָּֽי⁠ו

"and they shall set its poles"

By set its poles, Yahweh means they put the poles into the rings that were on the sides of the altar so that they could carry it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar use of this clause in 4:6. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the altar in order to carry it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:12 (#1)
content:
כְּלֵ֨י הַ⁠שָּׁרֵ֜ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְשָֽׁרְתוּ־בָ֣⁠ם

"the vessels of the ministry with which they minister"

It might seem that the expression the vessels of the ministry with which they minister contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [the vessels with which they minister]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 4:12 (#2)
content:
בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֔לֶת

"a cloth of blue"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:7.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:12 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נָתְנ֖וּ עַל־הַ⁠מּֽוֹט

"And they shall put {them} on the carrying pole"

By put them on the carrying pole, Yahweh means they must attach these items to poles that people will use to carry them. See how you translated this clause in 4:10. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall attach them to a long piece of wood in order to carry them]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:13 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠דִשְּׁנ֖וּ אֶת־הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֑חַ

"And they shall remove the ashes from the altar"

By remove the ashes, Yahweh means that the priests were to clean out the fat and ashes that remained after burning the sacrifices on the altar. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And they shall cleanse the altar of fat and ashes]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:13 (#2)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֑חַ

"the altar"

The text the altar refers to the bronze altar used for sacrifices that was placed in front of the tent of meeting. Yahweh assumes that readers will know which altar this is, since there were two altars used in worship. You could say this explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the sacrificial altar]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:13 (#3)
content:
בֶּ֖גֶד אַרְגָּמָֽן

"a cloth of purple"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a cloth that is characterized by purple. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a cloth that is purple]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:14 (#1)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠מַּחְתֹּ֤ת אֶת־הַ⁠מִּזְלָגֹת֙ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠יָּעִ֣ים וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠מִּזְרָקֹ֔ת

"the trays, the meat forks and the shovels and the basins"

The trays were like large, flat plates and were used for holding meat and other things. The meat forks were used to stab and move the meat. The shovels and basins were used for moving and storing ashes, blood, and anything else. If your readers would not be familiar with these tools, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [the platters, the utensils for stabbing meat and the scoops and the containers]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:14 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠מִּזְרָקֹ֔ת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֑חַ

"and the basins—all the vessels of the altar"

It might seem that the expression the basins—all the vessels of the altar contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and the basins]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 4:14 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠שָׂמ֥וּ בַדָּֽי⁠ו

"and they shall set its poles"

The implied meaning is that the poles were put into rings on the sides of the altar so that people could use them to carry it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar use of this clause in 4:6. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the altar in order to carry it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:15 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠כִלָּ֣ה אַֽהֲרֹן־וּ֠⁠בָנָי⁠ו לְ⁠כַסֹּ֨ת

"And Aaron and his sons shall finish to cover"

The phrase shall finish to cover is a common expression of this culture that means “shall finish covering.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Aaron and his sons shall finish covering]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:15 (#2)
content:
בִּ⁠נְסֹ֣עַ הַֽ⁠מַּחֲנֶה֒

"when the camp sets out"

Here, the camp represents the people who are in the camp. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated this clause in 4:5. Alternate translation: [when the people in the camp set out]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:15 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִגְּע֥וּ אֶל־הַ⁠קֹּ֖דֶשׁ

"and they shall not touch the holy place"

Here, the holy place represents the sacred objects that belong in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they shall not touch the things that belong in the holy place]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:15 (#4)
content:
וָ⁠מֵ֑תוּ

"and die"

The words and die express the result of touching the holy place. If it would be more natural in your language, you could make this connection more explicit. Alternate translation: [which would cause them to die]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 4:15 (#5)
content:
אֵ֛לֶּה מַשָּׂ֥א בְנֵֽי־קְהָ֖ת

"These are the burden of the sons of Kohath"

The phrase the burden of refers to the objects that the sons of Kohath were responsible for carrying when the Israelites traveled. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [These are the things that must be carried by the sons of Kohath]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:16 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠פְקֻדַּ֞ת אֶלְעָזָ֣ר & פְּקֻדַּ֗ת כָּל

"And the oversight of Eleazar & the oversight of all"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of oversight, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And what is overseen by Eleazar … and he oversees]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:16 (#2)
content:
שֶׁ֤מֶן הַ⁠מָּאוֹר֙

"is} the oil of the light"

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the oil as oil that produces light. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the oil that is burned to produce light]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:16 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠קְטֹ֣רֶת הַ⁠סַּמִּ֔ים

"and the incense of the spices"

The phrase incense of the spices is using the possessive form to describe incense that is made out of spices. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the incense that is made of spices]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:16 (#4)
content:
וּ⁠מִנְחַ֥ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֖יד

"and the grain offering of continuity"

The phrase the grain offering of continuity refers to a grain offering that is characterized by continuity—it was offered regularly. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated the same use of continuity in 4:7. Alternate translation: [and the grain offering that is offered continually]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:16 (#5)
content:
וּ⁠מִנְחַ֥ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֖יד

"and the grain offering of continuity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of continuity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the continual grain offering]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:16 (#6)
content:
וְ⁠שֶׁ֣מֶן הַ⁠מִּשְׁחָ֑ה

"and the oil of the anointing"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the oil that is used for anointing. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the oil that is used for anointing]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:16 (#7)
content:
פְּקֻדַּ֗ת כָּל־הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּן֙

"the oversight of all the Dwelling"

It might seem that the expression the oversight of all the Dwelling contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and all the Dwelling]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 4:16 (#8)
content:
וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֔⁠וֹ בְּ⁠קֹ֖דֶשׁ וּ⁠בְ⁠כֵלָֽי⁠ו

"and all that {is} in it, in the holy place, and in its vessels"

The implication is that this refers to everything that is contained in the Dwelling, holy place, and vessels. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and everything that is in it, and everything that is in the holy place, and everything that is in its vessels]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:16 (#9)
content:
בְּ⁠קֹ֖דֶשׁ

"in the holy place"

Here, holy place represents the things that belong in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:15. Alternate translation: [in the things that belong in the holy place]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:18 (#1)
content:
אֶת־שֵׁ֖בֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֑י

"the tribe of the clans of the Kohathite"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a tribe that is made up of the clans of the Kohathite. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the tribe that is made up of the clans of]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:18 (#2)
content:
אֶת־שֵׁ֖בֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת

"the tribe of the clans of"

Here, tribe represents the descendants of Kohath who comprise part of the tribe. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the portion of the tribe of]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:18 (#3)
content:
הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֑י

"the Kohathite"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific Kohathite. He means all the members of the Kohathite clan in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Kohathites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 4:18 (#4)
content:
מִ⁠תּ֖וֹךְ הַ⁠לְוִיִּֽם

"from the midst of the Levites"

Here, Moses is speaking as if the Kohathites were objects that could be physically removed from the midst of the Levites. He means that they could be eliminated as a group from among the Levites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [so that they no longer exist among]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 4:19 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠זֹ֣את

"But this"

The pronoun this refers to the instructions that follow about how Aaron and his sons must assign specific tasks to each of the Kohathites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But here is what you must]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 4:19 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠חָיוּ֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יָמֻ֔תוּ

"and they will live and not die"

The phrases live and not die mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and they will certainly live]

See: Doublet

title: Numbers 4:19 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠חָיוּ֙

"and they will live"

Here, and they will live marks this clause as the purpose of Aaron and his sons showing each man what to carry. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that they will live]

See: Connect — Goal (Purpose) Relationship

title: Numbers 4:19 (#4)
content:
אֶת־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַ⁠קֳּדָשִׁ֑ים

"the holy of the holies"

Here, holy of the holies represents the most sacred items. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the things that are most holy]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:19 (#5)
content:
יָבֹ֔אוּ

"shall go"

By shall go, Yahweh means Aaron and his sons will enter the sacred tent to show each Kohathite man what he should carry. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [shall enter the sacred tent]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:19 (#6)
content:
וְ⁠שָׂמ֣וּ אוֹתָ֗⁠ם אִ֥ישׁ אִ֛ישׁ

"and set them man by man"

The phrase set them man by man is a common expression of this culture that means “to assign each person his own task.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and appoint each of them]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:19 (#7)
content:
עֲבֹדָת֖⁠וֹ

"his service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what he does to serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:19 (#8)
content:
מַשָּׂאֽ⁠וֹ

"his burden"

See how you translated the same use of burden in 4:15.

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:20 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠לֹא־יָבֹ֧אוּ

"But they shall not go"

The pronoun they refers to the sons of Kohath. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But the sons of Kohath shall not go]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 4:20 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠לֹא־יָבֹ֧אוּ

"But they shall not go"

The implication is that the Kohathites must not enter the sacred tent while Aaron and his sons are covering the holy items. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [But they shall not enter the sacred tent]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:20 (#3)
content:
כְּ⁠בַלַּ֥ע

"when swallowing"

The expression when swallowing is a common expression of this culture that means “even for a moment.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [even for a moment]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:20 (#4)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠קֹּ֖דֶשׁ

"the holy place"

Here, holy place represents the things that belong in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:15. Alternate translation: [the things that belong in the holy place]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 4:20 (#5)
content:
וָ⁠מֵֽתוּ

"and die"

The words and die express the result of touching the holy place. If it would be more natural in your language, you could make this connection more explicit. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:15. Alternate translation: [which would cause them to die]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 4:22 (#1)
content:
נָשֹׂ֗א אֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ בְּנֵ֥י

"Lift up the head of the sons"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:2.

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:22 (#2)
content:
גַּם־הֵ֑ם

"also them"

By also them, Moses means that he should count the descendants of Gershon in addition to having counted the descendants of Kohath. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in addition to the sons of Kohath]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:22 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠בֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָ֖⁠ם לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽ⁠ם

"according to the house of their fathers, according to their clans"

See how you translated these phrases in 4:2.

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:23 (#1)
content:
מִ⁠בֶּן֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה וָ⁠מַ֗עְלָ⁠ה עַ֛ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה

"From a son of 30 years and upward up to a son of 50 years"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:3. Alternate translation: [From 30–50 years old]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:23 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠בָּא֙ לִ⁠צְבֹ֣א

"who comes to fight"

The phrase who comes to is a common expression of this culture that means “who is able to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who can fight]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:23 (#3)
content:
לִ⁠צְבֹ֣א צָבָ֔א

"to fight in the army"

Here, Yahweh is speaking of serving in the tabernacle as if it were fighting in the army. This emphasizes that the work was strenuous and required careful coordination and attention to detail. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to be part of the group of workers]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 4:23 (#4)
content:
לִ⁠צְבֹ֣א צָבָ֔א

"to fight in the army"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to be in the army]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 4:23 (#5)
content:
לַ⁠עֲבֹ֥ד עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"to serve service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to serve what needs to be served]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:23 (#6)
content:
לַ⁠עֲבֹ֥ד עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"to serve service"

Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve carefully]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 4:24 (#1)
content:
זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֔ת מִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת הַ⁠גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֑י

"This {is} the service of the clans of the Gershonite"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This is how the clans of the Gershonite serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:24 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֑י

"the Gershonite"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific Gershonite. He means all the descendants of Gershon in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gershonites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 4:24 (#3)
content:
לַ⁠עֲבֹ֖ד וּ⁠לְ⁠מַשָּֽׂא

"to serve and according to a burden"

These phrases specify what exactly the service of the Gershonites was. It included both serving and carrying burdens. You could make this idea more explicit if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [both to serve and to carry their burdens]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:25 (#1)
content:
אֶת־יְרִיעֹ֤ת הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּן֙ וְ⁠אֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד

"the curtains of the Dwelling and the tent of meeting"

Here, the word Dwelling refers specifically to the inner part of the sacred tent. The phrase tent of meeting refers specifically to the outer part of the sacred tent. See how you translated the similar phrases in 3:25. Alternate translation: [the curtains of the inner part of the Dwelling and the outer curtains of the Dwelling]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:25 (#2)
content:
מִכְסֵ֕⁠הוּ וּ⁠מִכְסֵ֛ה הַ⁠תַּ֥חַשׁ אֲשֶׁר־עָלָ֖י⁠ו

"its covering and the covering of porpoise which {is} on it"

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that the sacred tent had both an inner and an outer covering. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [its inner covering and the outer covering of porpoise which is on it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:25 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠מִכְסֵ֛ה הַ⁠תַּ֥חַשׁ

"and the covering of porpoise"

See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:6.

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:25 (#4)
content:
מִ⁠לְ⁠מָ֑עְלָ⁠ה

"from above"

The implication is that the covering being referred to was placed on top of the other coverings that were already on the tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on top of all these things]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:25 (#5)
content:
מָסַ֔ךְ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד

"the curtain of the opening of the tent of meeting"

See how you translated this phrase in 3:25.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:26 (#1)
content:
פֶּ֣תַח ׀ שַׁ֣עַר

"the opening of the gate of"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an opening that is a gate. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the opening that is the gate of]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:26 (#2)
content:
אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּ֤ן וְ⁠עַל־הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ סָבִ֔יב

"that {is} on the Dwelling and on the altar all around"

See how you translated this clause in 3:26.

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:26 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠אֵת֙ מֵֽיתְרֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וְ⁠אֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבֹדָתָ֑⁠ם וְ⁠אֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵעָשֶׂ֛ה לָ⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠עָבָֽדוּ

"and their ropes and all the vessels of their service and all that is done for them; and they shall serve"

Here, the pronouns their and them refer to the curtains for the sacred tent, and the pronoun they refers to the Gershonites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the ropes for the curtains and all the vessels of the curtain’s service and all that is done for the curtains; and the Gershonites shall serve]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 4:26 (#4)
content:
כְּלֵ֖י עֲבֹדָתָ֑⁠ם

"the vessels of their service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vessels with which they are served]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:26 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠אֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵעָשֶׂ֛ה לָ⁠הֶ֖ם

"and all that is done for them"

The expression is to be done is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the Gershonites. Alternate translation: [all that the Gershonites do for them]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 4:27 (#1)
content:
עַל־פִּי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן וּ⁠בָנָ֜י⁠ו

"Upon the mouth of Aaron and his sons"

The phrase upon the mouth of Aaron and his sons is a common expression of his culture to mean “according to what Aaron and his sons command.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [According to what Aaron and his sons say]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:27 (#2)
content:
כָּל־עֲבֹדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַ⁠גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֔י

"all the service of the sons of the Gershonite"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how the sons of the Gershonite serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:27 (#3)
content:
הַ⁠גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֔י

"the Gershonite"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific Gershonite. He means Gershonites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gershonites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 4:27 (#4)
content:
וּ⁠לְ⁠כֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתָ֑⁠ם

"and according to all their service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and according to how they serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:27 (#5)
content:
וּ⁠פְקַדְתֶּ֤ם

"And you shall count"

The word you is plural here because God is speaking to Moses and Aaron. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 4:27 (#6)
content:
וּ⁠פְקַדְתֶּ֤ם

"And you shall count"

The implication is that Moses and Aaron are to assign specific tasks and equipment to specific people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar phrase in 3:10. Alternate translation: [And you shall appoint]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:27 (#7)
content:
בְּ⁠מִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת אֵ֖ת כָּל־מַשָּׂאָֽ⁠ם

"all their burden in keeping"

By all their burden in keeping, Yahweh means everything that they must guard while they are carrying it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [everything that they must guard as they carry it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:28 (#1)
content:
זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֗ת מִשְׁפְּחֹ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י הַ⁠גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י

"This {is} the service of the clans of the sons of the Gershonite"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This is how the clans of the sons of the Gershonite serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:28 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י

"the Gershonite"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific Gershonite. He means the Gershonites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gershonites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 4:28 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠יַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר

"is} in the hand of Ithamar"

Yahweh is using the common expression of his culture in the hand of to mean “under the authority of” or “under the supervision of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [under the control of]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:29 (#1)
content:
בְּנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֥⁠ם לְ⁠בֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖⁠ם תִּפְקֹ֥ד אֹתָֽ⁠ם

"The sons of Merari, according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers, you shall count them"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about counting first, followed by the information about their clans and the house of their fathers. Alternate translation: [You shall count the sons of Merari, according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 4:29 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֥⁠ם לְ⁠בֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖⁠ם

"according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers"

See how you translated these phrases in 4:2.

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:29 (#3)
content:
תִּפְקֹ֥ד

"you shall count"

The word you is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [you, Moses, shall count]

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 4:30 (#1)
content:
כָּל־הַ⁠בָּא֙ לַ⁠צָּבָ֔א

"everyone who comes to the army"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:23.

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:30 (#2)
content:
לַ⁠עֲבֹ֕ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת

"to serve the service"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 4:30 (#3)
content:
אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד

"the service of the tent of meeting"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as the tent of meeting needs to be served]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:31 (#1)
content:
לְ⁠כָל־עֲבֹדָתָ֖⁠ם

"according to all their service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [according to how they serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:31 (#2)
content:
קַרְשֵׁי֙ הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּ֔ן וּ⁠בְרִיחָ֖י⁠ו וְ⁠עַמּוּדָ֥י⁠ו וַ⁠אֲדָנָֽי⁠ו

"the frames of the Dwelling and its crossbars and its pillars and its bases"

See how you referred to these items in 3:36.

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:32 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠עַמּוּדֵי֩ הֶ⁠חָצֵ֨ר סָבִ֜יב וְ⁠אַדְנֵי⁠הֶ֗ם וִֽ⁠יתֵדֹתָ⁠ם֙ וּ⁠מֵ֣יתְרֵי⁠הֶ֔ם

"and the pillars of the courtyard all around and their bases and their pegs and their ropes"

See how you referred to these items in 3:37.

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 4:32 (#2)
content:
וּ⁠לְ⁠כֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתָ֑⁠ם

"and for all their service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and for all the ways that they are served]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:32 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠בְ⁠שֵׁמֹ֣ת

"and by names"

The phrase by names means that the priests were to assign specific items to specific people by recording each person’s name with the items he was to be responsible for. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and by each man’s name]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:32 (#4)
content:
תִּפְקְד֔וּ

"you shall count"

The word you is plural here because Yahweh is speaking to Moses and Aaron. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 4:32 (#5)
content:
תִּפְקְד֔וּ

"you shall count"

The implication is that Moses and Aaron are to assign specific tasks and equipment to specific people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:27. Alternate translation: [you shall appoint]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:32 (#6)
content:
אֶת־כְּלֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת מַשָּׂאָֽ⁠ם

"the vessels of the keeping of their burden"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe vessels that are a burden and that require keeping. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vessels that they must keep as they carry them]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 4:33 (#1)
content:
זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֗ת מִשְׁפְּחֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י לְ⁠כָל־עֲבֹדָתָ֖⁠ם

"This {is} the service of the clans of the sons of Merari for all their service"

It might seem that the expression This is the service of the clans of the sons of Merari for all their service contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [This is the service of the clans of the sons of Merari]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 4:33 (#2)
content:
זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֗ת מִשְׁפְּחֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י לְ⁠כָל־עֲבֹדָתָ֖⁠ם

"This {is} the service of the clans of the sons of Merari for all their service"

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of service and service, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [This is how the clans of the sons of Merari serve as they serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:33 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠יַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר

"in the hand of Ithamar"

The phrase in the hand of is a common expression of this culture that means “under the control of” or “under the direction of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See you how you translated the similar phrase in 4:28. Alternate translation: [under the control of]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:34 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יִּפְקֹ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְ⁠אַהֲרֹ֛ן וּ⁠נְשִׂיאֵ֥י הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה

"And Moses and Aaron and the leaders of the congregation counted"

The word translated as And indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, Moses and Aaron and the leaders of the congregation counted]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 4:34 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֑י

"the Kohathite"

The author is not referring to a specific Kohathite. He means all the members of the Kohathite clan in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Kohathites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 4:34 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠בֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָֽ⁠ם

"according to their clans and according to the house of their fathers"

See how you translated these phrases in 4:2.

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 4:35 (#1)
content:
כָּל־הַ⁠בָּא֙ לַ⁠צָּבָ֔א

"everyone who comes to the army"

See how you translated this phrase in 4:30.

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 4:35 (#2)
content:
לַ⁠עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"for service"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of service, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to serve]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 4:36 (#1)
content:
פְקֻדֵי⁠הֶ֖ם

"their counted ones"

The expression their counted ones is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. See how you translated this phrase in 3:22. Alternate translation: [the ones whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders counted]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 4:36 (#2)
content:
אַלְפַּ֕יִם שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וַ⁠חֲמִשִּֽׁים

"2,750"

Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [two thousand seven hundred and fifty]

See: Numbers

title: Numbers 4:37 (#1)
content:
אֵ֤לֶּה פְקוּדֵי֙ מִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת

"These {were} the counted ones of the clans of"

See how you translated counted ones in 4:37.

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 4:37 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֔י

"the Kohathite"

title: Numbers - Chapter 5 Introduction
content:
Numbers 5 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter gives instructions for keeping the camp pure because Yahweh lives among his people. It addresses ceremonial uncleanness, repayment for wrongdoing, and what to do when a husband suspects his wife has been unfaithful.

  1. Yahweh commands Israel to send ceremonially unclean people outside the camp (1–4)
  2. Yahweh gives instructions for confessing sins and making repayment (5–10)
  3. Yahweh gives instructions on what to do when a husband suspects his wife has been unfaithful (11–31)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Uncleanness

When people or things are unclean, or impure, they are not fit to be in or near God’s presence. Uncleanness can be caused by sin, but it can also be caused by diseases or events that are not sinful. In 5:2–3, the uncleanness comes from diseases or from contact with a corpse. While having a disease or coming into contact with a corpse is not sinful, it still causes uncleanness. On the other hand, a wife who commits adultery, as discussed later in the chapter, is also unclean. This is because of the sin of adultery. With or without sin as the cause of the uncleanness, unclean people should not be in or near God’s presence.

Guilt

In 5:6–8, the word “guilt” can refer both to the fact that someone did something wrong and to the restitution that the person must pay because he or she did something wrong. Because the person has “guilt” (he or she did something wrong), he or she must return the “guilt” (the payment for restitution) to the person he or she sinned against. See the notes on these verses for translation examples.

Ceremony for a jealous husband

In 5:11–31, Yahweh tells Moses what a man should do when he thinks his wife has committed adultery. The instructions state that the man does not have direct proof, so they pertain only when he is suspicious. The ceremony includes an oath with a curse that the wife speaks, special water that she drinks, and a grain offering. Yahweh promises that he will punish any wife who has actually committed adultery, but he will not punish any wife who is innocent. The punishment is sickness or failure in reproductive organs so that the guilty wife will no longer be able to have children. It is important that Yahweh is the one who brings the punishment or not. The ceremony itself has no effect without Yahweh.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

“The priest”

Throughout this chapter, Yahweh refers to “the priest.” Since there were several priests, this phrase probably refers to whichever priest was on duty at the time. Be sure that your readers would not misunderstand the phrase “the priest.”

Order of actions in the ceremony for a jealous husband

As he outlines the ceremony for a jealous husband, Yahweh does not include all the steps in exact sequential order. Specifically, 5:24 indicates that the woman drinks the water. However, 5:27 also indicates that the woman drinks the water. Yahweh has stated the general command in 5:24, but then he specifies in 5:25–27 the steps required in having the woman drink the water. So, 5:24 is the general command, and 5:25–27 are the details of how to perform that command. You could state this more explicitly if it would be helpful in your language. See the first note on 5:25.

Belly swelling and thigh falling

The punishment that Yahweh inflicts on the wife who committed adultery includes her belly swelling and her thigh falling. These phrases refer generally to illness or failure in her reproductive organs. Scholars are unsure what specific symptoms or illnesses these phrases might refer to, but it is clear that the woman will no longer be able to have children. Consider how to express that meaning without identifying a specific illness or failure. See the notes for translation options.

title: Numbers 5:1 (#1)
content:
לֵּ⁠אמֹֽר

title: Numbers 5:2 (#1)
content:
וִֽ⁠ישַׁלְּחוּ֙ מִן־הַֽ⁠מַּחֲנֶ֔ה

content:

By everyone flowing, Moses means everyone who has an abnormal discharge from their genitals. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [everyone with abnormal discharge from their genitals]

title: Numbers 5:3 (#2)
content:

title: Numbers 5:3 (#3)
content:
תְּשַׁלֵּ֔חוּ

"you shall send"

The pronoun you here is in the plural form since Yahweh was speaking to Moses but wanted him to convey this command to all the Israelites. You could make this explicit if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [all of you must send] or [you Israelites must send]

title: Numbers 5:3 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠לֹ֤א יְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת־מַ֣חֲנֵי⁠הֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֥ן בְּ⁠תוֹכָֽ⁠ם

Alternate translation: [I am dwelling in the midst of them, so they shall not make unclean their camp]

title: Numbers 5:6 (#1)
content:
דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אִ֣ישׁ

"Speak to the sons of Israel: ‘A man"

title: Numbers 5:6 (#2)
content:
אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַעֲשׂוּ֙ מִ⁠כָּל־חַטֹּ֣את הָֽ⁠אָדָ֔ם לִ⁠מְעֹ֥ל מַ֖עַל בַּ⁠יהוָ֑ה וְ⁠אָֽשְׁמָ֖ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִֽוא

"A man or a woman, when they do from all the sins of the man to be unfaithful {in} unfaithfulness against Yahweh, then that person is guilty"

In this verse, Yahweh alternates between singular and plural forms. He does this because the instructions relate to any person. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use just the singular or plural throughout this verse. Alternate translation: [A man or woman, when he or she does from all the sins of the man to be unfaithful in unfaithfulness against Yahweh, then that person is guilty] or [Men or women, when they do from all the sins of the man to be unfaithful in unfaithfulness against Yahweh, then those people are guilty]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 5:6 (#3)
content:
חַטֹּ֣את הָֽ⁠אָדָ֔ם

"the sins of the man"

Here, Yahweh could be using the possessive form to refer to sins that are: (1) committed against a man. Alternate translation: [the sins against a man]; or (2) committed by a man. Alternate translation: [the sins by a man]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:6 (#4)
content:
הָֽ⁠אָדָ֔ם

"the man"

Here the masculine term man has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [the human]

See: When Masculine Words Include Women

title: Numbers 5:6 (#5)
content:
לִ⁠מְעֹ֥ל

"to be unfaithful"

The words translated as to be unfaithful indicate that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [with the result that they are unfaithful]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

content:
לִ⁠מְעֹ֥ל מַ֖עַל

Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to be very unfaithful]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 5:6 (#7)
content:
מַ֖עַל

"in} unfaithfulness"
