See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:7 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִתְוַדּ֗וּ אֶֽת־חַטָּאתָ⁠ם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂוּ֒ וְ⁠הֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־אֲשָׁמ⁠וֹ֙ בְּ⁠רֹאשׁ֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠חֲמִישִׁת֖⁠וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑י⁠ו וְ⁠נָתַ֕ן לַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם לֽ⁠וֹ

"And they shall confess their sin that they did, and he shall return his guilt in its head and he shall add its fifth upon it, and he shall give to him to whom he is guilty"

As in the previous verse, Yahweh alternates between singular and plural forms. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use just the singular or plural throughout this verse. Do what you did in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [And he or she shall confess his or her sin that he or she did, and he or she shall return his or her guilt in its head and he or she shall add its fifth upon it, and he or she shall give to him to whom he or she is guilty] or [And they shall confess their sin that they did, and they shall return their guilt in its head and they shall add its fifth upon it, and they shall give to him to whom they are guilty]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 5:7 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠הֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־אֲשָׁמ⁠וֹ֙ בְּ⁠רֹאשׁ֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠חֲמִישִׁת֖⁠וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑י⁠ו וְ⁠נָתַ֕ן לַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם לֽ⁠וֹ

"and he shall return his guilt in its head and he shall add its fifth upon it, and he shall give to him to whom he is guilty"

Here the masculine pronouns he, his, and him have a generic sense that includes both men and women. This can be seen from verse 6, which explicitly refers to “a man or a woman.” If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and that person shall return his or her guilt in its head and he or she shall add its fifth upon it, and he or she shall give to the person to whom he or she is guilty]

See: When Masculine Words Include Women

title: Numbers 5:7 (#3)
content:
אֶת־אֲשָׁמ⁠וֹ֙

"his guilt"

Here, guilt represents the payment that must be made as compensation for causing damage or loss to someone. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the payment for his guilt]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:7 (#4)
content:
אֶת־אֲשָׁמ⁠וֹ֙

"his guilt"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of guilt, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his guilty payment]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:7 (#5)
content:
בְּ⁠רֹאשׁ֔⁠וֹ

"in its head"

Yahweh is using in its head as a common expression of his culture to mean “in its entirety” or “in full.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in its entirety]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:7 (#6)
content:
וַ⁠חֲמִישִׁת֖⁠וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑י⁠ו

"and he shall add its fifth upon it"

Yahweh is using add its fifth as a common expression of his culture to mean “include an additional 20 percent.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall include a fifth more]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:7 (#7)
content:
וַ⁠חֲמִישִׁת֖⁠וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף

"and he shall add its fifth"

A fifth means one part out of five equal parts. Alternate translation: [and he shall add 20 percent]

See: Fractions

title: Numbers 5:7 (#8)
content:
לַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם

"to whom he is guilty"

Yahweh here refers to whomever the person sinned against. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [whom he sinned against when he became guilty]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:8 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אִם־אֵ֨ין לָ⁠אִ֜ישׁ גֹּאֵ֗ל

"And if there is not one redeeming for the man"

The implication is that the wronged person has died and there are no close relatives who can receive the payment. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And if the person who was sinned against has died and there is not one redeeming for him]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:8 (#2)
content:
לָ⁠אִ֜ישׁ גֹּאֵ֗ל

"one redeeming for the man"

The implication is that a one redeeming refers to a close relative who could receive payment on behalf of a deceased person who had been wronged. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a close relative who can represent the man]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:8 (#3)
content:
לָ⁠אִ֜ישׁ & לְ⁠הָשִׁ֤יב הָ⁠אָשָׁם֙ אֵלָ֔י⁠ו

"for the man to return the guilt to him"

Here the masculine term man has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [for the person to return the guilt to him or her]

See: When Masculine Words Include Women

title: Numbers 5:8 (#4)
content:
הָ⁠אָשָׁם֙ אֵלָ֔י⁠ו הָ⁠אָשָׁ֛ם

"the guilt to him, the guilt"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of guilt, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the guilty payment to him, the guilty payment]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:8 (#5)
content:
הָ⁠אָשָׁם֙ אֵלָ֔י⁠ו הָ⁠אָשָׁ֛ם

"the guilt to him, the guilt"

The term guilt represents “payment for guilt” or “compensation.” See how you translated the similar use of guilt in 5:7. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the payment for his guilt to him, the payment for the guilt]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:8 (#6)
content:
הָ⁠אָשָׁ֛ם הַ⁠מּוּשָׁ֥ב

"the guilt being returned"

The expression being returned is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the guilt that the guilty person is returning]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:8 (#7)
content:
לַ⁠יהוָ֖ה לַ⁠כֹּהֵ֑ן

"is} to Yahweh to the priest"

The implication is that the payment belongs to Yahweh and therefore must be given to the priest who serves him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [is for Yahweh and thus given to the priest]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:8 (#8)
content:
אֵ֚יל הַ⁠כִּפֻּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְכַפֶּר־בּ֖⁠וֹ עָלָֽי⁠ו

"the ram of the atonement upon which he shall make atonement for him"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of atonement, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the ram for atoning upon which he shall atone for him]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:8 (#9)
content:
אֵ֚יל הַ⁠כִּפֻּרִ֔ים

"the ram of the atonement"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a ram that is used for atonement. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the ram that is offered to atone]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:8 (#10)
content:
יְכַפֶּר־בּ֖⁠וֹ

"he shall make atonement for him"

The pronoun he refers to the priest, while the pronoun him refers to the guilty person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the priest shall make atonement for the guilty person]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 5:8 (#11)
content:
בּ֖⁠וֹ

"for him"

Here the masculine term him has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [for him or her]

See: When Masculine Words Include Women

title: Numbers 5:9 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠כָל־תְּרוּמָ֞ה לְ⁠כָל־קָדְשֵׁ֧י בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל

"And every contribution of all the holy things of the sons of Israel"

Yahweh is using the possessive form of the sons of Israel to describe the holy things that are characterized by belonging to or coming from Israel. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And every holy contribution by the sons of Israel]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:10 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־קֳדָשָׁ֖י⁠ו ל֣⁠וֹ יִהְי֑וּ אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִתֵּ֥ן לַ⁠כֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥⁠וֹ יִהְיֶֽה

"And a man, his holy things shall be to him; a man, what he gives to the priest, to him shall be"

These two phrases his holy things shall be to him and what he gives to the priest, to him shall be mean basically the same thing, as long as him refers in both places to the priest (see the note below on these pronouns). The second phrase emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And a man, the holy things he gives to the priest shall be to him]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 5:10 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אִ֥ישׁ & אִ֛ישׁ

"And a man & a man"

The phrase a man … a man is a common expression of his culture used to emphasize that this rule applies separately to each individual person. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [As for each man … as for each man]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:10 (#3)
content:
ל֣⁠וֹ יִהְי֑וּ & ל֥⁠וֹ יִהְיֶֽה

"shall be to him & to him shall be"

The second occurrence of him refers to the priest. The first occurrence of him could refer to: (1) the priest. Alternate translation: [shall be to the priest … to the priest shall be]; or (2) the man who owns it before giving it to the priest. Alternate translation: [shall be to that man himself …to the priest shall be]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 5:12 (#1)
content:
דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם אִ֥ישׁ

"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘A man"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to the sons of Israel. Say to them that a man]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 5:12 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם

"and say to them"

The phrase and say to them introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 5:12 (#3)
content:
אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙

"A man, a man"

In Hebrew, the repetition of a man, a man creates emphasis. If your language has different ways to show emphasis, you could use one of those instead. Alternate translation: [Any man]

See: Reduplication

title: Numbers 5:12 (#4)
content:
תִשְׂטֶ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠מָעֲלָ֥ה ב֖⁠וֹ מָֽעַל

"his wife turns aside and is unfaithful against him {in} unfaithfulness"

These two phrases turns aside and is unfaithful against him in unfaithfulness mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [his wife is unfaithful against him in unfaithfulness] or [his wife turns aside to unfaithfulness against him]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 5:12 (#5)
content:
תִשְׂטֶ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔⁠וֹ

"his wife turns aside"

Here, Yahweh is speaking of a wife’s unfaithfulness as if she had literally turned aside from a path. This metaphor means that she has stopped being faithful to her husband. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his wife does what is wrong]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:12 (#6)
content:
וּ⁠מָעֲלָ֥ה ב֖⁠וֹ מָֽעַל

"and is unfaithful against him {in} unfaithfulness"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and is unfaithful against him]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 5:12 (#7)
content:
מָֽעַל

"in} unfaithfulness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of unfaithfulness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in an unfaithful way]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:13 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠שָׁכַ֨ב אִ֣ישׁ אֹתָ⁠הּ֮ שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע֒

"and a man lies with her the lying of seed"

Yahweh is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase lies with her the lying of seed. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [has sexual relations with her] or [commits adultery with her]

See: Euphemism

title: Numbers 5:13 (#2)
content:
אִ֣ישׁ

"a man"

By a man Yahweh means a man who is not the woman’s husband. This would have been clear to the original readers from the context. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a man who is not her husband]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:13 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נֶעְלַם֙ מֵ⁠עֵינֵ֣י אִישָׁ֔⁠הּ

"and it is concealed from the eyes of her husband"

The expression it is concealed from the eyes of her husband is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the eyes of her husband do not see it]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:13 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠נֶעְלַם֙ מֵ⁠עֵינֵ֣י אִישָׁ֔⁠הּ וְ⁠נִסְתְּרָ֖ה

"and it is concealed from the eyes of her husband, and it is hidden"

These two phrases it is concealed from the eyes of her husband and it is hidden mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 5:13 (#5)
content:
מֵ⁠עֵינֵ֣י אִישָׁ֔⁠הּ

"from the eyes of her husband"

Here, from the eyes of her husband represents her husband’s knowledge or awareness. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from her husband]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:13 (#6)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְתְּרָ֖ה

"and it is hidden"

The expression it is hidden is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and she hides it]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:13 (#7)
content:
וְ⁠הִ֣יא נִטְמָ֑אָה & וְ⁠הִ֖וא לֹ֥א נִתְפָּֽשָׂה

"and she, she is made unclean & and she, she has not been caught"

Yahweh is stating the pronoun she separately, even though the verbs translated as she is made unclean and she has … been caught already include this meaning. He is doing that to switch from speaking about the husband to speaking about the wife. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that emphasis. Alternate translation: [and as for her, she is made unclean … and as for her, she has not been caught]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 5:13 (#8)
content:
וְ⁠הִ֣יא נִטְמָ֑אָה

"and she, she is made unclean"

The expression is made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and she, she has made herself unclean]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:13 (#9)
content:
וְ⁠הִ֖וא לֹ֥א נִתְפָּֽשָׂה

"and she, she has not been caught"

The expression has not been caught is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one has caught her]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:14 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה וְ⁠קִנֵּ֥א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖⁠וֹ וְ⁠הִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙ וְ⁠קִנֵּ֣א & וְ⁠הִ֖יא לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה

"and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife and she, she is made unclean, or a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous & and she, she is not made unclean"

It might seem that the second occurrence of the expression a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife and she, she is made unclean or she, she is not made unclean]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 5:14 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה וְ⁠קִנֵּ֥א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖⁠וֹ & אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙ וְ⁠קִנֵּ֣א & וְ⁠הִ֖יא

"and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife & or a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous & and she"

The two phrases a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could connect the phrases with a word other than and in order to show that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him so that he is jealous of his wife … or a spirit of jealousy passes over on him so that he is jealous of his wife]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 5:14 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה & אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙

"and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him & or a spirit of jealousy passes over on him"

Yahweh is using a spirit of jealousy passes over on him as a common expression of his culture to mean “he feels jealous.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he feels jealous … or he feels jealous]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:14 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠הִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה & לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה

"and she, she is made unclean & she is not made unclean"

The expression is made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and she, she has made herself unclean … and she, she has not made herself unclean]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:14 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠הִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה & לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה

"and she, she is made unclean & she is not made unclean"

Yahweh is stating the pronoun she separately, even though the verbs translated as she is made unclean and she is … made unclean already include this meaning. He is doing that to switch from speaking about the husband to speaking about the wife. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that emphasis. Alternate translation: [and as for her, she is made unclean … and as for her, she is not made caught]

See: Reflexive Pronouns

title: Numbers 5:15 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הֵבִ֤יא אֶת־קָרְבָּנָ⁠הּ֙ עָלֶ֔י⁠הָ

"And he shall bring her offering upon her"

Yahweh is using bring her offering upon her as a common expression of his culture to mean “bring the offering for her.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he shall bring the offering for her]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:15 (#2)
content:
עֲשִׂירִ֥ת הָ⁠אֵיפָ֖ה

"the tenth of the ephah"

This ephah was equivalent to 22 liters or nearly two thirds of a bushel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [about 2.2 liters] or [about two thirds of a bushel]

See: Biblical Volume

title: Numbers 5:15 (#3)
content:
עֲשִׂירִ֥ת

"the tenth"

A tenth means one part out of ten equal parts. Alternate translation: [one-tenth]

See: Fractions

title: Numbers 5:15 (#4)
content:
קֶ֣מַח שְׂעֹרִ֑ים

"of flour of barley"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe flour that is made from barley. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [flour made with barley]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:15 (#5)
content:
לֹֽא־יִצֹ֨ק עָלָ֜י⁠ו שֶׁ֗מֶן וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִתֵּ֤ן עָלָי⁠ו֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּֽי־מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ ה֔וּא מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן

"He shall not pour oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it, for it {is} a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial causing iniquity to be remembered"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the first phrase. The phrase it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial causing iniquity to be remembered gives the reason why he shall not pour oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it. Alternate translation: [It is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial causing iniquity to be remembered, so he shall not pour oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 5:15 (#6)
content:
מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ & מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן

"a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial causing iniquity to be remembered"

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of jealousy, memorial, and iniquity, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [a grain offering of a jealous husband, a grain offering that reminds a person and that causes any bad thing the person did to be remembered]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:15 (#7)
content:
מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ & מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן

"a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a grain offering that is characterized by jealousy and serves as a memorial. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a grain offering offered because of jealousy and to make a memorial]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:15 (#8)
content:
מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן

"causing iniquity to be remembered"

The expression to be remembered is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [causing people to remember iniquity]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:16 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖⁠הּ הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֑ן

"And the priest shall present her"

The implication is that the priest presents the woman at the altar to have her stand before Yahweh for judgment. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall have her come near the altar]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:16 (#2)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, to the face of represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:17 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠לָקַ֧ח הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֛ן מַ֥יִם קְדֹשִׁ֖ים בִּ⁠כְלִי־חָ֑רֶשׂ

"And the priest shall take holy water in a vessel of clay"

The implication is that the priest must first get water that was set apart for sacred use and then put it in a clay pot. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall fill a vessel of clay with holy water]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:17 (#2)
content:
וּ⁠מִן־הֶֽ⁠עָפָ֗ר & יִקַּ֥ח הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֖ן

"and the priest shall take from the dust"

Yahweh is using take from the dust as a common expression of his culture to mean “take some of the dust.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the priest shall take some of the dust]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:17 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נָתַ֥ן אֶל־הַ⁠מָּֽיִם

"and he shall put {it} to the water"

Here, Yahweh could mean that the priest should: (1) mix the dust in with the water. Alternate translation: [and he shall mix it into the water]; or (2) pour the dust on top of the water. Alternate translation: [and he shall pour it onto the water]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:18 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, to the face of represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:18 (#2)
content:
וּ⁠פָרַע֙ אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ הָֽ⁠אִשָּׁ֔ה

"and he shall loose the head of the woman"

Here, the word head could refer to: (1) the woman’s hair. In this case, the priest lets down her hair. Alternate translation: [and he shall let the woman’s hair down]; or (2) the woman’s head, which has hair on it. In this case, the priest uncovers the woman’s head and her hair. Alternate translation: [and he shall uncover the head of the woman]

See: Synecdoche

title: Numbers 5:18 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נָתַ֣ן עַל־כַּפֶּ֗י⁠הָ

"and he shall put on her palm"

Yahweh is using put on her palm as a common expression of his culture to mean “hand to her” or “give to her to hold.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall hand her]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:18 (#4)
content:
אֵ֚ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַ⁠זִּכָּר֔וֹן מִנְחַ֥ת קְנָאֹ֖ת הִ֑וא

"the grain offering of memorial. It {is} a grain offering of jealousy"

See how you translated the phrases grain offering of memorial and grain offering of jealousy in 5:15.

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:18 (#5)
content:
מֵ֥י הַ⁠מָּרִ֖ים

"the water of bitterness"

Here, Yahweh could be using the possessive form to indicate that the water: (1) causes bitterness in the woman’s life. Alternate translation: [the water that causes a bitter life]; or (2) tastes bitter. Alternate translation: [the water that tastes bitter]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:18 (#6)
content:
מֵ֥י הַ⁠מָּרִ֖ים

"the water of bitterness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of bitterness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the water that makes bitter]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:18 (#7)
content:
מֵ֥י

"the water"

Here, the water represents the vessel containing the water that has been prepared with dust from the tabernacle floor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the vessel full of the water]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:19 (#1)
content:
לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔⁠ךְ

"a man did not lie with you"

The priest is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase lie with you. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [a man did not have sexual relations with you] or [a man did not have intimate relations with you]

See: Euphemism

title: Numbers 5:19 (#2)
content:
אִישׁ֙

"a man"

By a man, Yahweh means a man who is not the woman’s husband. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a man who is not your husband]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:19 (#3)
content:
לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה

"you did not turn aside to uncleanness"

Here, Yahweh is speaking of sexual unfaithfulness as if it were turning aside to uncleanness. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you did not do what is unclean and wrong]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:19 (#4)
content:
טֻמְאָ֖ה

"to uncleanness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of uncleanness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to do what is unclean]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:19 (#5)
content:
תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑⁠ךְ

"under your husband"

Here, Yahweh could be using the phrase under your husband to indicate that: (1) the woman was married to her husband at the time. Alternate translation: [while married to your husband]; or (2) the uncleanness would have been committed with someone besides her husband. Alternate translation: [instead of your husband]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:19 (#6)
content:
הִנָּקִ֕י מִ⁠מֵּ֛י & הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה

"be free from this water"

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if this water were a captor from whom the woman could be free. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [be unaffected by this water]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:19 (#7)
content:
הִנָּקִ֕י

"be free"

The priest is using the imperative form be free to state a promise rather than to give a command. He is telling the woman that if she has not committed adultery, she will not suffer any harm from drinking the water that brings a curse. If your language does not use an imperative form to express a promise, you could use a statement about the future. Alternate translation: [you will be free]

See: Imperatives — Other Uses

title: Numbers 5:19 (#8)
content:
מִ⁠מֵּ֛י הַ⁠מָּרִ֥ים הַֽ⁠מְאָרֲרִ֖ים הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה

"from this water of bitterness that brings a curse"

See how you translated this phrase in 5:18.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:19–20 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אָמַ֤ר אֶל־הָֽ⁠אִשָּׁה֙ אִם־לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔⁠ךְ וְ⁠אִם־לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑⁠ךְ הִנָּקִ֕י מִ⁠מֵּ֛י הַ⁠מָּרִ֥ים הַֽ⁠מְאָרֲרִ֖ים הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה׃ וְ⁠אַ֗תְּ כִּ֥י שָׂטִ֛ית תַּ֥חַת אִישֵׁ֖⁠ךְ וְ⁠כִ֣י נִטְמֵ֑את וַ⁠יִּתֵּ֨ן אִ֥ישׁ בָּ⁠ךְ֙ אֶת־שְׁכָבְתּ֔⁠וֹ מִֽ⁠בַּלְעֲדֵ֖י אִישֵֽׁ⁠ךְ

"and he shall say to the woman, “If a man did not lie with you, and if you did not turn aside to uncleanness under your husband, be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse. But you, if you did turn aside under your husband, and if you were made unclean and a man gave his lying in you besides your husband"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and he shall tell the woman that if a man did not lie with her, and if she did not turn aside to uncleanness under her husband, she shall be free from the water of bitterness that brings a curse. And he will also tell that if she did turn aside under her husband, and if she was made unclean and a man gave his lying in her besides her husband,]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 5:20 (#1)
content:
שָׂטִ֛ית

"you did turn aside"

Here, Yahweh is speaking of unfaithfulness to one’s husband as if it were physically turning aside from the right path. See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:12. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you did what was wrong]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:20 (#2)
content:
תַּ֥חַת אִישֵׁ֖⁠ךְ

"under your husband"

See how you translated this phrase in 5:19.

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:20 (#3)
content:
נִטְמֵ֑את

"you were made unclean"

The expression were made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you made yourself unclean]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:20 (#4)
content:
וַ⁠יִּתֵּ֨ן אִ֥ישׁ בָּ⁠ךְ֙ אֶת־שְׁכָבְתּ֔⁠וֹ

"and a man gave his lying in you"

Yahweh is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase gave his lying in you. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [a man had sexual relations with you] or [a man had intimate relations with you]

See: Euphemism

title: Numbers 5:21 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת־הָֽ⁠אִשָּׁה֮ בִּ⁠שְׁבֻעַ֣ת

"and the priest shall make the woman swear with the oath of"

The implication is that the priest would speak the oath and then pause while the woman repeated the words after him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the priest shall stop speaking and shall make the woman swear]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:21 (#2)
content:
בִּ⁠שְׁבֻעַ֣ת הָ⁠אָלָה֒

"swear with the oath of the curse"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an oath that contains the curse. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the curse section of the oath]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:21 (#3)
content:
יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛⁠ךְ לְ⁠אָלָ֥ה וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑⁠ךְ

"Yahweh will give you to a curse and to an oath in the midst of your people"

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Yahweh were actually giving the woman to a curse and an oath. This means that Yahweh will bring about the consequences of the curse she speaks. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will make you suffer among your people what you swore in the curse and in the oath]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:21 (#4)
content:
לְ⁠אָלָ֥ה וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁבֻעָ֖ה

"to a curse and to an oath"

The phrase curse and oath expresses a single idea. The word oath tells more about curse. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [to a curse in an oath]

See: Hendiadys

title: Numbers 5:21 (#5)
content:
בְּ⁠תֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְרֵכֵ⁠ךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְ⁠אֶת־בִּטְנֵ֖⁠ךְ צָבָֽה

"when Yahweh gives your thigh falling and your belly swelling"

Here the priest refers to general sickness or failure of female reproductive organs. These phrases are general and probably do not refer to one specific type of disease or failure. However, it is clear that the sickness or failure will prevent the conception and birth of children. Consider how to make this clear to your readers. Alternate translation: [when Yahweh gives your reproductive organs failure] or [when Yahweh makes you unable to bear children]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 5:21 (#6)
content:
אֶת־יְרֵכֵ⁠ךְ֙

"your thigh"

Yahweh is referring to sexual organs in a polite way by using the phrase thigh. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [your genital organs]

See: Euphemism

title: Numbers 5:21–22 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אָמַ֤ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵן֙ לָֽ⁠אִשָּׁ֔ה יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛⁠ךְ לְ⁠אָלָ֥ה וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑⁠ךְ בְּ⁠תֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְרֵכֵ⁠ךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְ⁠אֶת־בִּטְנֵ֖⁠ךְ צָבָֽה׃ וּ֠⁠בָאוּ הַ⁠מַּ֨יִם הַ⁠מְאָרְרִ֤ים הָ⁠אֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּֽ⁠מֵעַ֔יִ⁠ךְ לַ⁠צְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְ⁠לַ⁠נְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ

"And the priest shall say to the woman, “Yahweh will give you to a curse and to an oath in the midst of your people when Yahweh gives your thigh falling and your belly swelling. And this water that brings a curse will go in your insides to cause belly to swell and to cause thigh to fall"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall tell the woman that Yahweh will give her to a curse and to an oath in the midst of her people when Yahweh gives her thigh falling and her belly swelling. He will tell her that this water that brings a curse will go in her insides to cause belly to swell and to cause thigh to fall.]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 5:22 (#1)
content:
לַ⁠צְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְ⁠לַ⁠נְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ

"to cause belly to swell and to cause thigh to fall"

See how you translated the similar phrases in 5:21.

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 5:22 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אָמְרָ֥ה הָ⁠אִשָּׁ֖ה אָמֵ֥ן ׀ אָמֵֽן

"And the woman shall say, “Amen, amen"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And the woman shall say amen twice.]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 5:23 (#1)
content:
אֶת־הָ⁠אָלֹ֥ת הָ⁠אֵ֛לֶּה

"these curses"

The implication is that these curses refers to the curse oath that the woman swore in 5:21. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the curses the woman spoke]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:23 (#2)
content:
בַּ⁠סֵּ֑פֶר

"in the book"

The priest is not referring to a specific book. He means a scroll or other writing material in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in a book]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 5:23 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠מָחָ֖ה אֶל־מֵ֥י הַ⁠מָּרִֽים

"and he shall wipe {them} out into the water of bitterness"

The implication is that the priest will write the curses on a book or scroll and then wash off the ink into the water of bitterness so that the water contains the written curses. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and he shall use the water of bitterness to wash the words of the curses off the book into the water]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:23 (#4)
content:
אֶל־מֵ֥י הַ⁠מָּרִֽים

"into the water of bitterness"

See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:18.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:24 (#1)
content:
אֶת־מֵ֥י הַ⁠מָּרִ֖ים הַ⁠מְאָֽרֲרִ֑ים

"the water of bitterness that brings a curse"

See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:18.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 5:24 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠מַּ֥יִם הַֽ⁠מְאָרֲרִ֖ים לְ⁠מָרִֽים

"the water that brings a curse to bitterness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of bitterness, you could express the same idea in another way. This phrase is similar to the one earlier in the verse, so see how you translated the word bitterness there. Alternate translation: [the water that brings a curse and so makes bitter]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:25 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠לָקַ֤ח הַ⁠כֹּהֵן֙

"And the priest shall take"

In 5:25–27, Yahweh explains the process by which the priest will have the woman drink the water, which is summarized in 5:24. If it would be helpful in your language, you could indicate that this is an explanation, not the next action in sequence. Alternate translation: [Specifically, the priest shall take] or [Before he has her drink the water, the priest shall take]

See: Connect — Background Information

title: Numbers 5:25 (#2)
content:
אֵ֖ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַ⁠קְּנָאֹ֑ת

"the grain offering of jealousy"

See how you translated this phrase in 5:15.

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:25 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠הֵנִ֤יף אֶת־הַ⁠מִּנְחָה֙ לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה

"and he shall raise the grain offering to the face of Yahweh"

The raising of the grain offering was a symbolic action by which the priest showed that he was presenting the offering to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and he shall lift up the grain offering to the face of Yahweh to dedicate it to him]

See: Symbolic Action

title: Numbers 5:25 (#4)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, to the face of represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:25 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠הִקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖⁠הּ אֶל־הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּֽחַ

"and he shall present it to the altar"

Yahweh is using present it to the altar as a common expression of his culture to mean “bring it near to the altar.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall bring it near the altar]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 5:26 (#1)
content:
אֶת־אַזְכָּ֣רָתָ֔⁠הּ

"its memorial portion"

The implication is the priest presented only a handful the grain offering to represent the entire offering before God and to serve as a memorial or reminder. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a handful, which is its memorial portion,]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:27 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִשְׁקָ֣⁠הּ אֶת־הַ⁠מַּ֗יִם

"And he shall make her drink the water"

It might seem that the expression And he shall make her drink the water contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language since this was just stated in 5:26. If so, you can omit it.

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 5:27 (#2)
content:
נִטְמְאָה֮ וַ⁠תִּמְעֹ֣ל מַ֣עַל בְּ⁠אִישָׁ⁠הּ֒

"she was made unclean and was unfaithful {in} unfaithfulness against her husband"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since she was made unclean describes the result and was unfaithful in unfaithfulness against her husband gives the reason for that result. Alternate translation: [she was unfaithful in unfaithfulness against her husband and so was made unclean]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 5:27 (#3)
content:
וַ⁠תִּמְעֹ֣ל מַ֣עַל בְּ⁠אִישָׁ⁠הּ֒

"and was unfaithful {in} unfaithfulness against her husband"

See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:12.

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 5:27 (#4)
content:
נִטְמְאָה֮

"she was made unclean"

The expression was made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [she made herself unclean]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:27 (#5)
content:

title: Numbers 5:27 (#6)
content:
וְ⁠צָבְתָ֣ה בִטְנָ֔⁠הּ וְ⁠נָפְלָ֖ה יְרֵכָ֑⁠הּ

title: Numbers 5:27 (#7)
content:
וְ⁠הָיְתָ֧ה הָ⁠אִשָּׁ֛ה לְ⁠אָלָ֖ה בְּ⁠קֶ֥רֶב עַמָּֽ⁠הּ

"and the woman will become a curse in the midst of her people"

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the woman herself were actually a curse. This refers to how she will experience the bad things in the curse, and her people will see this. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the woman will suffer among her people what she swore in the curse]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:28 (#1)
content:
לֹ֤א נִטְמְאָה֙ הָֽ⁠אִשָּׁ֔ה וּ⁠טְהֹרָ֖ה הִ֑וא

"the woman was not made unclean, and she {is} clean"

The phrases the woman was not made unclean and she is clean mean the same thing. For emphasis, Yahweh is saying it first negatively and then positively. If a speaker of your language would not use repetition like this, in your translation you can convey the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [the woman is completely clean]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 5:28 (#2)
content:
לֹ֤א נִטְמְאָה֙ הָֽ⁠אִשָּׁ֔ה

"the woman was not made unclean"

The expression was not made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the woman did not make herself unclean]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 5:28 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נִקְּתָ֖ה

"then she will be free"

Here, the woman could be free: (1) from the negative affects of the water and the curse. This is what free explicitly refers to in 5:19. Alternate translation: [then she will be free of the water and the curse]; or (2) from any declaration of guilt. Alternate translation: [then she will be free of guilt]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 5:28 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠נִזְרְעָ֥ה זָֽרַע

"and she will be sown {with} seed"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and she will be sown successfully]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 5:28 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠נִזְרְעָ֥ה זָֽרַע

"and she will be sown {with} seed"

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if a woman’s ability to have children were the same as if someone were planting seed in a field. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and she will be able to have children]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:28 (#6)

וְ⁠נִזְרְעָ֥ה זָֽרַע

If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is her husband. Alternate translation: [and her husband will sow her with seed]

content:
תּוֹרַ֖ת הַ⁠קְּנָאֹ֑ת

"the law of jealousy"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a law that is followed when there is jealousy. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the law for dealing with jealousy]

title: Numbers 5:29 (#2)

תּוֹרַ֖ת הַ⁠קְּנָאֹ֑ת

אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּשְׂטֶ֥ה אִשָּׁ֛ה

"when a woman turns aside"

Here, Yahweh is speaking of a wife who is unfaithful to her husband as if she had physically turned aside from him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when a woman does what is wrong]

content:
תַּ֥חַת אִישָׁ֖⁠הּ

"under her husband"

title: Numbers 5:29 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠נִטְמָֽאָה

"and is made unclean"

The expression is made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and makes herself unclean]

title: Numbers 5:30 (#1)
content:
תַּעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֛י⁠ו ר֥וּחַ קִנְאָ֖ה וְ⁠קִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֑⁠וֹ

"a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife"

content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, to the face of represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

title: Numbers 5:30 (#3)
content:
אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַ⁠תּוֹרָ֖ה הַ⁠זֹּֽאת

"all this law"

Here, all this law represents the specific instructions given for the test of jealousy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everything that this law states]

title: Numbers 5:31 (#1)
content:
תִּשָּׂ֖א אֶת־עֲוֺנָֽ⁠הּ

"will lift up her iniquity"

Here, Yahweh speaks of being punished for iniquity as if it were lifting up that iniquity. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will bear her iniquity] or [will be punished for her iniquity]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 5:31 (#2)
content:
מֵ⁠עָוֺ֑ן & אֶת־עֲוֺנָֽ⁠הּ

"from iniquity & her iniquity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the ideas of iniquity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from doing wrong … what she did wrong]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 5:31 (#3)
content:
מֵ⁠עָוֺ֑ן

"from iniquity"

Here, the word iniquity could refer to: (1) punishment because of iniquity. Alternate translation: [from punishment]; or (2) guilt because of iniquity. Alternate translation: [from guilt]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 5:31 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠הָ⁠אִשָּׁ֣ה הַ⁠הִ֔וא

"and this woman"

By this woman, Yahweh means the woman who has committed adultery. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the woman who is guilty]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers - Chapter 6 Introduction
content:
Numbers 6 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter outlines laws for Nazirites (people who dedicate themselves to Yahweh in a special way and for a specific period of time). These laws indicate what the Nazirites must abstain from, what to do if they become unclean before the end of their time as Nazirites, and the sacrifices they should offer once they complete their time as Nazirites. The chapter ends with a blessing that the priests pronounce over the Israelites.

  1. Yahweh gives instructions for the Nazirite vow (1–21)
  2. Yahweh instructs Aaron and his sons to bless Israel (22–27)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Nazirite vow

The term “Nazirite” refers to someone who has vowed to separate himself or herself to Yahweh for a period of time. This period of time could be the person’s entire life, as in the case of Samson. Nazirites had to avoid three things: (1) eating or drinking anything produced from grapes or with any alcoholic content, (2) cutting their hair, (3) coming into contact with dead bodies. If any Nazirite came into contact with a dead body, he or she had to offer sacrifices and restart the time of separation. Once the time was complete, each Nazirite had to shave off his or her hair and offer a specific set of sacrifices. He or she could also offer more than what was required.

Priestly blessing

In 6:24–26, Yahweh provides a blessing that the priests should speak to the Israelites. This blessing asks Yahweh to protect, care for, and give peace to the Israelites. Yahweh then promises that he will indeed carry out what this blessing asks. Consider how you might express a blessing in your language.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

Gender and number

In 6:2, Yahweh clearly states that a Nazirite can be a man or a woman. However, the rest of the chapter uses masculine and singular language to refer to each Nazirite. In Moses’ language, masculine and singular language could refer generically to anyone. If masculine and singular language would not refer generically to anyone in your language, consider how you might naturally include anyone who could be a Nazirite. The UST often models how to use plural forms in many verses. You could also consider using the second person to address Nazirites directly in these verses.

The “separation”

Throughout this chapter, Yahweh refers to Nazirites’ “separation,” which refers to the way in which Nazirites avoid certain things as they dedicate themselves to Yahweh. Yahweh uses the word “separation” to refer to the action of separating and to the long hair that they grow during this time. The notes on specific verses will indicate which meaning of “separation” is in view.

title: Numbers 6:1 (#1)
content:
לֵּ⁠אמֹֽר

"saying"

Here and throughout the chapter, the word saying introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated saying in 1:1.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 6:2 (#1)
content:
דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה

"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘A man or a woman"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them that a man or a woman]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 6:2 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם

"and say to them"

The phrase and say to them introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 6:2 (#3)
content:
כִּ֤י יַפְלִא֙

"when he does something wonderful"

Here and in 6:3–21, the masculine language refers generically to men or women, as the phrase “A man or a woman” earlier in this verse shows. See the chapter introduction for more information. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [when he or she does something wonderful]

See: When Masculine Words Include Women

title: Numbers 6:2 (#4)
content:
כִּ֤י יַפְלִא֙ לִ⁠נְדֹּר֙ נֶ֣דֶר

"when he does something wonderful to vow a vow"

The implication is that when someone makes a vow to become a Nazirite, they are making a serious and special commitment to Yahweh. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [when he makes a special vow, the vow of]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:2 (#5)
content:
לִ⁠נְדֹּר֙ נֶ֣דֶר נָזִ֔יר

"to vow a vow of a Nazirite"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to vow to be]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 6:2 (#6)
content:
לְ⁠הַזִּ֖יר לַֽ⁠יהוָֽה

"to make separate to Yahweh"

The phrase to make separate to Yahweh is a common expression of this culture that means “to dedicate oneself to Yahweh” or “to set oneself apart for service to Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to set himself apart for Yahweh]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:3 (#1)
content:
מִ⁠יַּ֤יִן & יַזִּ֔יר

"he shall make separate from wine"

The phrase make separate from is a common expression of his culture to mean “completely avoid” or “abstain from.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he shall completely avoid]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:3 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠שֵׁכָר֙ & שֵׁכָ֖ר

"and intoxicating drink & intoxicating drink"

The term intoxicating drink refers to any alcoholic beverage made from grains or other substances. If your readers would not be familiar with what intoxicating drink is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and any drink with alcohol in it … any drink with alcohol in it]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 6:3 (#3)
content:
חֹ֥מֶץ יַ֛יִן וְ⁠חֹ֥מֶץ שֵׁכָ֖ר

"the vinegar of wine and the vinegar of intoxicating drink"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe vinegar that is made from wine or intoxicating drink. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [vinegar made from wine and vinegar made from intoxicating drink]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:3 (#4)
content:
חֹ֥מֶץ יַ֛יִן וְ⁠חֹ֥מֶץ שֵׁכָ֖ר

"the vinegar of wine and the vinegar of intoxicating drink"

Here, vinegar is a kind of sour liquid made from fermented wine or other fermented drinks. If your readers would not be familiar with what vinegar is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [sour juice of … sour juice of]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 6:4 (#1)
content:
כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֑⁠וֹ

"All the days of his separation"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [All the days he is separate]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:4 (#2)
content:
מִ⁠גֶּ֣פֶן הַ⁠יַּ֗יִן

"from the vine of the wine"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a vine that is connected with wine. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from the vine from which wine is produced]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:4 (#3)
content:
מִ⁠גֶּ֣פֶן

"from the vine"

Here, vine represents everything that comes from grape vines. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the grapes of the vine]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:4 (#4)
content:
מִ⁠כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה

"from all that is made"

The expression is made is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [from all that anyone makes]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 6:4 (#5)
content:
מֵ⁠חַרְצַנִּ֛ים וְ⁠עַד־זָ֖ג

"from seeds and up to skin"

Yahweh is referring to all parts of a grape by naming two major components, seeds and skin. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from any part of a grape]

See: Merism

title: Numbers 6:5 (#1)
content:
נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"the vow of his separation"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a vow that is characterized by separation. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vow in which he swore separation]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:5 (#2)
content:
נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"the vow of his separation"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his vow to be separate]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:5 (#3)
content:
תַּ֖עַר

"a razor"

A razor is a kind of tool for cutting hair. If your readers would not be familiar with what a razor is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a shaving tool]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 6:5 (#4)
content:
תַּ֖עַר לֹא־יַעֲבֹ֣ר עַל־רֹאשׁ֑⁠וֹ

"a razor shall not pass over upon his head"

Yahweh is using a razor shall not pass over upon his head as a common expression of this culture to mean “he must not cut his hair.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a razor shall not be used on his head]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:5 (#5)
content:
רֹאשׁ֑⁠וֹ

"upon his head"

Here, head represents the hair on the head. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair on his head]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:5 (#6)
content:
אֲשֶׁר־יַזִּ֤יר לַ⁠יהוָה֙

"that he made separate to Yahweh"

Yahweh is using the phrase made separate to Yahweh as a common expression of his culture to mean “set himself apart for Yahweh” or “dedicated himself to Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:2. Alternate translation: [that he set himself apart for Yahweh]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:5 (#7)
content:
גַּדֵּ֥ל

"and shall make great"

The implication is that shall make great means to let the hair grow long. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and shall grow out]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:5 (#8)
content:
פֶּ֖רַע שְׂעַ֥ר רֹאשֽׁ⁠וֹ

"the locks of the hair of his head"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe locks that are the hair that is on his head. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the hairs on his head]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:6 (#1)
content:
הַזִּיר֖⁠וֹ לַ⁠יהוָ֑ה

"him making separate to Yahweh"

The phrase making separate to Yahweh is a common expression of this culture that means “dedicating oneself to Yahweh” or “setting oneself apart for Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:2. Alternate translation: [him setting himself apart for Yahweh]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:6 (#2)
content:
עַל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ מֵ֖ת לֹ֥א יָבֹֽא

"he shall not go upon a person having died"

Here, Yahweh is speaking of being close to a dead person as if one could literally go upon them. This refers to approaching a dead body. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he shall not come close to a person having died]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 6:7 (#1)
content:
לְ⁠אָבִ֣י⁠ו וּ⁠לְ⁠אִמּ֗⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָחִי⁠ו֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠אַ֣חֹת֔⁠וֹ לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָ⁠הֶ֖ם בְּ⁠מֹתָ֑⁠ם כִּ֛י נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖י⁠ו עַל־רֹאשֽׁ⁠וֹ

"For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not make himself unclean for them in their death, because the separation of his God {is} upon his head"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since because the separation of his God is upon his head gives the reason for the result that For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not make himself unclean for them in their death describes. Alternate translation: [Since the separation of his God is upon his head, he shall not make himself unclean for his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, in their death.]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 6:7 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠אָבִ֣י⁠ו וּ⁠לְ⁠אִמּ֗⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָחִי⁠ו֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠אַ֣חֹת֔⁠וֹ לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָ⁠הֶ֖ם בְּ⁠מֹתָ֑⁠ם

"For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not make himself unclean for them in their death"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about making himself unclean before the list of relatives (his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister). Alternate translation: [He shall not make himself unclean for his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, in their death]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 6:7 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠אָבִ֣י⁠ו וּ⁠לְ⁠אִמּ֗⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָחִי⁠ו֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠אַ֣חֹת֔⁠וֹ

"For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister"

Here, Yahweh refers to a person’s closest relatives to refer to any close relatives. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For any close relatives, even his father, mother, brother, and sister]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:7 (#4)
content:
לְ⁠אָחִי⁠ו֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠אַ֣חֹת֔⁠וֹ

"for his brother and for his sister"

The terms brother and sister include both older and younger siblings. Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship. Alternate translation: [for any brother or sister]

See: Kinship

title: Numbers 6:7 (#5)
content:
לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָ⁠הֶ֖ם

"he shall not make himself unclean for them"

By he shall not make himself unclean for them, Yahweh means he must not participate in funeral rituals or come near the dead bodies of even his closest relatives. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he shall not make himself unclean for them by coming close to them]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:7 (#6)
content:
בְּ⁠מֹתָ֑⁠ם

"in their death"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of death, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when they die]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:7 (#7)
content:
נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖י⁠ו

"the separation of his God"

Here, separation represents the hair that a Nazirite grew to show his dedication to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair that represents the separation of his God]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:7 (#8)
content:
נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖י⁠ו

"the separation of his God"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a separation that is directed toward his God. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the separation for his God’s sake]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:7 (#9)
content:
נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖י⁠ו

"the separation of his God"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how he separated himself for his God]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:8 (#1)
content:
כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֑⁠וֹ

"All the days of his separation"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [All the days while he separates himself]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:9 (#1)
content:
יָמ֨וּת מֵ֤ת

"a dying one dies"

It might seem that the expression a dying one dies contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [a person dies]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 6:9 (#2)
content:
מֵ֤ת עָלָי⁠ו֙

"dies upon him"

Yahweh is using dies upon him as a common expression of his culture to mean “dies close to him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [dies close to him]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:9 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠פֶ֣תַע פִּתְאֹ֔ם

"in suddenness suddenly"

Here Yahweh is using a construction in which two words come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [very suddenly]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 6:9 (#4)
content:
בְּ⁠פֶ֣תַע

"in suddenness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of suddenness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [unexpectedly]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:9 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠טִמֵּ֖א

"and he makes & unclean"

The word translated as and indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and so he makes unclean]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 6:9 (#6)
content:
רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑⁠וֹ

"the head of his separation"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a head that shows or represents his separation. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his head that represents his separation]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:9 (#7)
content:
רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑⁠וֹ

"the head of his separation"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his head that represents how he made himself separate]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:9 (#8)
content:
רֹ֣אשׁ

"the head"

Here, head represents the hair on the head. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair on the head]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:9 (#9)
content:
וְ⁠גִלַּ֤ח רֹאשׁ⁠וֹ֙ בְּ⁠י֣וֹם טָהֳרָת֔⁠וֹ בַּ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י יְגַלְּחֶֽ⁠נּוּ

"then he shall shave his head on the day of his purification; on the seventh day he shall shave it"

It might seem that the expression he shall shave it contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [then he shall shave his head on the day of his purification, which is the seventh day]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 6:9 (#10)
content:
רֹאשׁ⁠וֹ֙

"his head"

Here, head represents the hair on the head of the Nazirite. The long hair was a visible sign of the Nazirite’s dedication to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair on his head]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:9 (#11)
content:
בְּ⁠י֣וֹם טָהֳרָת֔⁠וֹ בַּ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י יְגַלְּחֶֽ⁠נּוּ

"on the day of his purification; on the seventh day he shall shave it"

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that a person who becomes unclean from being near a dead body must wait seven days before being purified, according to the law in Numbers 19:11–22. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the day of his purification. That is the seventh day after he was near a dead body according to the law concerning impurity from corpses, and on that day he shall shave it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:9 (#12)
content:
בְּ⁠י֣וֹם טָהֳרָת֔⁠וֹ

"on the day of his purification"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of purification, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on the day when he is purified]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:9 (#13)
content:
בַּ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י

"on the seventh day"

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as the seventh day, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [day seven]

See: Ordinal Numbers

title: Numbers 6:10 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁמִינִ֗י

"And on the eighth day"

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as the eighth day, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [And on day eight]

See: Ordinal Numbers

title: Numbers 6:10 (#2)
content:
בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֑ה

"sons of a pigeon"

Here, sons of a pigeon refers to young pigeons. Yahweh is speaking as if they were actually children of the mother bird. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [pigeons that are young]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 6:11 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠כִפֶּ֣ר

"and he shall make atonement"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of atonement, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he shall atone]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:11 (#2)
content:
עָלָ֔י⁠ו מֵ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖א

"for him from what he sinned"

Yahweh is using for him from what he sinned as a common expression of this culture to mean “to restore him after he had sinned.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to restore him after he sinned]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:11 (#3)
content:
עַל־הַ⁠נָּ֑פֶשׁ

"upon the person"

The implication is that the person was defiled by touching or being near a dead person. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [concerning the dead person]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:11 (#4)
content:
אֶת־רֹאשׁ֖⁠וֹ

"his head"

Here, head represents the Nazirite’s hair, which showed that he was dedicated to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair that will grow on his head]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:12 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִזִּ֤יר לַֽ⁠יהוָה֙ אֶת־יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"And he shall make separate to Yahweh the days of his separation"

Yahweh is using the expression make separate as a common expression of this culture to mean “set himself apart” or “dedicate himself.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:2. Alternate translation: [And he shall set himself apart for Yahweh during the days of his separation]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:12 (#2)
content:
אֶת־יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"the days of his separation"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the days he is separate]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:12 (#3)
content:
בֶּן־שְׁנָת֖⁠וֹ

"a son of his year"

The expression a son of his year is a common expression of his culture that means “one year old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a year old]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 6:12 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠הַ⁠יָּמִ֤ים הָ⁠רִאשֹׁנִים֙ יִפְּל֔וּ

"And the first days shall fall"

Here, the text speaks of the first days of separation as if they could fall, meaning they would not count toward the total time of separation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the first days must not be included in the time of separation]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 6:12 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠הַ⁠יָּמִ֤ים הָ⁠רִאשֹׁנִים֙

"And the first days"

The implication is that this is the first period during which the Nazirite had taken the vow before he was made unclean. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the days before he was made unclean]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:12 (#6)
content:
טָמֵ֖א נִזְרֽ⁠וֹ

"his separation was made unclean"

The expression his separation was made unclean is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the dead body made his separation unclean]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 6:12 (#7)
content:
טָמֵ֖א נִזְרֽ⁠וֹ

"his separation was made unclean"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he was made unclean while he was separate]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:12 (#8)
content:
נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"of his separation"

Here, separation represents the condition or state of being set apart as a Nazirite. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he, during his time of separation,]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 6:13 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַ⁠נָּזִ֑יר

"And this is the law of the Nazirite"

By this, Yahweh means the instructions that follow about what should happen when a Nazirite’s period of dedication is complete. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [What follows is the law concerning the Nazirite]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 6:13 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠נָּזִ֑יר

"the Nazirite"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific Nazirite. He means Nazirites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Nazirites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 6:13 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠י֗וֹם מְלֹאת֙ יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"On the day of the fulfilling of the days of his separation"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the day on which the days that make up his time of separation are fulfilled. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [On the day when the time during which he is separate is fulfilled]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 6:13 (#4)
content:
יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔⁠וֹ

"the days of his separation"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of separation, you could express the same idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in 6:12. Alternate translation: [the days he is separate]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 6:13 (#5)
content:
יָבִ֣יא אֹת֔⁠וֹ

"he shall bring him"
