See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:33 (#2)
content:
וַ⁠תְּכַ֤ס עֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ

"and the earth covered over them"

The author is speaking of the earth as if it were a living thing that could cover people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they were covered with earth]

See: Personification

title: Numbers 16:34 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל

"And all Israel"

Here, all Israel represents each member of the Israelite community. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And each Israelite]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:34 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠קֹלָ֑⁠ם

"to their voice"

The implication is that the Israelites fled because they heard the screams of those who were falling into the opening in the ground. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because of their yells as they fell] or [when they heard them shouting as they fell]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:34 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠קֹלָ֑⁠ם

"to their voice"

Here, to their voice represents the sounds they made when the ground opened and swallowed them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the sounds they made]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:34 (#4)
content:
כִּ֣י אָֽמְר֔וּ

"for they said"

The word translated as for indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [and here is why: they said]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 16:34 (#5)
content:
פֶּן־תִּבְלָעֵ֖⁠נוּ הָ⁠אָֽרֶץ

"Lest the earth swallow us"

The implication is that the Israelites would die if they did not run away. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [If we do not flee, the earth will swallow us]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:34 (#6)
content:
תִּבְלָעֵ֖⁠נוּ הָ⁠אָֽרֶץ

"the earth swallow us"

The author is speaking of the earth as if it were a living thing that could swallow people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar clause in verse 30. Alternate translation: [the earth engulf them]

See: Personification

title: Numbers 16:35 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אֵ֥שׁ יָצְאָ֖ה

"And fire went out"

The author does not clarify whether the event narrated in this verse happened during or after the events narrated in the previous verses. If possible, do not use a time word or phrase to introduce this verse. Alternate translation: [In addition, fire went out]

See: Order of Events

title: Numbers 16:35 (#2)
content:
יָצְאָ֖ה

"went out"

In a context such as this, your language might say “came out” instead of went out. Alternate translation: [came out]

See: Go and Come

title: Numbers 16:35 (#3)
content:
וַ⁠תֹּ֗אכַל

"and it ate"

Here the author is speaking of fire as if it were a living thing that could eat. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it burned up]

See: Personification

title: Numbers 16:35 (#4)
content:
אֵ֣ת הַ⁠חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּ⁠מָאתַ֨יִם֙

"the 250"

Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [two hundred and fifty]

See: Numbers

title: Numbers 16:37 (#1)
content:
אֱמֹ֨ר אֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֗ן וְ⁠יָרֵ֤ם אֶת־הַ⁠מַּחְתֹּת֙ מִ⁠בֵּ֣ין הַ⁠שְּׂרֵפָ֔ה וְ⁠אֶת־הָ⁠אֵ֖שׁ זְרֵה־הָ֑לְאָה כִּ֖י קָדֵֽשׁוּ

"Say to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, and he shall raise the censers from between the burning, and scatter the fire beyond, for they are holy"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the last phrase for they are holy gives the reason for the result that the first phrases describe. Alternate translation: [The censers are holy. Because of that, say to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, and he shall raise the censers from between the burning, and scatter the fire beyond]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 16:37 (#2)
content:
אֱמֹ֨ר אֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֗ן וְ⁠יָרֵ֤ם אֶת־הַ⁠מַּחְתֹּת֙ מִ⁠בֵּ֣ין הַ⁠שְּׂרֵפָ֔ה וְ⁠אֶת & זְרֵה

"Say to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, and he shall raise the censers from between the burning, and scatter"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a direct quotation. Alternate translation: [Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, “Raise the censers from between the burning.” And scatter]

See: Direct and Indirect Quotations

title: Numbers 16:37 (#3)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠מַּחְתֹּת֙

"the censers"

A censer is a kind of container used to burn incense. If your readers would not be familiar with what a censer is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. See how you translated censer in verse 6. Alternate translation: [the containers for incense]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 16:37 (#4)
content:
מִ⁠בֵּ֣ין הַ⁠שְּׂרֵפָ֔ה

"from between the burning"

The implication is that the censers were to be taken from among the ashes and remains of the men who had been burned up. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from the place where the men were burned up]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:37 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠אֶת־הָ⁠אֵ֖שׁ זְרֵה

"and scatter the fire"

Here, Yahweh may be commanding Moses: (1) to scatter the fire himself. Alternate translation: [and you, scatter the fire]; or (2) to have Eleazar scatter the fire. Alternate translation: [and he shall scatter the fire]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:37 (#6)
content:
הָ⁠אֵ֖שׁ

"the fire"

Here, fire represents the burning coals. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the embers]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:37 (#7)
content:
הָ֑לְאָה

"beyond"

Here, the word beyond could refer to: (1) an area far away from the campsite. Alternate translation: [a distance from the camp]; or (2) a spread out area. In other words, the coals should be scattered in many different places. Alternate translation: [far and wide] or [in many places]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:38 (#1)
content:
אֵ֡ת מַחְתּוֹת֩ הַֽ⁠חַטָּאִ֨ים הָ⁠אֵ֜לֶּה בְּ⁠נַפְשֹׁתָ֗⁠ם וְ⁠עָשׂ֨וּ אֹתָ֜⁠ם רִקֻּעֵ֤י פַחִים֙ צִפּ֣וּי לַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כִּֽי־הִקְרִיבֻ֥⁠ם לִ⁠פְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה וַ⁠יִּקְדָּ֑שׁוּ

"The censers of these ones sinning against their lives, and they shall make them hammered sheets of thin plates, plating for the altar, for they presented them to the face of Yahweh, and they are holy"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [These ones sinning against their lives presented the censers to the face of Yahweh, and they are holy. Because of that, they shall make them hammered sheets of thin plates, plating for the altar]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 16:38 (#2)
content:
אֵ֡ת מַחְתּוֹת֩ הַֽ⁠חַטָּאִ֨ים הָ⁠אֵ֜לֶּה בְּ⁠נַפְשֹׁתָ֗⁠ם וְ⁠עָשׂ֨וּ אֹתָ֜⁠ם רִקֻּעֵ֤י פַחִים֙

"The censers of these ones sinning against their lives, and they shall make them hammered sheets of thin plates"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what should be done with the censers before the information about how these men sinned. Alternate translation: [And they shall make the censers of these ones sinning against their lives hammered sheets of thin plates]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 16:38 (#3)
content:
הַֽ⁠חַטָּאִ֨ים & בְּ⁠נַפְשֹׁתָ֗⁠ם

"ones sinning against their lives"

Yahweh is using ones sinning against their lives as a common expression of the culture to mean “ones who caused their own deaths by sinning.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [ones sinning in a way that ends their lives] or [ones sinning with death as the result]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 16:38 (#4)
content:
בְּ⁠נַפְשֹׁתָ֗⁠ם

"against their lives"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of lives, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in such a way that they cease living]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 16:38 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠עָשׂ֨וּ

"and they shall make"

Here Yahweh is using the pronoun they in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people shall make]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 16:38 (#6)
content:
רִקֻּעֵ֤י פַחִים֙

"hammered sheets of thin plates"

Here, hammered sheets of thin plates are a kind of metalwork where metal is flattened into very thin pieces. If your readers would not be familiar with what hammered sheets of thin plates are, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [thin sheets of metal that they hammered into that shape]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 16:38 (#7)
content:
צִפּ֣וּי לַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֔חַ

"plating for the altar"

Here, plating is a kind of thin metal that is attached to the outside of something, in this case the altar. If your readers would not be familiar with what plating is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [close-fitting covering for the altar]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 16:38 (#8)
content:
לַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֔חַ

"for the altar"

Here, Yahweh does not state explicitly which altar he means. He is probably referring to the bronze altar for sacrifices, not the golden incense altar. Alternate translation: [for the altar of sacrifice]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:38 (#9)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, to the face of represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:38 (#10)
content:
וְ⁠יִֽהְי֥וּ

"and they shall be"

The pronoun they refers to the censers that were hammered into plating for the altar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the censers that are now plating for the altar shall be]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 16:39 (#1)
content:
הַ⁠שְּׂרֻפִ֑ים

"the ones being burned"

The expression ones being burned is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [the ones whom the fire burned]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 16:39 (#2)
content:
וַֽ⁠יְרַקְּע֖וּ⁠ם

"and they hammered them"

Here the author is using the pronoun they in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. See how you translated the similar form in verse 38. Alternate translation: [and people hammered them]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 16:39 (#3)
content:
צִפּ֥וּי לַ⁠מִּזְבֵּֽחַ

"as} plating for the altar"

See how you translated this phrase in 16:38. Alternate translation: [close-fitting covering for the altar of sacrifice]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 16:40 (#1)
content:
אִ֣ישׁ זָ֗ר

"a strange man"

Here, strange describes a person as if he were a foreigner when he actually is simply someone who is not authorized to perform the duties of a priest. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase “strange fire” in Numbers 3:4. Alternate translation: [an unauthorized man]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:40 (#2)
content:
מִ⁠זֶּ֤רַע אַהֲרֹן֙

"from the seed of Aaron"

Here, the author is speaking as if Aaron’s descendants were actually his seed. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the offspring of Aaron]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:40 (#3)
content:
זִכָּר֞וֹן לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְ֠מַעַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יִקְרַ֜ב אִ֣ישׁ זָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א מִ⁠זֶּ֤רַע אַהֲרֹן֙ ה֔וּא לְ⁠הַקְטִ֥יר קְטֹ֖רֶת לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה כְ⁠קֹ֨רַח֙ וְ⁠כַ֣⁠עֲדָת֔⁠וֹ כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּ⁠יַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֽ⁠וֹ

"a memorial for the sons of Israel, so that a strange man, who {is} not from the seed of Aaron, shall not come near to cause incense to become smoke to the face of Yahweh, and he shall not be like Korah and like his congregation, just as Yahweh spoke in the hand of Moses to him"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about how Yahweh spoke in the hand of Moses with the information about how Eleazar was instructed before indicating that the plating would serve as a memorial to prevent unauthorized people from offering incense. Alternate translation: [just as Yahweh spoke in the hand of Moses to him. They became a memorial for the sons of Israel, so that a strange man, who is not from the seed of Aaron, shall not come near to cause incense to become smoke to the face of Yahweh, and he shall not be like Korah and like his congregation]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 16:40 (#4)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, to the face of Yahweh represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:40 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה

"and he shall not be"

The phrase and he shall not be indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [lest he be] or [and so he shall not be]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 16:40 (#6)
content:
כְ⁠קֹ֨רַח֙ וְ⁠כַ֣⁠עֲדָת֔⁠וֹ

"like Korah and like his congregation"

The point of this comparison is that just as Korah and his congregation were punished for approaching God inappropriately, so would anyone else be who violated this command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [punished as Korah and his congregation were]

See: Simile

title: Numbers 16:40 (#7)
content:
וְ⁠כַ֣⁠עֲדָת֔⁠וֹ

"and like his congregation"

The author is using the possessive form to describe a congregation that is characterized by following Korah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated the similar form in verse 5. Alternate translation: [the people who joined him]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 16:40 (#8)
content:
בְּ⁠יַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה

"in the hand of Moses"

The author is using in the hand of as a common expression of the culture to mean “under the supervision of” or “through.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:37. Alternate translation: [under the supervision of Moses]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 16:40 (#9)
content:
לֽ⁠וֹ

"to him"

The pronoun him refers to Eleazar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to Eleazar]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 16:41 (#1)
content:
מִֽ⁠מָּחֳרָ֔ת

"from the next day"

The author is using from the next day as a common expression of the culture to mean “starting on the next day.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [starting on the next day]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 16:41 (#2)
content:
אַתֶּ֥ם הֲמִתֶּ֖ם

"You, you killed"

Here the Israelites are stating the pronoun you separately, even though they repeat it twice for emphasis. The Israelites are emphasizing that they hold Moses and Aaron personally responsible. If a speaker of your language would use a repeated pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that meaning here. Alternate translation: [You are the one who killed]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 16:41 (#3)
content:
אֶת־עַ֥ם יְהוָֽה

"the people of Yahweh"

The Israelites are using the possessive form to describe people that are characterized by serving or worshiping Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the people who serve Yahweh] or [the people who worship Yahweh]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 16:42 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִנֵּ֥ה & הֶ⁠עָנָ֑ן

"and behold, the cloud"

The author is using the term behold to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and look, the cloud] or [and they immediately noticed that the cloud]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:42 (#2)
content:
כִסָּ֖ה⁠וּ הֶ⁠עָנָ֑ן

"the cloud covered it"

By the cloud covered it, the author means that the cloud that represented God’s presence descended upon the tent of meeting. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [it was enveloped in the cloud] or [the cloud rested on it]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:42 (#3)
content:
הֶ⁠עָנָ֑ן

"the cloud"

The author assumes that readers will know this is the cloud that had been with the Israelites since their departure from Egypt and is described in Numbers 9:15–23. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the cloud that had previously been over the tent]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:42 (#4)
content:
וַ⁠יֵּרָ֖א כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה

"and the glory of Yahweh appeared"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of glory, you could express the same idea in another way. See how you translated this clause in verse 19. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh showed himself gloriously]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 16:43 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יָּבֹ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וְ⁠אַהֲרֹ֔ן

"And Moses and Aaron went"

In a context such as this, your language might say “came” instead of went. Alternate translation: [And Moses and Aaron came]

See: Go and Come

title: Numbers 16:43 (#2)
content:
אֶל־פְּנֵ֖י אֹ֥הֶל

"to the face of the tent of"

Here, to the face of represents being in front of the tent of meeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the front of] or [to the area before]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:45 (#1)
content:
הֵרֹ֗מּוּ

"Lift yourselves up"

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Moses and Aaron could physically lift themselves up and take themselves away from the assembly. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Move far away]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:45 (#2)
content:
הֵרֹ֗מּוּ

"Lift yourselves up"

The word yourselves is plural here because Yahweh is addressing Moses and Aaron, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 16:45 (#3)
content:
וַ⁠אֲכַלֶּ֥ה אֹתָ֖⁠ם

"and I shall finish them"

Yahweh is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase finish them. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. See how you translated this clause in verse 21. Alternate translation: [and I shall end their lives] or [and I will make them experience death]

See: Euphemism

title: Numbers 16:45 (#4)
content:
כְּ⁠רָ֑גַע

"according to a moment"

Here Yahweh is using according to a moment as a common expression of the culture to mean “instantly” or “immediately.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in verse 21. Alternate translation: [instantly]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 16:45 (#5)
content:
וַֽ⁠יִּפְּל֖וּ עַל־פְּנֵי⁠הֶֽם

"And they fell on their faces"

Falling on their faces was a symbolic action by which Moses and Aaron showed grief and submission to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. See how you translated this clause in verse 22. Alternate translation: [And they lay with their faces on the ground to show their grief] or [And they bowed with their faces to the ground in sorrow]

See: Symbolic Action

title: Numbers 16:46 (#1)
content:
יָצָ֥א הַ⁠קֶּ֛צֶף

"the wrath has gone out"

Here, Moses is speaking of the wrath as if it were something that could physically move out from God. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is angry and has sent punishment]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:46 (#2)
content:
קַ֣ח אֶת־הַ֠⁠מַּחְתָּה וְ⁠תֶן־עָלֶ֨י⁠הָ אֵ֜שׁ מֵ⁠עַ֤ל הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ וְ⁠שִׂ֣ים קְטֹ֔רֶת וְ⁠הוֹלֵ֧ךְ מְהֵרָ֛ה אֶל־הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה וְ⁠כַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם כִּֽי־יָצָ֥א הַ⁠קֶּ֛צֶף מִ⁠לִּ⁠פְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֵחֵ֥ל הַ⁠נָּֽגֶף

"Take the censer, and put fire on it from upon the altar, and set incense, and bring {it} quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them, for the wrath has gone out from to the face of Yahweh. The plague has begun"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these clauses, since the second set of clauses (the wrath has gone out from to the face of Yahweh. The plague has begun) gives the reason for the result that the first set of clauses describes (Take the censer, and put fire on it from upon the altar, and set incense, and bring it quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them). Alternate translation: [The wrath has gone out from to the face of Yahweh. The plague has begun. Because of that, take the censer, and put fire on it from upon the altar, and set incense, and bring it quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 16:46 (#3)
content:
אֶת־הַ֠⁠מַּחְתָּה

"the censer"

The implication is that this is the same censer Aaron had used earlier when offering incense (see Numbers 16:6–7). You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your censer] or [the censer you used earlier]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:46 (#4)
content:
אֵ֜שׁ

"fire"

Here, fire represents burning coals from the altar. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated the similar form in verse 7. Alternate translation: [embers]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:46 (#5)
content:
מֵ⁠עַ֤ל הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙

"from upon the altar"

By from upon the altar, Moses means from the altar of sacrifice where the sacred fire was kept burning. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from upon the altar of sacrifice]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:46 (#6)
content:
וְ⁠הוֹלֵ֧ךְ

"and bring {it"

In a context such as this, your language might say “take” instead of bring. Alternate translation: [and take it]

See: Go and Come

title: Numbers 16:46 (#7)
content:
וְ⁠כַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם

"and make atonement for them"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of atonement, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and offer the incense to restore them to Yahweh]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 16:46 (#8)
content:
מִ⁠לִּ⁠פְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה

"from to the face of Yahweh"

Here, from to the face of Yahweh represents coming from Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from Yahweh’s presence]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 16:46 (#9)
content:
הַ⁠נָּֽגֶף

"The plague"

Moses is not referring to a specific, known plague. He means a plague that is happening. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [A plague]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 16:47 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יִּקַּ֨ח אַהֲרֹ֜ן

"And Aaron took"

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And Aaron took a censer with fire in it]

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 16:47 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠הִנֵּ֛ה

"And behold"

The author is using the term behold to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And indeed]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 16:47 (#3)
content:
הַ⁠נֶּ֖גֶף

"the plague"

The author is not referring to a specific, known plague. He means a sickness or disease that had already begun. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a plague]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 16:47 (#4)
content:
וַ⁠יִּתֵּן֙ אֶֽת־הַ⁠קְּטֹ֔רֶת

"And he put the incense"

The implication is that Aaron put the incense on the fire in the censer. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he put the incense on the fire in the censer]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:47 (#5)
content:
וַ⁠יְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־הָ⁠עָֽם

"and he made atonement for the people"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of atonement, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he offered the incense to restore the people to Yahweh]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 16:48 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יַּעֲמֹ֥ד בֵּֽין־הַ⁠מֵּתִ֖ים וּ⁠בֵ֣ין הַֽ⁠חַיִּ֑ים

"And he stood between the ones dying and between the ones living"

The implication is that Aaron positioned himself where he could stop the plague from spreading to the rest of the people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he stood where the plague was spreading, stationing himself between the people who were dying and the people who were still alive]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:48 (#2)
content:
וַ⁠תֵּעָצַ֖ר הַ⁠מַּגֵּפָֽה

"And the plague was restrained"

The expression was restrained is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [And the plague stopped] or [And Yahweh restrained the plague]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 16:49 (#1)
content:
אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר אֶ֖לֶף וּ⁠שְׁבַ֣ע מֵא֑וֹת

"14,700"

Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [fourteen thousand seven hundred]

See: Numbers

title: Numbers 16:49 (#2)
content:
עַל־דְּבַר־קֹֽרַח

"on account of the matter of Korah"

The implication is that Korah and his followers had rebelled against Moses and Aaron, and God had killed them because of their rebellion. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because Korah and the people with him had rebelled]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 16:50 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הַ⁠מַּגֵּפָ֖ה נֶעֱצָֽרָה

"and the plague was restrained"

Here the word and introduces what happened immediately before Aaron returned to Moses. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [once the plague had been restrained] or [as soon as the plague was restrained]

See: Connecting Words and Phrases

title: Numbers 16:50 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠הַ⁠מַּגֵּפָ֖ה נֶעֱצָֽרָה

"and the plague was restrained"

See how you translated this clause in 16:48. Alternate translation: [and the plague stopped] or [and Yahweh restrained the plague]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers - Chapter 17 Introduction
content:
Numbers 17 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

In this chapter, Moses places 13 staffs representing the leaders of the Israelite tribes before Yahweh. Yahweh makes Aaron’s staff blossom and produce nuts, showing that Aaron is the one chosen to be priest. The Israelites then exclaim that they expect to die if they are close to the sacred tent.

  1. Yahweh commands each tribal leader to provide a staff (1–7)
  2. Aaron’s staff produces buds, blossoms, and almonds (8–11)
  3. The people express fear of dying near the tabernacle (12–13)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

The staffs

Yahweh instructs Moses to place 12 staffs in the sacred tent. These staffs represented the leaders of each of the Israelite tribes. That is why each staff had the name of a leader written on it. Yahweh used the staffs to show the Israelites which leader he had chosen to be priest.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

How many staffs?

It is clear that Moses placed 12 staffs in the sacred tent, one for the leader of each tribe. It is less clear whether the staff with Aaron’s name on it was one of the 12 staffs or an additional 13th staff. It is most plausible that it was an additional 13th staff, so the notes and UST follow that interpretation.

“House of the fathers”

In this chapter, the phrase “house of the fathers” refers to an entire tribe, as is made clear by the number of staffs: 12. This is different than what the phrase means in Numbers 1–4, where it refers to the largest divisions of each tribe. The phrase is flexible and refers to a group of people who are related through a specific ancestor. The specific ancestor is defined by the context. So, you do not need to translate the phrase the same way you did in Numbers 1–4.

title: Numbers 17:1 (#1)
content:
לֵּ⁠אמֹֽר

"saying"

Here, the word saying introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated saying in 1:1.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 17:2 (#1)
content:
בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל

"the sons of Israel"

Here, the sons of Israel represents the people or descendants of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 17:2 (#2)
content:
מַטֶּ֣ה מַטֶּה֩ לְ⁠בֵ֨ית אָ֜ב מֵ⁠אֵ֤ת כָּל־נְשִֽׂיאֵ⁠הֶם֙ לְ⁠בֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֔⁠ם שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר מַטּ֑וֹת

"a staff, a staff for a house of a father, from with all their leaders for the house of their fathers, 12 staffs"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about how many staffs there were before the information about whom the staffs represented. You may also be able to combine or shorten some of the phrases. Alternate translation: [12 staffs, one for each of the leaders for the house of each of their fathers]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 17:2 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠בֵ֨ית אָ֜ב & לְ⁠בֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֔⁠ם

"for a house of a father & for the house of their fathers"

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrases house of a father and house of their fathers refer to whole tribes. This is unlike Numbers 3–4, where the phrases refer to the largest divisions within each tribe. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could make that idea more explicit. Alternate translation: [for an ancestral tribe … for each of their ancestral tribes]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:2 (#4)
content:
אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־שְׁמ֔⁠וֹ תִּכְתֹּ֖ב עַל־מַטֵּֽ⁠הוּ

"A man, his name you shall write on his staff"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about writing before the information about each man’s name. Alternate translation: [You shall write each man’s name on his staff]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 17:3 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אֵת֙ שֵׁ֣ם אַהֲרֹ֔ן תִּכְתֹּ֖ב עַל־מַטֵּ֣ה לֵוִ֑י כִּ֚י מַטֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד לְ⁠רֹ֖אשׁ בֵּ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽ⁠ם

"And the name of Aaron you shall write on the staff of Levi, for one staff {is} for the head of the house of their fathers"

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And because one staff is for the head of the house of their fathers, the name of Aaron you shall write on the staff of Levi]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 17:3 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠אֵת֙ שֵׁ֣ם אַהֲרֹ֔ן תִּכְתֹּ֖ב

"And the name of Aaron you shall write"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about writing before the information about the name of Aaron. Alternate translation: [And you shall write the name of Aaron]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 17:3 (#3)
content:
מַטֵּ֣ה לֵוִ֑י

"the staff of Levi"

By the staff of Levi, Yahweh means another staff in addition to the twelve from the previous verse. See the chapter introduction for more information. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on another staff, the staff of Levi]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 17:3 (#4)
content:
מַטֵּ֣ה לֵוִ֑י

"the staff of Levi"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a staff that is characterized by representing the tribe of Levi. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the staff that represents Levi]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 17:3 (#5)
content:
לְ⁠רֹ֖אשׁ

"is} for the head of"

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the leader of a tribe were the head of a body. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is for the leader of]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 17:3 (#6)
content:
בֵּ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽ⁠ם

"the house of their fathers"

See how you translated this phrase in verse 2. Alternate translation: [each ancestral tribe]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:4 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ הָֽ⁠עֵד֔וּת

"to the face of the Testimony"

Here, face represents the area in front of the Testimony. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before the Testimony]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 17:4 (#2)
content:
הָֽ⁠עֵד֔וּת

"the Testimony"

Here, the Testimony means the Ten Commandments, and here it refers to the box or chest that contained the Ten Commandments. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the box that contained the Testimony] or [the box with the Ten Commandments in it]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 17:4 (#3)
content:
אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִוָּעֵ֥ד לָ⁠כֶ֖ם שָֽׁמָּ⁠ה

"where I congregate with you there"

Here, the pronoun you is plural and refers to Moses and the representatives of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [where I meet with all of you there]

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 17:5 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠הֲשִׁכֹּתִ֣י מֵֽ⁠עָלַ֗⁠י אֶת־תְּלֻנּוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל

"And I will cause to subside from upon me the murmurings of the sons of Israel"

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the murmurings of the Israelites were a physical burden resting upon him. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will end the murmurings of the sons of Israel that trouble me]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 17:5 (#2)
content:
וַ⁠הֲשִׁכֹּתִ֣י

"And I will cause to subside"

The word translated as And indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, I will cause to subside]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 17:5 (#3)
content:
אֶת־תְּלֻנּוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם מַלִּינִ֖ם עֲלֵי⁠כֶֽם

"the murmurings of the sons of Israel, which they are murmuring against you"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [the murmurings of the sons of Israel against you] or [how the sons of Israel murmur against you]

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 17:5 (#4)
content:
עֲלֵי⁠כֶֽם

"against you"

Here, the pronoun you is plural and refers to Moses and Aaron. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [against the two of you]

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 17:6 (#1)
content:
מַטֶּה֩ לְ⁠נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד מַטֶּ֨ה לְ⁠נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙

"a staff for one leader, a staff for one leader"

Here, the author repeats the phrase a staff for one leader to indicate that each leader gave one staff. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [one staff from each of them]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:6 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠בֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֔⁠ם

"for the house of their fathers"

See how you translated the similar expression in 17:2.

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:6 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠מַטֵּ֥ה אַהֲרֹ֖ן בְּ⁠ת֥וֹךְ מַטּוֹתָֽ⁠ם

"And the staff of Aaron {was} in the midst of their staffs"

Here the author implies that the staff of Aaron was an additional staff added to the 12 staffs from the other leaders. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the staff of Aaron was placed among the other 12 staffs]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 17:7 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, face represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 17:7 (#2)
content:
בְּ⁠אֹ֖הֶל הָ⁠עֵדֻֽת

"in the tent of the Testimony"

The author is using the possessive form to describe the tent that contained the Testimony, which is the Ten Commandments. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in the tent that contained the Testimony] or [in the tent in which were the Ten Commandments]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 17:8 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יְהִ֣י

"And it happened"

The author is using the word translated as it happened to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

See: Introduction of a New Event

title: Numbers 17:8 (#2)
content:
מִֽ⁠מָּחֳרָ֗ת

"from the next day"

The author is using from the next day as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the day after.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on the day after]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:8 (#3)
content:
אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל הָ⁠עֵד֔וּת

"to the tent of the Testimony"

See how you translated this phrase in verse 7.

See: Possession

title: Numbers 17:8 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠הִנֵּ֛ה & מַטֵּֽה־אַהֲרֹ֖ן

"and behold, the staff of Aaron"

The author is using behold as a common expression of the culture to mean “pay attention to what follows.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he saw that the staff of Aaron]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:8 (#5)
content:
מַטֵּֽה־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לְ⁠בֵ֣ית לֵוִ֑י

"the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi"

The author is not distinguishing this staff of Aaron from another staff of Aaron that is not for the house of Levi. The author is reminding readers which tribal staff was Aaron’s. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [the staff that represented the house of Levi, which was Aaron’s staff,]

See: Distinguishing Versus Informing or Reminding

title: Numbers 17:8 (#6)
content:
פָּרַ֥ח & וַ⁠יֹּ֤צֵֽא פֶ֨רַח֙ וַ⁠יָּ֣צֵֽץ צִ֔יץ וַ⁠יִּגְמֹ֖ל שְׁקֵדִֽים

"had sprouted. And it brought out a blossom and it blossomed a flower, and it ripened almonds"

Here, the author could be indicating that all these stages of growth: (1) had happened during the night, and Moses saw the final result: the almonds. Alternate translation: [had sprouted, brought out a blossom, blossomed a flower, and finally ripened almonds]; or (2) were present at one time when Moses saw it. Alternate translation: [was sprouting, bringing out a blossom, blossoming a flower, and ripening almonds almost all at once]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 17:8 (#7)
content:
פֶ֨רַח֙ & צִ֔יץ

"a blossom & a flower"

In this verse, the words blossom and flower are singular in form, but they refer to several blossoms and flowers as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural forms of these words. Alternate translation: [blossoms … flowers]

See: Collective Nouns

title: Numbers 17:8 (#8)
content:
שְׁקֵדִֽים

"almonds"

The author implies that these almonds, a kind of nut, were fully ripe. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [almonds to full ripeness]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 17:9 (#1)
content:
מִ⁠לִּ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה

"from to the face of Yahweh"

Here, face represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from before Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 17:9 (#2)
content:
וַ⁠יִּרְא֥וּ וַ⁠יִּקְח֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מַטֵּֽ⁠הוּ

"And they saw, and they took, a man his staff"

The author is using a man his staff as a common expression of the culture to mean that each man saw and took his own staff. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And each one saw and then took his own staff]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:10 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י הָ⁠עֵד֔וּת

"to the face of the Testimony"

See how you translated the similar expression in 17:4.

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 17:10 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת

"for keeping"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of keeping, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be kept]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 17:10 (#3)
content:
לִ⁠בְנֵי־מֶ֑רִי

"for the sons of rebellion"

Yahweh is using the sons of rebellion as a common expression of the culture to mean “the people who rebel.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for the people who rebel]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 17:10 (#4)
content:
לִ⁠בְנֵי־מֶ֑רִי

"for the sons of rebellion"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of rebellion, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the rebellious sons]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 17:10 (#5)
content:
וּ⁠תְכַ֧ל תְּלוּנֹּתָ֛⁠ם מֵ⁠עָלַ֖⁠י

"And you shall finish their murmurings from upon me"

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the murmurings of the Israelites were a physical burden resting upon him. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in verse 5. Alternate translation: [And you shall end their murmuring against me]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 17:10 (#6)
content:
תְּלוּנֹּתָ֛⁠ם

"their murmurings"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of murmurings, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the words they murmur]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 17:10 (#7)
content:
וְ⁠לֹ֥א יָמֻֽתוּ

"and they shall not die"

Here, and marks they shall not die as the goal or purpose of you shall finish their murmurings from upon me. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [and that way, they shall not die]

See: Connect — Goal (Purpose) Relationship

title: Numbers 17:11 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יַּ֖עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֑ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹת֖⁠וֹ כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה

"And Moses did. Just as Yahweh had commanded him, thus he did"

It might seem that the expression thus he did contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [And Moses did just as Yahweh had commanded him]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 17:12 (#1)
content:
הֵ֥ן

"Behold"

The Israelites are using the word Behold to express a strong feeling of alarm and despair. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. If not, you could say what the Israelites were feeling, or you could say what made them afraid. Alternate translation: [Alas]

See: Exclamations

title: Numbers 17:12 (#2)
content:
גָּוַ֛עְנוּ אָבַ֖דְנוּ כֻּלָּ֥⁠נוּ אָבָֽדְנוּ

"we expire! We perish; all of us perish"

The Israelites say we expire! We perish; all of us perish as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [we are like those who expire! It is as if we perish, as if all of us perish]

See: Hyperbole

title: Numbers 17:12 (#3)
content:
גָּוַ֛עְנוּ אָבַ֖דְנוּ כֻּלָּ֥⁠נוּ אָבָֽדְנוּ

"we expire! We perish; all of us perish"

These three phrases we expire, We perish, and all of us perish mean basically the same thing. The repetition emphasizes the meaning by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [We are all going to die!]

See: Parallelism

title: Numbers 17:13 (#1)
content:
כֹּ֣ל הַ⁠קָּרֵ֧ב ׀ הַ⁠קָּרֵ֛ב אֶל־מִשְׁכַּ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה יָמ֑וּת

title: Numbers - Chapter 18 Introduction
content:
Numbers 18 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter includes instructions about how the Levites and the priests serve at the sacred tent. It also includes regulations about which sacred things belong to the priests and to the Levites. It concludes with the requirement that the Levites give a tithe to the priests.

  1. Yahweh assigns duties to the priests and Levites (1–7)
  2. Yahweh gives portions of Israel’s offerings to the priests (8–20)
  3. Yahweh gives Israel’s tithes to the Levites for their service (21–24)
  4. Yahweh commands the Levites to give a tenth of their tithes to the priests (25–32)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Priests and Levites

This chapter indicates that the Levites and the priests are responsible for making sure that no one defiles any of the holy things or places. The priests are responsible especially for the sacred tent and for who acts as a priest. The Levites are responsible for making sure that no one comes near the sacred tent, especially when they are setting it up, taking it down, and moving it. This chapter also makes it clear that the Levites are under the direction of the priests.

Contributions for the priests

In 18:8–19, Yahweh outlines the contributions from the Israelites that go directly to the priests. These include parts of the grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering that the priests do not burn. These also include the firstfruits of crops and the firstborn male animals and humans. In the case of humans and clean animals, however, the priests receive money instead of the human or animal. All these contributions are very holy, so Yahweh gives them to the priests specifically.

Contributions for the Levites

In 18:20–24, Yahweh outlines the contributions from the Israelites that go directly to the Levites. The tithes are made up of one-tenth of all the produce and animals that Israelites have grown or raised. The Israelites give these tithes to Yahweh, and Yahweh gives them to the Levites instead of land.

Tithes from the Levites

In 18:25–32, Yahweh indicates that the Levites also must give tithes. They tithe directly to the priests. Once the Levites have given their tithes, they can use the rest of what they receive from the Israelites as regular food. It is not considered sacred any longer.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

“Keeping” and “service”

As in Numbers 3–4, the word “keeping” refers to keeping watch or guarding. No one else was supposed to approach the sacred items, so the Levites were required to guard these items, especially when they were transporting them. The word “service” refers to physical labor, particularly taking down and setting up the sacred tent and the items that were in it. The Levites were also responsible for these tasks. See how you translated “keeping” and “service” in Numbers 3–4.

Singular and plural “you”

In 18:1–7, both singular and plural “you” appear in many verses. See the notes on those verses for details. In 18:8–20, Yahweh only uses the singular “you,” since he is addressing Aaron. In 18:21–32, every “you” is plural except the occurrences in 18:26, 30 where Yahweh tells Moses to speak.

Quotes in quotes

In 18:25–32, there are quotes inside quotes. Consider how your language indicates that a quote contains a quote. The UST models how to express the idea with only one level of quotation.

title: Numbers 18:1 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן

"And Yahweh said to Aaron"

The phrase And Yahweh said to Aaron introduces a direct quotation. Use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 18:1 (#2)
content:
אַתָּ֗ה וּ⁠בָנֶ֤י⁠ךָ וּ⁠בֵית־אָבִ֨י⁠ךָ֙ אִתָּ֔⁠ךְ תִּשְׂא֖וּ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן הַ⁠מִּקְדָּ֑שׁ וְ⁠אַתָּה֙ וּ⁠בָנֶ֣י⁠ךָ אִתָּ֔⁠ךְ

"You and your sons and the house of your father with you shall lift up the iniquity of the holy place, and you and your sons with you"

Here, you is singular. It refers to Aaron, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 18:1 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠בֵית־אָבִ֨י⁠ךָ֙

"and the house of your father"

The phrase house of your father could refer to: (1) the clan of Kohath, one of the three major clans within the tribe of Levi. Aaron belonged to this clan. This is how the phrase “house of a father” is used in Numbers 3–4. Alternate translation: [and your ancestral family, the Kohathites,]; or (2) the tribe of Levi as a whole. This is how the phrase “house of a father” is used in Numbers 17. Alternate translation: [and your tribe, the Levites,]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 18:1 (#4)
content:
תִּשְׂא֖וּ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן הַ⁠מִּקְדָּ֑שׁ

"shall lift up the iniquity of the holy place"

Yahweh is using shall lift up the iniquity of the holy place as a common expression of the culture to mean “shall be responsible for any offenses against the holy place.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shall be responsible for any offenses against the holy place]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 18:1 (#5)

title: Numbers 18:1 (#6)

הַ⁠מִּקְדָּ֑שׁ

"the holy place"

The phrase the holy place could refer to: (1) the sacred objects that were inside the holy place. This is what the phrase means in 10:21. Alternate translation: [the things that belong in the holy place]; or (2) the sacred tent itself. This is what the phrase means in 3:38. Alternate translation: [the sacred tent]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 18:2 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠גַ֣ם אֶת־אַחֶי⁠ךָ֩ מַטֵּ֨ה לֵוִ֜י שֵׁ֤בֶט אָבִ֨י⁠ךָ֙ הַקְרֵ֣ב אִתָּ֔⁠ךְ וְ⁠יִלָּו֥וּ עָלֶ֖י⁠ךָ וִֽ⁠ישָׁרְת֑וּ⁠ךָ וְ⁠אַתָּה֙ וּ⁠בָנֶ֣י⁠ךָ אִתָּ֔⁠ךְ לִ⁠פְנֵ֖י אֹ֥הֶל הָ⁠עֵדֻֽת

title: Numbers 18:2 (#2)

וְ⁠יִלָּו֥וּ עָלֶ֖י⁠ךָ

"and they shall be joined to you"

title: Numbers 18:3 (#1)

content:
כָּל־קָ֠רְבָּנָ⁠ם לְֽ⁠כָל־מִנְחָתָ֞⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠כָל־חַטָּאתָ֗⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠כָל־אֲשָׁמָ⁠ם֙

title: Numbers 18:10 (#1)
content:
בְּ⁠קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַ⁠קֳּדָשִׁ֖ים

"In the holy of holies"

Here, the phrase In the holy of holies could indicate: (1) the area in which the priests should eat. This cannot be the Most Holy Place, since the high priest only entered that place once a year. Most likely, it refer to any area within the tabernacle and its courtyard. Alternate translation: [In a very holy place] or [Within the tabernacle area]; or (2) the manner in which the priests should eat. In other words, they treat it as holy while they eat it. Alternate translation: [In a very holy way] or [As a very holy thing]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 18:10 (#2)

title: Numbers 18:10 (#3)

If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express the value of five shekels of silver in modern terms. A shekel weighed about 11 grams, so five shekels would be about 55 grams of silver.

title: Numbers 18:16 (#5)

The shekel of the holy place is a standard unit of weight used by the priests for official measurements. If your readers would not be familiar with what a shekel of the holy place is, you could use the name of a similar standard that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express the value of 20 gerahs in modern terms. A gerah was a small unit of weight, and 20 gerahs equaled one shekel, which weighed about 11 grams.

title: Numbers 18:16 (#7)

title: Numbers 18:20 (#4)

If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am what you will possess and what you will inherit]

title: Numbers 18:21 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י לֵוִ֔י הִנֵּ֥ה נָתַ֛תִּי כָּל־מַֽעֲשֵׂ֥ר בְּ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְ⁠נַחֲלָ֑ה חֵ֤לֶף עֲבֹֽדָתָ⁠ם֙ אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣ם עֹֽבְדִ֔ים אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד

"And to the sons of Levi, behold, I have given every tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in exchange for their service which they are serving, the service of the tent of meeting"

The phrase translated as in exchange for indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [And to the sons of Levi, behold, I have given every tithe in Israel for an inheritance, because of the service they are serving, the service of the tent of meeting]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [And the sons of Israel shall not again come near to the tent of meeting to lift up sin, or they will die]

title: Numbers 18:23 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הֵ֖ם יִשְׂא֣וּ עֲוֺנָ֑⁠ם

"and they shall bear their iniquity"

Here, the pronoun they refers to the Levites. The pronoun their could refer to: (1) the Levites again. In this case, the Levites are responsible for their own sins concerning the holy things. Alternate translation: [and the Levites shall bear their own iniquity]; or (2) the Israelites in general. In this case, the Levites are responsible for any sins concerning the holy things. Alternate translation: [and the Levites shall the iniquity of any Israelite]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 18:23 (#2)
content:

title: Numbers - Chapter 19 Introduction
content:
Numbers 19 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter explains how people can become clean after contact with a dead person. The ashes of a red cow are mixed with water and used in the cleansing ceremony.

  1. Yahweh gives instructions for preparing the ashes of a red cow (1–10)
  2. Yahweh explains how to cleanse people and objects made unclean by contact with the dead (11–22)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Impurity from dead bodies

This chapter explains how dead bodies, including a burial site or even a bone from a body, make people impure. This impurity must be removed quickly. If people come in direct contact with a dead body, they must participate in this specific ritual twice over seven days. Even the person who helps them become pure is unclean until that evening. This chapter indicates how dangerous this kind of impurity is and how the Israelites must remove it.

Defiling the sacred tent

Because impurity from a dead body is so dangerous, Yahweh requires every Israelite who becomes impure in this way to cleanse themselves immediately. If anyone does not do this, their impurity makes the sacred tent impure, even if they do not visit the sacred tent. Making the sacred tent impure is a very serious crime that Yahweh will punish.

Priest or clean person

This chapter requires a priest to preside when someone burns the cow to create ashes. However, any clean person can apply the water and ashes to the people who are impure. It does not have to be a priest. In fact, because that clean person becomes unclean when he or she applies the water and ashes, it probably would not have been a priest.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

Being “cut off” from the people

The punishment for failing to purify oneself from impurity caused by a dead body was being “cut off” from the rest of the Israelites. Scholars are unsure exactly what penalty this phrase implies. It could refer to death by execution. It could refer to punishment from Yahweh in a way of his choice. It could refer to expulsion from the Israelite community. The UST and notes follow this last option. If possible, use a word or phrase that could be understood in several of these ways. If you must specify, it is recommended that you follow the UST and notes.

title: Numbers 19:10 (#1)
content:
הָ⁠אֹסֵ֨ף אֶת־אֵ֤פֶר הַ⁠פָּרָה֙

"the one gathering the ashes of the cow"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific person by the phrase the one gathering the ashes of the cow. He means anyone who gathers the ashes. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [anyone who gathers the ashes of the cow]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 19:10 (#2)
content:
לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל

"for the sons of Israel"

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the Israelites were literally the sons of the patriarch Israel. He means that they are his descendants. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for the descendants of Israel]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 19:10 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠לַ⁠גֵּ֛ר הַ⁠גָּ֥ר בְּ⁠תוֹכָ֖⁠ם

"and for the sojourner, the one sojourning in their midst"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific sojourner. He means any foreigner who lives among the Israelites. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and for any foreigner who lives among them]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 19:10 (#4)
content:
לְ⁠חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם

"for a statute of eternity"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a statute that is characterized by eternity. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for a statute that lasts forever]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 19:11 (#1)
content:
The ideas of “clean” and “purify” represent being acceptable to God. The ideas of “unclean,” “defile,” “impurity,” and “uncleanness” represent not being acceptable to God.

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 19:11 (#2)
content:
בְּ⁠מֵ֖ת לְ⁠כָל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֑ם

"a dying one for every person of a man"

Alternate translation: [the dead body of any person]

title: Numbers 19:12 (#1)
content:
ה֣וּא יִתְחַטָּא־ב֞⁠וֹ בַּ⁠יּ֧וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י יִטְהָ֑ר וְ⁠אִם־לֹ֨א יִתְחַטָּ֜א בַּ⁠יּ֧וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י לֹ֥א יִטְהָֽר

"He shall purify himself with it on the third day and on the seventh day. He will be clean. And if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean"

Here, the phrase on the seventh day in both places could go with: (1) purify himself. In this case, the purification should happen twice, on day three and on day seven. Alternate translation: [He shall purify himself with it two times, on the third day and on the seventh day. Then he will be clean. And if he does not purify himself two times, on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean]; or (2) be clean. In this case, the purification happens once, on day three, and the person is clean on day seven. Alternate translation: [He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he will be clean. And if he does not purify himself on the third day, then on the seventh day he will not be clean]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 19:12 (#2)
content:
ה֣וּא יִתְחַטָּא־ב֞⁠וֹ בַּ⁠יּ֧וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י יִטְהָ֑ר וְ⁠אִם־לֹ֨א יִתְחַטָּ֜א בַּ⁠יּ֧וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י לֹ֥א יִטְהָֽר

"He shall purify himself with it on the third day and on the seventh day. He will be clean. And if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean"

Yahweh uses the word if here to indicate a contrast between the positive result of purification and the negative result of failing to purify. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [He shall purify himself with it on the third day and on the seventh day, and he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.]

See: Connect — Contrast Relationship

title: Numbers 19:12 (#3)
content:
ה֣וּא יִתְחַטָּא־ב֞⁠וֹ

"He shall purify himself with it"

The pronoun He refers to the person who touched a dead body, and the pronoun it refers to the purification water. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [He shall purify himself with the purification water]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 19:13 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נִכְרְתָ֛ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִ֖וא מִ⁠יִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל

"And that person shall be cut off from Israel"

The expression shall be cut off from Israel is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the rest of the Israelites. Alternate translation: [the Israelites shall drive that person out from among them]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 19:13 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠נִכְרְתָ֛ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִ֖וא מִ⁠יִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל

"And that person shall be cut off from Israel"

Yahweh is speaking as if the person being expelled from the community were being physically cut off. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And that person shall be expelled from Israel]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 19:13 (#3)
content:
מֵ֨י נִדָּ֜ה לֹא־זֹרַ֤ק עָלָי⁠ו֙

"water of impurity was not splashed on him"

The expression was not sprinkled on him is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one sprinkled the water of impurity on him]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 19:13 (#4)
content:
כִּי֩ מֵ֨י נִדָּ֜ה לֹא־זֹרַ֤ק עָלָי⁠ו֙

"for water of impurity was not splashed on him"

The word translated as for indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because the water of impurity was not splashed on him]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 19:13 (#5)
content:
ע֖וֹד טֻמְאָת֥⁠וֹ בֽ⁠וֹ

"his uncleanness {is} still on him"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of uncleanness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he has not yet become clean]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 19:13 (#6)
content:
מֵ֨י נִדָּ֜ה

"water of impurity"

See how you translated this phrase in 19:9.

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 19:14 (#1)
content:
אָדָ֖ם כִּֽי־יָמ֣וּת בְּ⁠אֹ֑הֶל

"a man, when he dies in a tent"

Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that a man dies in a tent, and everyone who comes to the tent or is in the tent will be unclean. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [if a man dies in a tent]

See: Connect — Hypothetical Conditions

title: Numbers 19:15 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠כֹל֙ כְּלִ֣י פָת֔וּחַ

"And every opened vessel"

The expression opened is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And every vessel that is open]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 19:15 (#2)
content:
צָמִ֥יד פָּתִ֖יל

"cover of cord"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a cover that is characterized by cord. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [cover tied with cord]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 19:16 (#1)
content:
פְּנֵ֣י הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֗ה

"the face of the field"

Here, the face of the field represents “the surface of the open land.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the surface of the open land]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 19:16 (#2)
content:
בַּֽ⁠חֲלַל־חֶ֨רֶב֙

"a slain one of the sword"

Here, sword represents “the means by which someone was killed.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [one who was killed]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 19:17 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠לָֽקְחוּ֙

"And they shall take"

The pronoun they refers to people in general, not to specific individuals. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And someone shall take]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 19:17 (#2)
content:
לַ⁠טָּמֵ֔א

"for the unclean one"

Yahweh is using the adjective unclean as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [for the person who is unclean]

See: Nominal Adjectives

title: Numbers 19:17 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נָתַ֥ן עָלָ֛י⁠ו מַ֥יִם חַיִּ֖ים

"and he shall put living water on it"

The pronoun he refers to the person preparing the purification water, and the pronoun it refers to the dust of the sin offering. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and that person shall put living water on the dust]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 19:17 (#4)
content:
מַ֥יִם חַיִּ֖ים

"living water"

Yahweh is using living water as a common expression of the culture to mean “flowing, fresh water.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [flowing water]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 19:18 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִזָּ֤ה עַל־הָ⁠אֹ֨הֶל֙

"and he shall sprinkle on the tent"

The pronoun he refers to the clean man who will perform the sprinkling. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the clean man shall sprinkle on the tent]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 19:18 (#2)
content:
אֵז֜וֹב

"hyssop"

A hyssop is a kind of small, bushy plant. If your readers would not be familiar with what hyssop is, you could use the name of a similar plant that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a small, bushy plant]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 19:19 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הִזָּ֤ה הַ⁠טָּהֹר֙ עַל־הַ⁠טָּמֵ֔א

"And the clean one shall sprinkle on the unclean one"

Yahweh is using the adjectives clean and unclean as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [And the clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean person]

See: Nominal Adjectives

title: Numbers 19:19 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠כִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛י⁠ו וְ⁠רָחַ֥ץ בַּ⁠מַּ֖יִם

"and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in the water"

The pronoun he refers to the person who was purified, not to the one who performed the sprinkling. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the unclean person shall wash his clothes and bathe in the water]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 19:19 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠חִטְּא⁠וֹ֙

"And he shall purify him"

Here, the pronoun him refers to the unclean one. The pronoun he could refer to: (1) the clean one. In this case, the phrase refers to the clean person sprinkling the water on the unclean person. Alternate translation: [And the clean one shall purify the unclean one]; or (2) the unclean one. In this case, the phrase indicates that the unclean person must successfully complete the ritual to become clean. Alternate translation: [And the unclean one shall purify himself]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 19:20 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נִכְרְתָ֛ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִ֖וא מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ הַ⁠קָּהָ֑ל

"that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly"

The expression shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the rest of the Israelites. Alternate translation: [the rest of the Israelites shall drive that person out from the midst of the assembly]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 19:20 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠נִכְרְתָ֛ה & מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ הַ⁠קָּהָ֑ל

"shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly"

Yahweh is speaking as if the person being expelled from the community were being physically cut off. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shall be expelled from the assembly]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 19:20 (#3)
content:
מֵ֥י נִדָּ֛ה לֹא־זֹרַ֥ק עָלָ֖י⁠ו

"Water of impurity was not splashed on him"

See how you translated the similar expression in 19:13. The expression was not splashed on him is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one splashed the water of impurity on him]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 19:20 (#4)
content:
מֵ֥י נִדָּ֛ה

"Water of impurity"

See how you translated the similar expression in 19:13. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of impurity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Water that makes people clean]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 19:20 (#5)
content:
וְ⁠אִ֤ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִטְמָא֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יִתְחַטָּ֔א וְ⁠נִכְרְתָ֛ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִ֖וא מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ הַ⁠קָּהָ֑ל כִּי֩ אֶת־מִקְדַּ֨שׁ יְהוָ֜ה טִמֵּ֗א מֵ֥י נִדָּ֛ה לֹא־זֹרַ֥ק עָלָ֖י⁠ו טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא

"And a man who is unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, for he has made the holy place of Yahweh unclean. Water of impurity was not splashed on him; he {is} unclean"

The word translated as for indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because he has made the holy place of Yahweh unclean]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 19:21 (#1)
content:
לְ⁠חֻקַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם

"for a statute of eternity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of eternity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for a statute that lasts forever]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 19:21 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠חֻקַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם

"for a statute of eternity"

Yahweh is using a statute of eternity as a common expression of the culture to mean “a permanent rule.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for a lasting regulation]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 19:21 (#3)
content:
מֵֽי־הַ⁠נִּדָּה֙

"the water of the impurity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of impurity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the water used to cleanse the unclean]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 19:22 (#1)
content:
הַ⁠טָּמֵ֖א

"the unclean one"

See how you translated the similar expression in 19:17. Moses is using the adjective unclean as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the person who is unclean]

See: Nominal Adjectives

title: Numbers 19:22 (#2)
content:
הַ⁠נֹּגַ֖עַת

"touching"

Here, Yahweh could be referring to touching: (1) any object that the unclean person has touched. Alternate translation: [touching something that the unclean one has touched]; or (2) the unclean person. Alternate translation: [touching the unclean one]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers - Chapter 20 Introduction
content:
Numbers 20 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter describes the deaths of Miriam and Aaron. It also tells how Moses and Aaron disobey Yahweh when the people need water. Yahweh declares that they will not lead Israel into the Promised Land.

  1. Miriam dies and is buried at Kadesh (1)
  2. Yahweh provides water from a rock, but Moses and Aaron disobey him (2–13)
  3. Edom refuses to let Israel travel through its land (14–21)
  4. Aaron dies, and Eleazar takes his place as high priest (22–29)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

What Moses and Aaron did wrong

In 20:12, Yahweh condemns Moses and Aaron for doing something wrong when they provided water for the people. However, Yahweh does not specify exactly which action was wrong, and scholars debate what it was. Yahweh told Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses also struck it twice with a staff. That may have been what he did wrong. Moses also spoke to the people as if he and Aaron were the ones providing the water. This may have implied that it was them instead of Yahweh. That may have been what he did wrong. Since the text does not make it explicit, it is recommended that you do not state exactly which action was wrong in your translation.

Transferring clothing

In 20:26–28, Moses must take Aaron’s clothing off and put it on his son Eleazar. This clothing was specifically the clothing that Aaron wore when he did his work as high priest. Moses only removed Aaron’s outer garments. He did not make Aaron completely naked. When Moses transferred the high priest clothing from Aaron to Eleazar, it symbolized that Eleazar was now high priest.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

Personifying people groups

In 20:14–21, both the messengers and the narrator often speak of the Israelites and the Edomites as if each group were one person. They use the first or third person singular for the entire group, but sometimes they also use plural forms. This alternation between singular and plural was natural in their culture. The UST models how to translate the verses using only plural forms, without the figure of speech.

title: Numbers 20:1 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יָּבֹ֣אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּל־הָ֨⁠עֵדָ֤ה מִדְבַּר־צִן֙ בַּ⁠חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽ⁠רִאשׁ֔וֹן
