"the land shall be divided"

The expression shall be divided is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall divide the land]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:53 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠נַחֲלָ֖ה

"in an inheritance"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of inheritance, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that they may inherit it]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 26:53 (#4)
content:
בְּ⁠מִסְפַּ֥ר שֵׁמֽוֹת

"by the number of the names"

Here, the names represents “the people whom Moses and Eleazar counted.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by the number of the people who were counted]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 26:54 (#1)
content:
נַחֲלָת֔⁠וֹ & נַחֲלָת֑⁠וֹ

"its inheritance & its inheritance"

Here, Yahweh could be speaking about: (1) the clans of the Israelites that were listed earlier. Alternate translation: [that clan’s inheritance … that clan’s inheritance]; or (2) the tribes of the Israelites that were listed earlier. Alternate translation: [that tribe’s inheritance … that tribe’s inheritance]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 26:54 (#2)
content:
לָ⁠רַ֗ב תַּרְבֶּה֙ נַחֲלָת֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠לַ⁠מְעַ֕ט תַּמְעִ֖יט נַחֲלָת֑⁠וֹ

"For the many & its inheritance, and for the few & its inheritance"

Yahweh is using the adjectives many and few as nouns to mean certain kinds of groups. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [For the numerous tribes you shall increase its inheritance, and for the small tribes you shall decrease its inheritance]

See: Nominal Adjectives

title: Numbers 26:54 (#3)
content:
אִ֚ישׁ לְ⁠פִ֣י פְקֻדָ֔י⁠ו

"A man to the mouth of its counted ones"

Yahweh is not referring to a specific man. He means each of the tribes in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Each tribe to the mouth of its counted ones]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 26:54 (#4)
content:
לְ⁠פִ֣י פְקֻדָ֔י⁠ו

"to the mouth of its counted ones"

Yahweh is using to the mouth of as a common expression of the culture to mean “in proportion to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in proportion to the number of those counted for it]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 26:54 (#5)
content:
יֻתַּ֖ן נַחֲלָתֽ⁠וֹ

"its inheritance"

The expression shall be given is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall give its inheritance]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:55 (#1)
content:
אַךְ־בְּ⁠גוֹרָ֕ל יֵחָלֵ֖ק אֶת־הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ

"Only & shall the land be divided"

The implication is that Yahweh himself would decide by means of the lots how the land was to be divided among the tribes. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Only by lots, through which I myself will show my decision, shall the land be divided]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 26:55 (#2)
content:
יֵחָלֵ֖ק אֶת־הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ

"shall the land be divided"

The expression shall the land be divided is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [shall you divide the land]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:55 (#3)
content:
מַטּוֹת־אֲבֹתָ֖⁠ם

"the tribes of their fathers"

Yahweh is using the tribes of their fathers as a common expression of the culture to mean “the tribes that descended from their ancestors.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the tribes descended from their ancestors]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 26:56 (#1)
content:
עַל־פִּי֙ הַ⁠גּוֹרָ֔ל

"Upon the mouth of the lot"

Here, the mouth of the lot represents “the decision that the lot indicates.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [According to the decision that the lot indicates]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 26:56 (#2)
content:
תֵּחָלֵ֖ק נַחֲלָת֑⁠וֹ

"shall its inheritance be divided"

The expression shall its inheritance be divided is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall divide its inheritance]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:57 (#1)
content:
פְקוּדֵ֣י הַ⁠לֵּוִי֮

"were} the counted ones of the Levite"

The author is not referring to a specific Levite. He means Levites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the counted ones of the Levites]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 26:57 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠גֵרְשׁ֗וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת֙ הַ⁠גֵּ֣רְשֻׁנִּ֔י לִ⁠קְהָ֕ת מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֑י לִ⁠מְרָרִ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ⁠מְּרָרִֽי

"of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonite; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathite; of Merari, the clan of the Merarite"

The words Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are the names of men, and Gershonite, Kohathite, and Merarite are the names of the clans that descended from them.

See: How to Translate Names

title: Numbers 26:58 (#1)
content:
הַ⁠לִּבְנִ֜י & הַֽ⁠חֶבְרֹנִי֙ מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַ⁠מַּחְלִי֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַ⁠מּוּשִׁ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ⁠קָּרְחִ֑י

"the Libnite & the Hebronite, the clan of the Mahlite, the clan of the Mushite, the clan of the Korahite"

The implication is that each of these clans was named after an ancestor whom the author does not name here. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the clan descended from a man named Libni, the clan descended from a man named Hebron, the clan descended from a man named Mahli, the clan descended from a man named Mushi, the clan descended from a man named Korah]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 26:58 (#2)
content:
וּ⁠קְהָ֖ת הוֹלִ֥ד אֶת־עַמְרָֽם

"And Kohath fathered Amram"

Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

See: Background Information

title: Numbers 26:58 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠קְהָ֖ת הוֹלִ֥ד אֶת־עַמְרָֽם

"And Kohath fathered Amram"

This could mean: (1) that Kohath was an important ancestor of Amram. Alternate translation: [And Kohath was an ancestor of Amram]; or (2) that Kohath was Amram’s father directly. Alternate translation: [And Kohath was Amram’s father]

See: Kinship

title: Numbers 26:59 (#1)
content:
יוֹכֶ֨בֶד֙ בַּת־לֵוִ֔י

"was} Jochebed, a daughter of Levi"

The word Jochebed is the name of a woman.

See: How to Translate Names

title: Numbers 26:59 (#2)
content:
בַּת־לֵוִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֥ה אֹתָ֛⁠הּ לְ⁠לֵוִ֖י בְּ⁠מִצְרָ֑יִם

"a daughter of Levi, whom she bore to Levi in Egypt"

This could mean: (1) that Jochebed was a descendant of Levi. Alternate translation: [a Levite, whom her mother bore to a Levite man in Egypt]; or (2) that Jochebed was an immediate daughter to Levi. Alternate translation: [Levi’s daughter, whom her mother bore to Levi, her husband, in Egypt]

See: Kinship

title: Numbers 26:59 (#3)
content:
אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֥ה אֹתָ֛⁠הּ לְ⁠לֵוִ֖י בְּ⁠מִצְרָ֑יִם

"whom she bore to Levi in Egypt"

The pronoun she refers to the wife of Levi, whom the author does not name here. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [whom his wife bore to Levi in Egypt]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 26:59 (#4)
content:
וַ⁠תֵּ֣לֶד לְ⁠עַמְרָ֗ם

"And she bore to Amram"

The pronoun she refers here to Jochebed rather than to the wife of Levi. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Jochebed bore to Amram]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 26:59 (#5)
content:
וַ⁠תֵּ֣לֶד לְ⁠עַמְרָ֗ם אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְ⁠אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְ⁠אֵ֖ת מִרְיָ֥ם אֲחֹתָֽ⁠ם

"And she bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister before the information about to Amram. Alternate translation: [And she bore Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister to Amram]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 26:60 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יִּוָּלֵ֣ד לְ⁠אַהֲרֹ֔ן

"And were born to Aaron"

The expression were born is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And Aaron fathered]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:60 (#2)
content:
אֶת־נָדָ֖ב וְ⁠אֶת־אֲבִיה֑וּא אֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְ⁠אֶת־אִיתָמָֽר

"Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar"

The words Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar are the names of men.

See: How to Translate Names

title: Numbers 26:61 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠יָּ֥מָת נָדָ֖ב וַ⁠אֲבִיה֑וּא

"Nadab & and Abihu"

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And Nadab and Abihu died]

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 26:61 (#2)
content:
אֵשׁ־זָרָ֖ה

"strange fire"

The expression strange fire refers to a kind of burning coals that Yahweh had not authorized for use in his presence. If your readers would not be familiar with what strange fire is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [unauthorized fire]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 26:61 (#3)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

"to the face of Yahweh"

Here, the face of Yahweh represents “the presence of Yahweh.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 26:62 (#1)
content:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף

"23,000"

Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [twenty-three thousand]

See: Numbers

title: Numbers 26:62 (#2)
content:
כִּ֣י ׀ לֹ֣א הָתְפָּקְד֗וּ

"For they were not counted"

The word translated as For indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This was because they were not counted]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 26:62 (#3)
content:
לֹ֣א הָתְפָּקְד֗וּ

"they were not counted"

The expression they were not counted is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one counted them]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:62 (#4)
content:
לֹא־נִתַּ֤ן לָ⁠הֶם֙ נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּ⁠ת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

"an inheritance in the midst of the sons of Israel was not given to them"

The expression was not given is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh did not give them an inheritance in the midst of the sons of Israel]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:63 (#1)
content:
אֵ֚לֶּה פְּקוּדֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְ⁠אֶלְעָזָ֖ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֑ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּֽקְד֜וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ⁠עַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב עַ֖ל יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ

"and Eleazar & who & the sons of & Moab beside & at} Jericho"

This sentence is a comment about what happened after the story as a result of the events within the story itself. This signals the end of a story. Use the natural form in your language for expressing the conclusion of a story. Alternate translation: [So that is the record of all those whom Moses and Eleazar the priest counted when they counted the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan at Jericho]

See: End of Story

title: Numbers 26:63 (#2)
content:
פְּקוּדֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְ⁠אֶלְעָזָ֖ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֑ן

"and Eleazar"

Moses is using the possessive form the counted ones of Moses and Eleazar the priest to describe the people whom he and Eleazar the priest counted. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the people whom Moses and Eleazar the priest registered]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 26:64 (#1)
content:
לֹא־הָ֣יָה אִ֔ישׁ מִ⁠פְּקוּדֵ֣י

"there was not a man from the counted ones of"

The author is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, not, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [every single one was missing from the counted ones]

See: Litotes

title: Numbers 26:64 (#2)
content:
אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקְד֛וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּ⁠מִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי

"who counted the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai"

The implication is that this refers to the first census, which Moses and Aaron took in the wilderness of Sinai about 40 years earlier. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who had counted the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai 40 years earlier]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 26:65 (#1)
content:
כִּֽי־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָ⁠הֶ֔ם

"For Yahweh had said to them"

The word translated as For indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This was because Yahweh had said to them]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 26:65 (#2)
content:
מ֥וֹת יָמֻ֖תוּ בַּ⁠מִּדְבָּ֑ר

"Dying, they shall die in the wilderness"

The implication is that Yahweh had declared this when the Israelites refused to enter the land of Canaan, as an earlier chapter describes. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Dying, they shall die in the wilderness because they refused to enter the land of Canaan]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 26:65 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠לֹא־נוֹתַ֤ר מֵ⁠הֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֚י אִם־כָּלֵ֣ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֔ה וִ⁠יהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נֽוּן

"And a man was not left from them, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun"

If it would appear in your language that the author was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [And only Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun were left from them]

See: Connect — Exception Clauses

title: Numbers 26:65 (#4)
content:
וְ⁠לֹא־נוֹתַ֤ר מֵ⁠הֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ

"And a man was not left from them"

The expression was not left is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And not a man from them remained]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 26:65 (#5)
content:
בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֔ה וִ⁠יהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נֽוּן

"the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun"

The words Jephunneh and Nun are the names of men.

See: How to Translate Names

title: Numbers 26:65 (#6)
content:
מ֥וֹת יָמֻ֖תוּ

"Dying, they shall die"

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb die in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [They shall certainly die]

See: Reduplication

title: Numbers - Chapter 27 Introduction
content:
Numbers 27 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter explains how a man’s daughters can inherit his property if he has no sons. It also describes how Yahweh chooses Joshua to lead Israel after Moses.

  1. Zelophehad’s daughters ask to inherit their father’s property, and Yahweh gives a law about inheritance (1–11)
  2. Yahweh tells Moses that he will see the Promised Land but will not enter it (12–14)
  3. Moses asks for a new leader, and Yahweh chooses Joshua (15–23)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Children and inheritance

In this culture, when a father died, his sons usually inherited his land and property. This practice maintained land and property within one group that was descended from a single ancestor. In this chapter, the daughters of a man who had no sons make a request. They want to inherit their father’s land and property. That way, a portion of their tribe’s land will continue to belong to the descendants of their father, just like it will for their father’s brothers. Yahweh agrees that this is the right thing to do. Daughters should inherit their father’s land and property if there are no sons. Only if there are also no daughters should the land and property be inherited by other relatives, like brothers or uncles.

Commissioning Joshua

When Moses learns that he will soon die, he asks Yahweh to appoint a leader who will replace him. Yahweh tells Moses to commission Joshua. Joshua will only share some of Moses’ glory, and he will have to communicate with God through the high priest instead of directly. However, he will be the next leader of the Israelites. Moses signifies this by laying his hands on Joshua.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

When does the story in 27:12–23 happen?

The Hebrew conjunction that begins the story in 27:12 does not indicate that the events narrated in this story happened immediately after the events in the story in 27:1–11. These events may have happened before or after daughters of Zelophehad asked to inherit their father’s land. Consider how you might introduce the story in 27:12–23 in a way that does not indicate that the events narrated in it immediately follow the events narrated in the previous story.

title: Numbers 27:1 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠תִּקְרַ֜בְנָה בְּנ֣וֹת צְלָפְחָ֗ד בֶּן־חֵ֤פֶר בֶּן־גִּלְעָד֙ בֶּן־מָכִ֣יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בֶן־יוֹסֵ֑ף

"And the daughters of Zelophehad the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh the son of Joseph, came near"

Here the author is introducing the daughters of Zelophehad as new participants in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Now there was a man named Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and his daughters came near]

See: Introduction of New and Old Participants

resource.label: Introduction of New and Old Participants

title: Numbers 27:2 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֗ה וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֔ן וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵ֥י הַ⁠נְּשִׂיאִ֖ם

"to the face of Moses and to the face of Eleazar the priest and to the face of the leaders"

Here, the face of represents the presence of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the leaders]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 27:3 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠ה֨וּא לֹא־הָיָ֜ה בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ הָ⁠עֵדָ֗ה

"and he was not in the midst of the congregation"

The pronoun he refers to Zelophehad, the father of these women. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Zelophehad was not in the midst of the congregation]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 27:3 (#2)
content:
וּ⁠בָנִ֖ים לֹא־הָ֥יוּ לֽ⁠וֹ

"and sons were not for him"

The implication is that Zelophehad had no sons who could receive his property. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and he had no sons to inherit his property]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 27:4 (#1)
content:
לָ֣⁠מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם־אָבִ֨י⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔⁠וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ל֖⁠וֹ בֵּ֑ן

"Why should the name of our father be taken away from the midst of his clan because there is not for him a son"

The daughters of Zelophehad are using the question form to insist that it would be wrong for their father to be forgotten among his relatives just because he had no son. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [The name of our father should not be taken away from the midst of his clan just because there is not for him a son!]

See: Rhetorical Question

title: Numbers 27:4 (#2)
content:
לָ֣⁠מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם־אָבִ֨י⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔⁠וֹ

"Why should the name of our father be taken away from the midst of his clan"

The expression be taken away is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Why should the name of our father disappear from the midst of his clan]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 27:4 (#3)
content:
יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם־אָבִ֨י⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔⁠וֹ

"should the name of our father be taken away from the midst of his clan"

Here, the name of our father represents the memory of him and his continuing place among his relatives. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [should the memory of our father be lost from the midst of his clan]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 27:4 (#4)
content:
תְּנָ⁠ה־לָּ֣⁠נוּ אֲחֻזָּ֔ה

"Give to us a possession"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of a possession, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Give to us land that we may own]

content:
וַ⁠יַּקְרֵ֥ב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־מִשְׁפָּטָ֖ן

title: Numbers 27:7 (#2)
content:

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a possession that is characterized by an inheritance. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an inherited possession]

title: Numbers 27:8 (#1)
content:
אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי־יָמ֗וּת וּ⁠בֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔⁠וֹ

title: Numbers 27:8 (#2)
content:
אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי־יָמ֗וּת וּ⁠בֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔⁠וֹ

title: Numbers 27:8 (#3)
content:

title: Numbers 27:11 (#1)
content:
לִ⁠שְׁאֵר֞⁠וֹ

"to his flesh"

Here, his flesh represents the closest blood relative of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to his blood relative]

title: Numbers 27:11 (#2)
content:
וְֽ⁠הָ֨יְתָ֜ה לִ⁠בְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְ⁠חֻקַּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֔ט

content:

"just as Yahweh has commanded Moses"

title: Numbers 27:13 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נֶאֱסַפְתָּ֥ אֶל־עַמֶּ֖י⁠ךָ

The expression be gathered is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and go to be with your peoples]

title: Numbers 27:13 (#2)

Yahweh is referring to the death of Moses in a polite way by using the phrase be gathered to your peoples. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [and then die]

title: Numbers 27:13 (#3)

This suggests that he is using the plural form to refer to all of the relatives and ancestors of Moses who had already died. content:

title: Numbers 27:16 (#1)
content:
יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָ⁠רוּחֹ֖ת לְ⁠כָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר אִ֖ישׁ עַל־הָ⁠עֵדָֽה

title: Numbers 27:17 (#1)
content:
אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵ֣א לִ⁠פְנֵי⁠הֶ֗ם וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָבֹא֙ לִ⁠פְנֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹצִיאֵ֖⁠ם וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְבִיאֵ֑⁠ם

title: Numbers 27:17 (#2)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵי⁠הֶ֗ם

title: Numbers 27:17 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠לֹ֤א תִהְיֶה֙ עֲדַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כַּ⁠צֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־לָ⁠הֶ֖ם רֹעֶֽה

"and the congregation of Yahweh will not be like sheep that there is not a shepherd for them"

The point of this comparison is that just as sheep without a shepherd have no one to lead and protect them, so the congregation of Yahweh would have no one to lead and protect them if Yahweh did not appoint a leader. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the congregation of Yahweh will not be left without anyone to lead and protect them]

title: Numbers 27:18 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠סָמַכְתָּ֥ אֶת־יָדְ⁠ךָ֖ עָלָֽי⁠ו

title: Numbers 27:18 (#2)
content:
אֲשֶׁר־ר֣וּחַ בּ֑⁠וֹ

This could mean: (1) that Joshua has a spirit that is wise and capable. The phrase means that he is a wise and capable man, a good leader. Alternate translation: [in whom is skill and wisdom]; or (2) that Joshua has the Holy Spirit, which empowers him. Alternate translation: [in whom is my Spirit]

title: Numbers 27:19 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֣ אֹת֗⁠וֹ לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֔ן

title: Numbers 27:19 (#2)
content:
לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֔ן וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵ֖י כָּל־הָ⁠עֵדָ֑ה

title: Numbers 27:19 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠עֵינֵי⁠הֶֽם

"to their eyes"

title: Numbers 27:20 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נָתַתָּ֥ה מֵ⁠הֽוֹדְ⁠ךָ֖ עָלָ֑י⁠ו לְמַ֣עַן יִשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּל־עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

content:
וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵ֨י אֶלְעָזָ֤ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵן֙

עַל־פִּ֨י⁠ו יֵצְא֜וּ וְ⁠עַל־פִּ֣י⁠ו יָבֹ֗אוּ

Here, his mouth represents what Eleazar would say after he learned the decision of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. יֵצְא֜וּ וְ⁠עַל־פִּ֣י⁠ו יָבֹ֗אוּ

"they shall go out and upon his mouth they shall come in"

Yahweh is referring to all of the activities of the people by naming two major components, go out and come in. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [they shall conduct all of their affairs]

בְּ⁠יַד־מֹשֶֽׁה
