title: Numbers - Chapter 28 Introduction
content:
Numbers 28 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

In this chapter, Yahweh gives instructions concerning the animals, grain, and wine that the Israelites needed to offer to him on certain days. That includes offerings for every day, for Sabbath days, for the first days of months, for the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and for the day of firstfruits during the Festival of Weeks.

  1. Yahweh gives instructions for daily offerings (1–8)
  2. Yahweh gives instructions for Sabbath offerings (9–10)
  3. Yahweh gives instructions for monthly offerings (11–15)
  4. Yahweh gives instructions for Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread (16–25)
  5. Yahweh gives instructions for the Festival of Weeks (26–31)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Grain and drink offerings

This chapter includes instructions for what the Israelites were supposed to offer along with animal sacrifices. For each male lamb, ram, and bull that they offered, they needed to offer also a specific portion of grain and wine. The portion size was different for each animal. When the Israelites included the grain and drink offerings with each animal, Yahweh was pleased.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

Quotes in quotes

Most of this chapter is part of a long quote within another quote. The ULT represents the quote within a quote. The UST models how to express the idea with only one level of quotation. Consider how your language indicates that a quote contains a quote.

“a scent of pleasing”

Multiple times in this chapter, Yahweh describes a sacrifice as “a scent of pleasing” to or for him. This phrase refers to burning the sacrifice in a way that causes smoke to go up, picturing the sacrifice as being converted to pleasant-smelling smoke by the fire and arising to Yahweh in heaven, where he would smell the smoke and be pleased. That the sacrifice was accompanied by the gift of the pleasant-smelling smoke of the sacrifice was apparently crucial to the acceptance of the offering as an appropriate sacrifice on a person’s behalf.

Second person singular and plural

Throughout this chapter, most occurrences of “you” are plural. There are a few exceptions. In 28:2–3, when Yahweh is commanding Moses what to say, “you” is singular. Further, in 28:4, 8, and 21, “you” is singular. It is possible that “you” in these verses refers to the individual person who was offering the animals.

Omitted words in the lists of offerings

Throughout this chapter, the instructions for grain offerings are given in abbreviated form. Two kinds of words are left out.

First, the verb is often omitted. Where the ULT reads simply “and two tenths of fine flour,” the reader is expected to supply “you shall offer” from the earlier instructions. If your language requires a verb in such statements, you may need to include one. Second, the unit of measure is omitted. “A tenth” and “two tenths” mean a tenth part and two tenth parts of an ephah, a standard dry measure. If your readers would be confused by a fraction with nothing to divide, you could supply the unit and translate this as “a tenth of an ephah.”

title: Numbers 28:1 (#1)
content:
לֵּ⁠אמֹֽר

"saying"

The term saying introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated saying in 1:1.

See: Quotations and Quote Margins

title: Numbers 28:2 (#1)
content:
צַ֚ו אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם

"Command the sons of Israel and say to them"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Command the sons of Israel to keep presenting to me at its appointed time my offering, my bread for my gifts, a scent of my pleasing]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 28:2 (#2)
content:
לַחְמִ֜⁠י

"my bread"

Yahweh is using one kind of food, my bread, to mean food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my food]

See: Synecdoche

title: Numbers 28:2 (#3)
content:
לְ⁠אִשַּׁ֗⁠י

"for my gifts"

Here, a gift is a kind of offering presented to Yahweh by burning it on the altar. If your readers would not be familiar with what a gift is in this sense, you could use the name of a similar practice that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [for my offerings made by fire]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 28:2 (#4)
content:
תִּשְׁמְר֕וּ לְ⁠הַקְרִ֥יב לִ֖⁠י

"you shall keep to present to me"

Yahweh is using you shall keep to present to me as a common expression of the culture to mean “you shall be careful to present to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you must be sure to present to me]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:3 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ לָ⁠הֶ֔ם

"And you shall say to them"

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell them that this is the gift that they shall present to Yahweh: perfect male lambs, sons of a year, two for the day, a continual burnt offering]

See: Quotes within Quotes

title: Numbers 28:3 (#2)
content:
כְּבָשִׂ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֧ה תְמִימִ֛ם

"perfect male lambs, sons of a year"

Offering animals that were perfect, that is, animals that had no defect, was a symbolic action by which the Israelites showed that they were giving Yahweh what was most valuable and complete. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [male lambs without any defect, showing that you give Yahweh the best]

See: Symbolic Action

title: Numbers 28:3 (#3)
content:
בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֧ה

"sons of a year"

Yahweh is using sons of a year as a common expression of the culture to mean “one year old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that are a year old]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:4 (#1)
content:
אֶת־הַ⁠כֶּ֥בֶשׂ אֶחָ֖ד תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה בַ⁠בֹּ֑קֶר

"The one male lamb you shall do in the morning"

Yahweh is using you shall do as a common expression of the culture to mean “you shall offer as a sacrifice.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The one male lamb you shall offer as a sacrifice in the morning]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:4 (#2)
content:
תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה & תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה

"you shall do & you shall do"

The word you is singular here. It may refer to the individual person who offered the lamb. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 28:4 (#3)
content:
בֵּ֥ין הָֽ⁠עַרְבָּֽיִם

"between the evenings"

Yahweh is using between the evenings as a common expression of the culture to mean “at twilight.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at twilight]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:5 (#1)
content:
וַ⁠עֲשִׂירִ֧ית הָ⁠אֵיפָ֛ה

"and the tenth of the ephah of"

A tenth means one part out of ten equal parts.

See: Fractions

title: Numbers 28:5 (#2)
content:
וַ⁠עֲשִׂירִ֧ית הָ⁠אֵיפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת

"and the tenth of the ephah of flour"

This ephah was equivalent to 22 liters or nearly two thirds of a bushel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

See: Biblical Volume

title: Numbers 28:5 (#3)
content:
בְּלוּלָ֛ה בְּ⁠שֶׁ֥מֶן כָּתִ֖ית

"mixed with beaten oil"

The expression mixed is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which you have mixed with beaten oil]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 28:5 (#4)
content:
בְּ⁠שֶׁ֥מֶן כָּתִ֖ית

"with beaten oil"

Here, beaten oil is a kind of olive oil that people made by pounding olives rather than by pressing them. If your readers would not be familiar with what beaten oil is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with high-quality olive oil]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 28:5 (#5)
content:
רְבִיעִ֥ת

"the fourth of"

A fourth means one part out of four equal parts.

See: Fractions

title: Numbers 28:5 (#6)
content:
רְבִיעִ֥ת הַ⁠הִֽין

"the fourth of the hin"

This hin was equivalent to about 3.7 liters or about one gallon. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

See: Biblical Volume

title: Numbers 28:6 (#1)
content:
עֹלַ֖ת תָּמִ֑יד

"a burnt offering of continuity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of continuity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a continual burnt offering]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 28:6 (#2)
content:
הָ⁠עֲשֻׂיָה֙ בְּ⁠הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י

"the one done at Mount Sinai"

This could mean: (1) that the Israelites had already offered this kind of sacrifice at Mount Sinai. Alternate translation: [the one you already performed at Mount Sinai]; or (2) that God had already instituted this kind of sacrifice at Mount Sinai. Alternate translation: [the one I instituted at Mount Sinai]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:6 (#3)
content:
הָ⁠עֲשֻׂיָה֙ בְּ⁠הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י

"the one done at Mount Sinai"

The expression done is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one that your ancestors offered at Mount Sinai]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 28:7 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְכּ⁠וֹ֙

"And its drink offering"

The pronoun its refers to the continual burnt offering that Yahweh has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the drink offering for that burnt offering]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 28:7 (#2)
content:
בַּ⁠קֹּ֗דֶשׁ

"In the holy place"

This could mean: (1) the outer room of the tabernacle, the Holy Place. Alternate translation: [In the outer room of the tabernacle]; or (2) any holy place, including courtyard around the tabernacle. Alternate translation: [In a holy area]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:7 (#3)
content:
בַּ⁠קֹּ֗דֶשׁ הַסֵּ֛ךְ

"In the holy place pour out"

The implication is that the priest is the one who pours out this drink offering. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [In the holy place the priest shall pour out]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:8 (#1)
content:
תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה & תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה

"you shall do & you shall do"

The word you is singular here. It may refer to the individual person who offered the lamb. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 28:8 (#2)
content:
בֵּ֣ין הָֽ⁠עַרְבָּ֑יִם

"between the evenings"

See how you translated these same phrases in Numbers 28:4. Alternate translation: [at twilight]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:8 (#3)
content:
כְּ⁠מִנְחַ֨ת הַ⁠בֹּ֤קֶר וּ⁠כְ⁠נִסְכּ⁠וֹ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה

"Like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you shall do"

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering, so you shall offer a grain offering and a drink offering with this male lamb]

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 28:9 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בְ⁠יוֹם֙ הַ⁠שַּׁבָּ֔ת שְׁנֵֽי־כְבָשִׂ֥ים

"And on the day of the Sabbath: two male lambs"

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And on the day of the Sabbath you shall offer two male lambs]

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 28:10 (#1)
content:
עֹלַ֥ת שַׁבַּ֖ת בְּ⁠שַׁבַּתּ֑⁠וֹ

"a burnt offering of a Sabbath on its Sabbath"

Yahweh is using a burnt offering of a Sabbath on its Sabbath as a common expression of the culture to mean “a burnt offering for every Sabbath.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [A burnt offering to be presented on every Sabbath]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:10 (#2)
content:
עַל־עֹלַ֥ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֖יד

"upon the burnt offering of the continuity"

The implication is that the Israelites are to present this offering in addition to the continual burnt offering, not in place of it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in addition to the regular burnt offering]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:11 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בְ⁠רָאשֵׁי֙ חָדְשֵׁי⁠כֶ֔ם

"And at the heads of your months"

Yahweh is using at the heads of your months as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the first day of each month.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And on the first day of every month]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:11 (#2)
content:
תְּמִימִֽם

"perfect"

This could mean: (1) that all the animals were perfect. Alternate translation: [and all the animals must be perfect]; or (2) that the lambs were perfect. Alternate translation: [each lamb perfect]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:11 (#3)
content:
בְּנֵֽי־בָקָ֤ר

"sons of cattle"

Yahweh is using sons of cattle as a common expression of the culture to mean “young bulls.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [which are young]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:13 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠עִשָּׂרֹ֣ן עִשָּׂר֗וֹן

"and a tenth, a tenth of"

Yahweh is repeating the phrase a tenth in order to express the idea that this amount applies to each male lamb individually. If your language can repeat words in this way, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing this idea. Alternate translation: [and one tenth of an ephah each of]

See: Reduplication

title: Numbers 28:14 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶ֗ם חֲצִ֣י הַ⁠הִין֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לַ⁠פָּ֜ר וּ⁠שְׁלִישִׁ֧ת הַ⁠הִ֣ין לָ⁠אַ֗יִל וּ⁠רְבִיעִ֥ת הַ⁠הִ֛ין לַ⁠כֶּ֖בֶשׂ יָ֑יִן

"And their drink offerings shall be the half of the hin for the bull, and the third of the hin for the ram, and the fourth of the hin for the male lamb, wine"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about wine with the information about how much is to be presented for each animal. Alternate translation: [And their drink offerings of wine shall be the half of the hin for the bull, and the third of the hin for the ram, and the fourth of the hin for the male lamb]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 28:14 (#2)
content:
חֲצִ֣י הַ⁠הִין֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לַ⁠פָּ֜ר וּ⁠שְׁלִישִׁ֧ת הַ⁠הִ֣ין לָ⁠אַ֗יִל

"shall be the half of the hin for the bull, and the third of the hin for the ram"

A half means one part out of two equal parts. A third means one part out of three equal parts.

See: Fractions

title: Numbers 28:15 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠שְׂעִ֨יר עִזִּ֥ים אֶחָ֛ד

"and one buck of goats"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a buck that is characterized by being one of the animals called goats. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and one male goat]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 28:15 (#2)
content:
עַל־עֹלַ֧ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֛יד יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה

"upon the burnt offering of the continuity it shall be done"

The expression it shall be done is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the priests shall offer it in addition to the burnt offering of the continuity]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 28:16 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בַ⁠חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָ⁠רִאשׁ֗וֹן

"And on the first month"

The first month of the Hebrew calendar includes the last part of March and the first part of April on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

See: Hebrew Months

title: Numbers 28:16 (#2)
content:
בְּ⁠אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַ⁠חֹ֑דֶשׁ

"on day 14 of the month"

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as day 14, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use, such as “the fourteenth day.” Alternate translation: [on the fourteenth day of the month]

See: Ordinal Numbers

title: Numbers 28:16 (#3)
content:
פֶּ֖סַח לַ⁠יהוָֽה

"is} the Passover of Yahweh"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a Passover that is characterized by being celebrated in honor of Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the Passover celebrated in honor of Yahweh]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 28:17 (#1)
content:
חָ֑ג שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים מַצּ֖וֹת

"is} a festival. Seven days unleavened bread"

This could mean: (1) that the festival itself lasted for seven days. Alternate translation: [is a festival for seven days, during which unleavened bread]; or (2) that the festival lasted one day, but for that day and the following six days the Israelites had to eat unleavened bread. Alternate translation: [is a one day festival. For seven days, starting with that day, unleavened bread]

title: Numbers 28:17 (#2)
content:
שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים מַצּ֖וֹת יֵאָכֵֽל

"Seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten"

The expression shall be eaten is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 28:17 (#3)
content:
שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים

"Seven days"

Yahweh is using seven days as a common expression of the culture to mean “during each of the seven days.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Throughout the seven days]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 28:18 (#1)
content:
מִקְרָא־קֹ֑דֶשׁ

"is} an assembly of holiness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of holiness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a holy assembly]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 28:18 (#2)
content:
כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"any work of service"

The phrase work of service expresses a single idea. The word service tells more about work. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [any ordinary labor]

See: Hendiadys

title: Numbers 28:19 (#1)
content:
תְּמִימִ֖ם יִהְי֥וּ לָ⁠כֶֽם

"They shall be perfect for you"

The implication is that the Israelites must choose animals that have no defects, since Yahweh accepts only animals of that kind. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They shall be without any defect, as Yahweh requires]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:20 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠מִ֨נְחָתָ֔⁠ם סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֜ים לַ⁠פָּ֗ר וּ⁠שְׁנֵ֧י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֛ים לָ⁠אַ֖יִל תַּעֲשֽׂוּ

"And their grain offering: flour mixed with the oil, three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram, you shall do"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what the Israelites are to do with the information about their grain offering. Alternate translation: [And you shall offer as their grain offering flour mixed with the oil, three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 28:21 (#1)
content:
תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה

"you shall do"

The word you is singular here. It may refer to the individual person who offered the lamb. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 28:21 (#2)
content:
לַ⁠כֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָ⁠אֶחָ֑ד לְ⁠שִׁבְעַ֖ת הַ⁠כְּבָשִֽׂים

"for the one male lamb, for the seven male lambs"

The implication is that the Israelites are to present this amount of flour for each one of the seven male lambs. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for each one of the seven male lambs]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:22 (#1)
content:
לְ⁠כַפֵּ֖ר עֲלֵי⁠כֶֽם

"to make atonement for you"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of atonement, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to take away your sin]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 28:23 (#1)
content:
מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַד֙ עֹלַ֣ת הַ⁠בֹּ֔קֶר

"Besides the burnt offering of the morning"

The word Besides introduces something additional. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [In addition to the burnt offering of the morning]

See: Connecting Words and Phrases

title: Numbers 28:23 (#2)
content:
תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת־אֵֽלֶּה

"you shall do these"

The pronoun these refers to the offerings that Yahweh has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you shall offer these sacrifices]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 28:24 (#1)
content:
לֶ֛חֶם אִשֵּׁ֥ה

"bread of gift"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe bread that is characterized by being a gift that the Israelites present to him. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [bread that is a gift]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 28:25 (#1)
content:
מִקְרָא־קֹ֖דֶשׁ

"an assembly of holiness"

See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:18. Alternate translation: [a holy assembly]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 28:25 (#2)
content:
כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"any work of service"

See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:18. Alternate translation: [any ordinary work]

See: Hendiadys

title: Numbers 28:26 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בְ⁠י֣וֹם הַ⁠בִּכּוּרִ֗ים

"And on the day of the firstfruits"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a day that is characterized by the presenting of the firstfruits. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And on the day set apart for the firstfruits]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 28:26 (#2)
content:
בְּ⁠הַקְרִ֨יבְ⁠כֶ֜ם מִנְחָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ לַֽ⁠יהוָ֔ה בְּ⁠שָׁבֻעֹ֖תֵי⁠כֶ֑ם

"when you present a new grain offering to Yahweh in your weeks"

The word that the ULT translates as when indicates that the Israelites are to hold an assembly of holiness at the same time as when they present a new grain offering to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [at the same time that you present a new grain offering to Yahweh in your weeks]

See: Connect — Simultaneous Time Relationship

title: Numbers 28:26 (#3)
content:
בְּ⁠שָׁבֻעֹ֖תֵי⁠כֶ֑ם

"in your weeks"

The implication is that the phrase in your weeks refers to the Festival of Weeks, which the Israelites celebrated seven weeks after they began to harvest their grain. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [during your Festival of Weeks]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 28:26 (#4)
content:
מִֽקְרָא־קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙

"an assembly of holiness"

See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:25. Alternate translation: [a holy assembly]

See: Hendiadys

title: Numbers 28:26 (#5)
content:
כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"any work of service"

See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:25. Alternate translation: [any ordinary work]

See: Hendiadys

title: Numbers 28:30 (#1)
content:
לְ⁠כַפֵּ֖ר עֲלֵי⁠כֶֽם

"to make atonement for you"

See how you translated these same phrases in Numbers 28:22. Alternate translation: [to take away your sin]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 28:31 (#1)
content:
מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַ֞ד עֹלַ֧ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֛יד וּ⁠מִנְחָת֖⁠וֹ תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ תְּמִימִ֥ם יִהְיוּ־לָ⁠כֶ֖ם וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶֽם

"Besides the burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering you shall do; they shall be perfect for you, and their drink offerings"

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about their drink offerings with the information about what the Israelites are to do. Alternate translation: [Besides the burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering you shall do, and their drink offerings; they shall be perfect for you]

See: Information Structure

title: Numbers 28:31 (#2)
content:
מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַ֞ד עֹלַ֧ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֛יד וּ⁠מִנְחָת֖⁠וֹ

"Besides the burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering"

The word Besides introduces something additional. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [In addition to the burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering]

See: Connecting Words and Phrases

title: Numbers 28:31 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶֽם

"and their drink offerings"

Here, the pronoun their could refer to: (1) the burnt offerings for the day of firstfruits and the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for all the offerings]; or (2) just the burnt offerings for the day of firstfruits. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings of the day of firstfruits]; or (3) just the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offering for the burnt offering of the continuity]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers - Chapter 29 Introduction
content:
Numbers 29 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

In this chapter, Yahweh continues to give instructions concerning the animals, grain, and wine that the Israelites needed to offer to him on certain days. That includes the first day of the seventh month (sometimes called the Festival of Trumpets), the tenth day of the seventh month (the Day of Atonement), the seven-day festival that began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (the Festival of Huts), and the day immediately after the Festival of Huts.

  1. Yahweh gives instructions for the Festival of Trumpets (1–6)
  2. Yahweh gives instructions for the Day of Atonement (7–11)
  3. Yahweh gives instructions for the Festival of Huts and the final assembly (12–38)
  4. Moses passes Yahweh’s instructions on to Israel (39–40)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Grain and drink offerings

This chapter includes instructions for what the Israelites were supposed to offer along with animal sacrifices. For each male lamb, ram, and bull that they offered, they needed to offer also a specific portion of grain and wine. The portion size was different for each animal. When the Israelites included the grain and drink offerings with each animal, Yahweh was pleased.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

Quotes in quotes

Most of this chapter is part of a long quote within another quote. The ULT represents the quote within a quote. The UST models how to express the idea with only one level of quotation. Consider how your language indicates that a quote contains a quote.

“a scent of pleasing”

Multiple times in this chapter, Yahweh describes a sacrifice as “a scent of pleasing” to or for him. This phrase refers to burning the sacrifice in a way that causes smoke to go up, picturing the sacrifice as being converted to pleasant-smelling smoke by the fire and arising to Yahweh in heaven, where he would smell the smoke and be pleased. That the sacrifice was accompanied by the gift of the pleasant-smelling smoke of the sacrifice was apparently crucial to the acceptance of the offering as an appropriate sacrifice on a person’s behalf.

Repetition

The list of offerings for each day of the Festival of Huts is very repetitive. There are some minor differences in wording (represented in the ULT), and the number of bulls goes down by one each day. Beyond that, the instructions for each day are identical. Most likely, this kind of repetition represents a list or table in sentence form. The author thought that listing each item for each day was important. Because of this, it is recommended that you do not shorten the repetition. Instead, be sure that the repeated verses are translated in the same way. You could also use formatting to make these verses look more like a list and enable readers to follow the repetition better. See how you handled the repetition in Numbers 7.

title: Numbers 29:1 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בַ⁠חֹ֨דֶשׁ הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֜י

"And in the seventh month"

The seventh month of the Hebrew calendar includes the last part of September and the first part of October on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

See: Hebrew Months

title: Numbers 29:1 (#2)
content:
בְּ⁠אֶחָ֣ד לַ⁠חֹ֗דֶשׁ

"on one of the month"

The text uses a cardinal number, one, to refer to the first day of the month. If your language would not represent a number in a form such as one, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [on the first of the month]

See: Ordinal Numbers

title: Numbers 29:1 (#3)
content:
מִֽקְרָא־קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙

"an assembly of holiness"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of holiness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an assembly dedicated to Yahweh]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 29:1 (#4)
content:
לָ⁠כֶ֔ם & לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֑וּ & לָ⁠כֶֽם

"for you. You shall not do & for you"

Here and throughout the chapter, the word you is plural because Yahweh is telling Moses what to the say to all the Israelites. So, use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

See: Forms of ‘You’ — Singular

title: Numbers 29:1 (#5)
content:
כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה

"any work of service"

The phrase work of service expresses a single idea. The word service tells more about work. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [any ordinary work]

See: Hendiadys

title: Numbers 29:1 (#6)
content:
י֥וֹם תְּרוּעָ֖ה

"a day of a loud blast"

The implication is that the people would blow trumpets on this day. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a day when you sound the trumpets]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:2 (#1)
content:
לְ⁠רֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֨חַ֙

"for a scent of pleasing"

Yahweh is using a scent of pleasing as a common expression of the culture to mean “an offering that he accepts.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as a sacrifice that is acceptable]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 29:2 (#2)
content:
לַֽ⁠יהוָ֔ה

"to Yahweh"

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [to me]

See: First, Second or Third Person

title: Numbers 29:2 (#3)
content:
פַּ֧ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֛ר אֶחָ֖ד

"one bull, a son of cattle"

It might seem that the expression one bull, a son of cattle contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [one young bull]

See: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

resource.label: Making Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information Explicit

title: Numbers 29:2 (#4)
content:
בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֛ה

"sons of a year"

Yahweh is using sons of a year as a common expression of the culture to mean “one year old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that are a year old]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 29:2 (#5)
content:
תְּמִימִֽם

"perfect"

This could mean: (1) that all the animals were perfect. Alternate translation: [and all the animals must be perfect]; or (2) that the lambs were perfect. Alternate translation: [each lamb perfect]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:3 (#1)
content:
סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶן

"flour mixed with the oil"

The expression mixed is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [flour that you have mixed with the oil]

See: Active or Passive

title: Numbers 29:3 (#2)
content:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶשְׂרֹנִים֙

"three tenths"

The fraction three tenths means three parts out of ten equal parts.

See: Fractions

title: Numbers 29:3 (#3)
content:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶשְׂרֹנִים֙

"three tenths"

The term tenths here refers to tenths of an ephah. An ephah was equivalent to 22 liters or nearly two thirds of a bushel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

See: Biblical Volume

title: Numbers 29:4 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠עִשָּׂר֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד לַ⁠כֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָ⁠אֶחָ֑ד לְ⁠שִׁבְעַ֖ת הַ⁠כְּבָשִֽׂים

"and one tenth for the one male lamb, for the seven male lambs"

The implication is that one tenth of an ephah of flour is required for each one of the seven lambs. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and one tenth of an ephah of flour for each one of the seven male lambs]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:5 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠שְׂעִיר־עִזִּ֥ים אֶחָ֖ד

"and one buck of goats"

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a buck that is characterized by being one of the goats. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and one male goat]

See: Possession

title: Numbers 29:5 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠כַפֵּ֖ר עֲלֵי⁠כֶֽם

"to make atonement for you"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of atonement, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to take away your sin]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 29:6 (#1)
content:
עֹלַ֨ת הַ⁠חֹ֜דֶשׁ

"the burnt offering of the month"

The implication is that the burnt offering of the month is the offering that Yahweh required at the beginning of every month, as described in 28:11–15. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the burnt offering required at the beginning of each month]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:6 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠עֹלַ֤ת הַ⁠תָּמִיד֙

"and the burnt offering of the continuity"

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of continuity, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the burnt offering that is offered continually]

See: Abstract Nouns

title: Numbers 29:6 (#3)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶ֖ם

"and their drink offerings"

Here, the pronoun their could refer to: (1) the burnt offerings for the first day of the seventh month, the regular offering for the first day of any month, and the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for all the offerings]; or (2) just the regular offering for the first day of any month and the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the first day of the month and the burnt offering of the continuity]; or (3) just the burnt offerings for the first day of the seventh month. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings of the first day of the seventh month]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 29:7 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠עִנִּיתֶ֖ם אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵי⁠כֶ֑ם

"and you shall humble your souls"

Yahweh is using you shall humble your souls as a common expression of the culture to mean “you shall deny yourselves food and comfort.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you shall deny yourselves food and comfort]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 29:11 (#1)
content:
חַטַּ֤את הַ⁠כִּפֻּרִים֙

"the sin offering of the atonement"

The implication is that the sin offering of the atonement is the offering that Yahweh required on this one day of the year, the Day of Atonement. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the sin offering presented on this annual Day of Atonement]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:11 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶֽם

"and their drink offerings"

Here, the pronoun their could refer to: (1) the burnt offerings for the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement offering, and the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for all the offerings]; or (2) just the offering for the Day of Atonement and the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the Day of Atonement and the burnt offering of the continuity]; or (3) just the burnt offerings for the tenth day of the seventh month. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings of the tenth day of the seventh month]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 29:17 (#1)
content:
וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠שֵּׁנִ֗י פָּרִ֧ים בְּנֵי־בָקָ֛ר שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר

"And on the second day: 12 bulls, sons of cattle"

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And on the second day you shall present 12 bulls, sons of cattle]

See: Ellipsis

title: Numbers 29:18 (#1)
content:
בְּ⁠מִסְפָּרָ֖⁠ם כַּ⁠מִּשְׁפָּֽט

"by their number according to the ordinance"

The implication is that the amounts of grain and drink offerings for each animal are the amounts that Yahweh prescribed earlier, in 29:14–15. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by their number according to the amounts prescribed earlier]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:19 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶֽם

"and their drink offerings"

Here, the pronoun their could refer to: (1) the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and its drink offering]; or (2) the special offerings for the second day of the festival as well as the burnt offering of the continuity. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings for the second day of the festival and for the burnt offering of the continuity]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 29:35 (#1)
content:
עֲצֶ֖רֶת

"a holiday"

A holiday is a kind of solemn gathering that closes a festival, on which people assemble to worship and do no work. If your readers would not be familiar with what a holiday is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a solemn closing assembly]

See: Translate Unknowns

title: Numbers 29:39 (#1)
content:
אֵ֛לֶּה תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ

"These you shall do"

The pronoun These refers to all of the offerings that Yahweh has described in this chapter and the previous one. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [These offerings that I have described you shall do]

See: Pronouns — When to Use Them

title: Numbers 29:39 (#2)
content:
לְ⁠עֹלֹֽתֵי⁠כֶם֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠מִנְחֹ֣תֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וּ⁠לְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠כֶ֖ם וּ⁠לְ⁠שַׁלְמֵי⁠כֶֽם

"for your burnt offerings, and for your grain offerings, and for your drink offerings, and for your peace offerings"

This could mean: (1) that the offerings outlined in Numbers 28–29 are in addition to all these offerings. Alternate translation: [besides your burnt offerings, and besides your grain offerings, and besides your drink offerings, and besides your peace offerings]; or (2) that the offerings in Numbers 28–29 are these kinds of offerings. Alternate translation: [as your burnt offerings, and as your grain offerings, and as your drinking offerings, and as your peace offerings]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 29:39 (#3)
content:
וּ⁠לְ⁠שַׁלְמֵי⁠כֶֽם

"and for your peace offerings"

This is the end of the second-level quotation that began in 28:3, and it is also the end of the first-level quotation that began in 28:2. You may wish to mark the ends of these speeches with closing second-level and first-level quotation marks or with some other punctuation or convention that your language uses to indicate the end of a quotation within a quotation.

See: Quote Markings

title: Numbers - Chapter 30 Introduction
content:
Numbers 30 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

In this chapter, Moses recounts instructions concerning vows and agreements made by women. The instructions deal with four situations: an unmarried woman living with her parents, a woman who has recently gotten married, a divorced woman or widow, and a woman who is married. In each case, if the woman is part of a man’s household, the man is responsible for confirming or nullifying the woman’s vow or agreement.

  1. Moses explains that vows made to Yahweh must be kept (1–2)
  2. A father may confirm or cancel the vow of a young woman living in his house (3–5)
  3. A husband may confirm or cancel a vow his wife made before their marriage (6–8)
  4. Widows and divorced women must keep their vows (9)
  5. Moses explains the rules for vows made by married women (10–16)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Household structure and authority

In this culture, the person who had authority over the whole household was the oldest male. So, a daughter living at home with her parents or a married woman living with her husband was under the authority of the man, whether her father or her husband. However, for a widow or divorced woman, there was no man with authority over her. Given this way of structuring households, this chapter indicates that the person in charge of the household (usually the husband or father) was responsible for confirming or nullifying any promises or agreements made by the women in the household.

Vows

Vows were promises that a person made to God. Often, the person would ask God to do something and then promise to do something or give something to God if God did what the person asked. Consider how you might refer to this kind of solemn promise made to God.

Oaths

Oaths were statements that confirmed promises and commitments. Oaths could call God as witness, or they could specify the consequences if the promise or commitment was broken. Consider how you might refer to this kind of solemn confirming statement.

Bonds

The word translated as “bond” in this chapter occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. Scholars debate exactly what it means. It could refer to a promise not to do something, while “vow” refers to a promise to do something. More likely, it refers to a binding agreement, sometimes written, with a person or people. The UST follows that interpretation. Consider how you might refer to a binding agreement between people.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

What is the class of the woman in 30:10–15?

Some scholars argue that 30:10–15 or 30:10–12 continues to speak about the same woman as 30:9 does: a divorced or widowed woman. In this case, 30:10–15 or 30:10–12 refer to the time before the woman was widowed or divorced. Other scholars argue that 3:10–15 deal with a new situation: a woman who is married when she makes vows or agreements. This seems to make more sense of the present tense verbs in 30:12. The UST follows this interpretation.

title: Numbers 30:1 (#1)
content:
רָאשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠מַּטּ֔וֹת

"the heads of the tribes"

The author is speaking as if the leaders of the tribes of Israel were the heads of those tribes. If this meaning would not be clear in your language, you could use a comparable expression or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the leaders of the tribes]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 30:2 (#1)
content:
אִישׁ֩ כִּֽי־יִדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לַֽ⁠יהוָ֗ה אֽוֹ־הִשָּׁ֤בַע שְׁבֻעָה֙ לֶ⁠אְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל־נַפְשׁ֔⁠וֹ לֹ֥א יַחֵ֖ל דְּבָר֑⁠וֹ

"A man, when he vows a vow to Yahweh or swears an oath to bind a bond on his life, he shall not profane his word"

Moses is presenting a possible condition, that a man might make a vow or swear an oath to Yahweh. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may also be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement comes first. Alternate translation: [If a man vows a vow to Yahweh or swears an oath to bind a bond on his life, he shall not profane his word]

See: Connect — Hypothetical Conditions

title: Numbers 30:2 (#2)
content:
לֶ⁠אְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל־נַפְשׁ֔⁠וֹ

"to bind a bond on his life"

Here and throughout the chapter, the word bond could mean: (1) that the person has formally committed to an agreement with someone. Alternate translation: [to commit to a binding contract]; or (2) that the person has made a promise to abstain from something. Alternate translation: [to refrain from doing something]

See: Metaphor

title: Numbers 30:2 (#3)
content:
אִישׁ֩

"A man"

Moses is not referring to a specific man. He means men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Any man]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 30:2 (#4)
content:
יִדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לַֽ⁠יהוָ֗ה אֽוֹ־הִשָּׁ֤בַע שְׁבֻעָה֙ לֶ⁠אְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל־נַפְשׁ֔⁠וֹ

"he vows a vow to Yahweh or swears an oath to bind a bond on his life"

Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

See: Poetry

title: Numbers 30:2 (#5)
content:
לֶ⁠אְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל־נַפְשׁ֔⁠וֹ

"to bind a bond on his life"

Moses is using to bind a bond on his life as a common expression of the culture to mean “to place himself under a binding obligation.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to place himself under a binding obligation]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 30:2 (#6)
content:
לֹ֥א יַחֵ֖ל דְּבָר֑⁠וֹ

"he shall not profane his word"

Moses is using he shall not profane his word as a common expression of the culture to mean “he must not break his promise.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he must not break his promise]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 30:2 (#7)
content:
כְּ⁠כָל־הַ⁠יֹּצֵ֥א מִ⁠פִּ֖י⁠ו

"According to everything going out from his mouth"

Here, going out from his mouth represents what the man has said. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [According to everything that he has spoken]

See: Metonymy

title: Numbers 30:3 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אִשָּׁ֕ה

"And a woman"

Moses is not referring to a specific woman. He means women in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And any woman]

See: Generic Noun Phrases

title: Numbers 30:3 (#2)
content:
בְּ⁠בֵ֥ית אָבִ֖י⁠הָ בִּ⁠נְעֻרֶֽי⁠הָ

"in the house of her father in her youth"

The implication is that this woman is young and unmarried and so is still living under the authority of her father. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in the house of her father while she is still young and unmarried]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 30:4 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠הֶחֱרִ֥ישׁ לָ֖⁠הּ אָבִ֑י⁠הָ

"and her father keeps silent to her"

Moses is using keeps silent to her as a common expression of the culture to mean “says nothing to oppose what she has done.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and her father says nothing to oppose what she has done]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 30:4 (#2)
content:
וְ⁠קָ֨מוּ֙ כָּל־נְדָרֶ֔י⁠הָ

"then all her vows shall stand"

Moses is using shall stand as a common expression of the culture to mean “will remain in force.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then all her vows shall remain in force]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 30:5 (#1)
content:
בְּ⁠י֣וֹם שָׁמְע⁠וֹ֒

"on the day of his hearing"

Moses is using on the day of his hearing as a common expression of the culture to mean “at the time when he learns about it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when he hears about it]

See: Idiom

title: Numbers 30:5 (#2)
content:
וַֽ⁠יהוָה֙ יִֽסְלַח־לָ֔⁠הּ

"and Yahweh will forgive her"

The implication is that Yahweh will forgive her for not doing what she vowed to do. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh will forgive her for not doing what she vowed to do]

See: Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information

title: Numbers 30:5 (#3)
content:
כִּי־הֵנִ֥יא אָבִ֖י⁠הָ אֹתָֽ⁠הּ

"for her father forbade her"

The word translated as for indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because her father forbade her]

See: Connect — Reason-and-Result Relationship

title: Numbers 30:6 (#1)
content:
וְ⁠אִם־הָי֤וֹ תִֽהְיֶה֙ לְ⁠אִ֔ישׁ

"And if being, she is for a man"

Moses is repeating forms of the verb being in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. Here, Moses could be speaking about: (1) a new situation, that of a woman who is married when she makes the vow or agreement. This situation is the topic of 30:10–15. Alternate translation: [And as for a married woman, if in the house of her husband she vowed]; or (2) the same situation, that of a widowed or divorced woman. In this case, Moses is explaining what the instructions are for vows and agreements she made before her husband died or divorced her. title: Numbers - Chapter 31 Introduction
content:
Numbers 31 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

This chapter describes Israel’s war against Midian. After the battle, Moses gives instructions about the captives and about cleansing the soldiers and captured goods. The goods are divided, and portions are given to Yahweh.

  1. Yahweh commands Israel to attack Midian, and Israel wins the battle (1–12)
  2. Moses gives instructions about the captives and purification after battle (13–24)
  3. The captives, animals, and goods are divided, with portions given to Yahweh (25–47)
  4. The army’s officers bring gold as an offering to Yahweh (48–54)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

War for Yahweh

When the Israelites fought wars that Yahweh commanded them to fight, they sometimes killed all the men of the people they were fighting. That is what they do when they defeat the Midianites in this chapter. While God does not give explicit instructions, Moses also requires the Israelites to kill the boys and the women who have had sex. These actions are very violent, and scholars interpret the meaning in different ways. It is recommended that translations simply represent the violence.

Purity and impurity

This chapter refers back to concepts that were important in Numbers 19. Those concepts include impurity because of dead bodies and the special water that the Israelites could use to cleanse this impurity. In this chapter, the soldiers, captives, and plunder are impure. The people must be cleansed by washing with the special water as they wait outside the camp for seven days. The plunder must be cleansed by the special water and, in some cases, by fire. Once everything is cleansed, the people and plunder may enter the Israelite camp.

The levy for Yahweh and the Levites

This chapter refers to a “levy” from the plunder that the Israelites needed to pay to Yahweh and to the Levites. Moses first divided the plunder in half. One half was for the soldiers who had fought in the battle. From this half, they had to give one out of every 500 people and animals to Yahweh as the “levy.” Yahweh then granted this levy to Eleazar and the rest of the priests. From the other half that belonged to the rest of the Israelites, they had to give one out of every 50 people and animals to the Levites. Some translations refer to this “levy” as a tax or a tribute. Consider how you might refer to the levy in your language.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

Balaam

This chapter refers to the same Balaam from Numbers 22–24. The Israelites killed him when they attacked the Midianites (see 31:8). Later in the chapter (31:16), Moses indicates that Balaam was the one who told the Midianites to convince the Israelites to worship Baal of Peor, which is narrated in Numbers 25. Consider how you can make it clear to your readers that this chapter refers to the same Balaam from Numbers 22–24 and the same event from Numbers 25.

Hyperbole

In this chapter, the narrator speaks as if the Israelites had completely destroyed all the Midianite men and cities and had taken every single thing that the Midianites owned. However, it is clear from later stories that many Midianites were not killed (for example, see the story in Judges 6). The narrator may be using hyperbole to indicate that the Israelites defeated and killed many Midianites. Or, the narrator may mean that the Israelites defeated and killed all the men in a specific group of Midianites. It is recommended that you preserve the strong language in your translation, but you could include a footnote explaining what the extreme language may mean.

Large numbers

There are many large numbers in this chapter, including many over 10,000. Consider how you would express large numbers in your language and use that form consistently in this chapter. See how you translated the large numbers in chapter 1.

title: Numbers 31:2 (#1)
content:
נְקֹ֗ם נִקְמַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל

"Avenge the vengeance of the sons of Israel"

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [Avenge the sons of Israel]

title: Numbers 31:2 (#2)
content:

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the vengeance that he will take on behalf of the sons of Israel, not vengeance that they take on their own. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [vengeance on behalf of the sons of Israel]

content:

title: Numbers 31:2 (#4)

תֵּאָסֵ֥ף אֶל־עַמֶּֽי⁠ךָ

title: Numbers 31:3 (#1)
content:
הֵחָלְצ֧וּ מֵ⁠אִתְּ⁠כֶ֛ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לַ⁠צָּבָ֑א וְ⁠יִהְיוּ֙ עַל־מִדְיָ֔ן לָ⁠תֵ֥ת נִקְמַת־יְהוָ֖ה בְּ⁠מִדְיָֽן

title: Numbers 31:4 (#1)

אֶ֚לֶף

"A thousand"

content:

content:
פְּקוּדֵ֣י הֶ⁠חָ֑יִל

content:

content:
לִ⁠מְסָר־מַ֥עַל

"to select unfaithfulness"

title: Numbers 31:17 (#1)
content:
יֹדַ֥עַת אִ֛ישׁ לְ⁠מִשְׁכַּ֥ב זָכָ֖ר

title: Numbers - Chapter 32 Introduction
content:
Numbers 32 Chapter Introduction

Structure and Formatting

In this chapter, Moses, Joshua, Eleazar, and the Israelite leaders make an agreement with the leaders of the tribes of Gad and Reuben. This agreement specifies that the soldiers from Gad and Reuben must help the rest of the Israelites conquer the land west of the Jordan River. However, once that is done, the people of Gad and Reuben receive land on the east side of the Jordan River. The chapter also briefly recounts some people from Manasseh who also conquered and received land on the east side of the Jordan River.

  1. Reuben and Gad ask to settle east of the Jordan (1–5)
  2. Moses warns them against discouraging the other Israelites from entering Canaan (6–15)
  3. Reuben and Gad promise to help the other tribes take the land (16–27)
  4. Moses confirms the agreement and gives land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh (28–42)

Religious and Cultural Concepts in This Chapter

Land on the east side and west side of the Jordan River

The land of Canaan itself was on the west side of the Jordan River. However, the Israelites conquered some land on the east side of the Jordan River. People from Gad, Reuben, and part of the tribe of Manasseh wanted to receive this land on the east side of the Jordan. Moses initially rejects their desire, but eventually he allows them to receive this land as long as they help the rest of the Israelites conquer the land of Canaan on the west side of the Jordan River.

Translation Issues in This Chapter

What did the Reubenites and Gadites request?

When the people from the tribes of Reuben and Gad request land on the east side of the Jordan River, they do not specify exactly what they mean. They may mean that they will settle in that land and refuse to help the rest of the Israelites conquer Canaan. This is what Moses thinks they mean. They may mean that they will settle in that land but will still help the rest of the Israelites conquer Canaan. This is what they offer in response to Moses’ rejection of their initial request. If possible, you should preserve this ambiguity in your translation of their initial request.

Quotes in quotes

In 32:11–12, there is a quote inside a quote. Consider how your language indicates that a quote contains a quote. The UST models how to express the idea with only one level of quotation.

Timing of events

The events that the author narrates in 32:39–42 almost certainly did not happen after the events narrated earlier in the chapter. They probably happened sometime around the events narrated in Numbers 21. Additionally, each specific battle that the author narrates may have happened at the same time or in a different sequence. Consider how you can introduce these events so that it is clear they do not follow the previous events in chronological sequence.

content:
